definition_en: relating to an organization as a body, to the way its parts are arranged and managed, to the work of arranging an activity, or to a person's ability to put work in order
core_image: 把散乱的人和事装进一张画好的架构图，每一格都标明谁向谁报告

sceneCN: 这里 organizational 是「组织结构的」（第 2 个义项：指机构内部层级与分工的排列方式）；句意：这张图显示每个部门的组织结构。

senses.title: Of the body as a body
senses.definition: relating to an organization as a whole, rather than to one member, one department, or one activity
senses.definitionCN: 指某个组织整体，而不是其中某个成员、某个部门或某项活动
senses.example: The merger changed the organizational name but left the staff in place.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并改掉了组织名称，却把人员原样留了下来。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun organization into a describing word. It points at the body as a body, the way a label on a pen points at the pen rather than at the animals inside it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词 organization 变成形容词。它指的是作为一个整体的机构，就像圈栏上的牌子指的是圈栏本身，而不是里面的牲畜。

senses.title: How the parts are arranged
senses.titleCN: 指内部层级与分工排列的
senses.definition: relating to the structure of an organization, especially the way roles, units, and levels are arranged under one another
senses.definitionCN: 指机构的内部结构，尤其是角色、单元与层级之间上下排列的方式
senses.example: A flat organizational structure puts few layers between the intern and the director.
senses.exampleCN: 扁平的组织结构让实习生和总监之间只隔很少的层级。
senses.why: The Greek source organon was a tool whose parts work together. Once the tool becomes a body of people, the adjective can describe the arrangement of those parts.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源 organon 是一件各部分协同工作的工具。当这件工具变成一个由人组成的机构后，这个形容词就可以描述各部分如何排列。

senses.title: Of management and administration
senses.definition: relating to management, decision-making, and the daily running of an organization rather than to its technical work
senses.definitionCN: 指管理、决策与机构日常运转，而不是指机构所做的技术性工作
senses.example: The audit blamed organizational failures rather than individual dishonesty.
senses.exampleCN: 审计把问题归因于管理层面的失误，而不是个人的不诚实。
senses.why: Management is the hand that holds the tool. This sense marks whatever belongs to that hand — budgets, chains of approval, reporting lines — as opposed to the work the tool is meant to do.
senses.whyCN: 管理是握着这件工具的手。这个义项标记的是属于这只手的东西——预算、审批链、汇报线——而不是工具本身要完成的工作。

senses.title: Of arranging an event or task
senses.definition: relating to the work of planning and arranging people or things so that an activity can take place
senses.definitionCN: 指为了让某项活动得以举行而规划、安排人与物的那部分工作
senses.example: The festival's organizational work began nine months before the first ticket was sold.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节的筹备工作在第一张票卖出前九个月就开始了。
senses.why: Here the adjective points back to the verb organize. It names the labour of drawing the chart, not the body that appears once the chart is drawn.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词回指的是动词 organize。它命名的是画这张架构图的劳作，而不是图画好之后出现的那个机构。

senses.title: Of organized labour
senses.definition: relating to a trade union, or to workers acting together as one body in negotiations
senses.definitionCN: 指工会，或指工人在谈判中以一个整体共同行动的
senses.example: Organizational membership in the union rose sharply after the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工之后，工会的组织成员人数大幅上升。
senses.why: A union is an organization in the plainest sense: workers gathered into one body. The adjective keeps that collective meaning and attaches it to labour rather than to management.
senses.whyCN: 工会是最字面意义上的组织：工人聚合成一个整体。这个形容词保留了这层集体含义，并把它挂到劳工一方，而不是管理层。

senses.title: Of organizational studies
senses.definition: relating to the academic study of how organizations behave, as in organizational psychology, organizational behaviour, and organizational theory
senses.definitionCN: 指对机构如何运作的学术研究，如组织心理学、组织行为学与组织理论
senses.example: She teaches organizational behaviour to first-year management students.
senses.exampleCN: 她给管理专业一年级学生讲授组织行为学。
senses.why: When a field takes the body itself as its object, the adjective enters the field's name. The subject is no longer how to run the tool but the regular patterns the tool shows.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学科把机构本身当作研究对象时，这个形容词就进入了学科名称。研究对象不再是怎样使用这件工具，而是这件工具呈现出的规律。

senses.title: Of levels of biological organization
senses.definition: relating to the nested levels at which living matter is arranged, from molecules and cells up to organs and ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 指生命物质由分子、细胞一直嵌套到器官与生态系统的各个层次
senses.example: Ecologists work at organizational levels above the single organism.
senses.exampleCN: 生态学家研究的是单个生物体以上的组织层次。
senses.why: Biology kept the literal sense of organon: organs are the body's tools. The adjective then names the ladder of parts nested inside larger parts, which is the chart drawn by nature.
senses.whyCN: 生物学保留了 organon 的字面义：器官是身体的工具。这个形容词于是命名部分嵌套在更大整体里的阶梯，也就是大自然自己画出的那张架构图。

senses.title: Of a unit inside a system
senses.definition: relating to a named subdivision inside a computer directory or an administrative filing system
senses.definitionCN: 指计算机目录或行政档案体系中被命名的下级单元
senses.example: Create one organizational unit for each regional office in the directory.
senses.exampleCN: 在目录里为每个地区办事处建立一个组织单元。
senses.why: Software imitates the chart literally: an organizational unit is a box drawn inside a larger box. Here the word names a container in a hierarchy rather than a group of people.
senses.whyCN: 软件把架构图照字面模仿了一遍：组织单元就是画在更大方框里的一个方框。这里这个词命名的是层级中的一个容器，而不是一群真实的人。

senses.title: Good at putting things in order
senses.definition: of a person, able to plan and arrange work so that many parts move in order without confusion
senses.definitionCN: 指人能够规划并安排工作，使许多部分有序推进而不混乱
senses.example: Her organizational ability kept the archive from collapsing into piles.
senses.exampleCN: 她的统筹能力让档案室没有塌成一堆堆纸山。
senses.why: The adjective moves from the thing to the person who makes the thing. A skill is called organizational when it produces the chart in real life, with boxes that actually report to the boxes above them.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从事物转到了制造事物的人身上。当一种本领能在现实里画出那张图、并且方框真的向它上面的方框汇报时，它就被称为组织能力。

intro.en: Organizational is the adjective of organization, built with the Latin suffix -alis (English -al). Organization comes from Medieval Latin organizatio, an action noun from organizare 'to organize', which rests on Latin organum 'instrument, implement, organ of the body'. Organum itself was borrowed from Greek organon 'tool, implement, organ', a derivative of ergon 'work'. The path is therefore 'tool' → 'body part that works like a tool' → 'parts arranged to work together' → 'an institution' → the English adjective.
intro.cn: organizational 是 organization 的形容词，由拉丁后缀 -alis（英语 -al）构成。organization 来自中世纪拉丁语 organizatio，是 organizare“组织”的动作名词，而 organizare 的基础是拉丁语 organum“工具、器具、身体器官”。organum 本身借自希腊语 organon“工具、器具、器官”，由 ergon“工作”派生。因此整条路径是“工具”→“像工具一样工作的身体部件”→“被安排协同工作的各部分”→“机构”→英语形容词。

items.en: Organon means 'tool, instrument, implement' and also 'organ of the body'. It derives from ergon 'work, deed', the same root that gives English energy and ergonomic.
items.cn: organon 意为“工具、器具、器械”，也指“身体器官”。它由 ergon“工作、行为”派生，同一词根还产生英语的 energy 与 ergonomic。

items.en: Latin borrowed organon as organum, widened it to 'musical instrument', and formed the verb organizare in medieval use, 'to furnish with organs, to arrange into a working body'.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 organon 借作 organum，词义扩大到“乐器”，并在中世纪用法中造出动词 organizare，意为“装备器官、安排成一个能运转的整体”。

items.en: English organization first names the act of organizing and the state of being organized; the sense 'an organized body of persons, an institution' is established in the 17th century.
items.cn: 英语 organization 最初指“组织的行为”和“被组织起来的状态”；“由人组成的组织、机构”这一义项在 17 世纪确立。

items.en: The adjective organizational appears in the 19th century, at first in the language of institutions and administration, then spreading to psychology, biology, and computing in the 20th.
items.cn: 形容词 organizational 出现在 19 世纪，最初用于机构与行政语言，20 世纪又扩展到心理学、生物学与计算机领域。

items.en: The family is regular: organ + -ize (from Greek -izein through Latin -izare) makes the verb, -ation makes the action noun, -al makes the adjective, and -ally the adverb. Reorganization adds re- 'again'.
items.cn: 这个词族的构词很规则：organ 加 -ize（经拉丁 -izare 上溯希腊 -izein）构成动词，加 -ation 构成动作名词，加 -al 构成形容词，加 -ally 构成副词。reorganization 则再加 re-“再次”。

items.en: Organic and organism share the same organon root but took the 'living body' branch. By contrast, ornament comes from Latin ornare 'to adorn', and its orn- has nothing to do with organ-; the two only share a few letters at the front.
items.cn: organic 与 organism 共享同一个 organon 词根，只是走了“活体”这一支。相反，ornament 来自拉丁语 ornare“装饰”，其中的 orn- 与 organ- 毫无关系，两者只是词头碰巧相似。

note.en: The first group follows the organon root from tool to body part to institution, and separates one word that only looks similar. The second group compares the adjectives learners use when they mean 'about an institution' or 'about running it'.
note.cn: 第一组沿着 organon 词根，从工具走到身体部件再到机构，并区分一个只是形近的词。第二组比较学习者在表示“关于机构”或“关于管理”时最常替换的几个形容词。

entries.definition: a part of the body that performs a special function, or a musical instrument. It is the literal organon, the tool of the body, from which the institution sense grew.
entries.definitionCN: 身体中执行特定功能的部件，或指乐器。它就是字面的 organon——身体的工具，机构义正是从这里长出来的。

entries.definition: relating to living things or to food grown without chemicals. It follows the 'organ of the body' branch of organon rather than the 'arranged institution' branch.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物有关，或指不用化学物质种植的食物。它走的是 organon 中“身体器官”那一支，而不是“被安排好的机构”那一支。

entries.definition: the act of arranging parts into a working whole, or the body so formed. The adjective adds -al to this noun and simply means 'of such a body'.
entries.definitionCN: 把各部分安排成一个能运转的整体的行为，或由此形成的机构。形容词只是在名词后加 -al，表示“属于这种机构的”。

entries.definition: a decorative object. Its root is Latin ornare 'to adorn', so the orn- resembles organ- only in spelling and shares no meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰品。它的词根是拉丁语 ornare“装饰”，所以 orn- 只在拼写上像 organ-，意义上毫无关联。

entries.definition: relating to a long-established body such as a university, bank, or hospital, often stressing its formal, slow-moving character. Organizational is neutral and can describe any body, including a new one.
entries.definitionCN: 指大学、银行、医院这类长期存在的机构，常强调其正式、迟缓的特征。organizational 是中性的，可以描述任何机构，包括刚成立的。

entries.definition: relating to the work of managing records, rules, and procedures. Organizational can cover culture, structure, and psychology as well as administration.
entries.definitionCN: 指管理记录、规则与程序的工作。organizational 除行政外，还可以涵盖文化、结构与心理层面。

entries.definition: relating to managers and their duties. It names one rank inside the body, while organizational can describe the whole body or its arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指管理者及其职责。它命名机构内部的一个层级，而 organizational 可以描述整个机构或其排列方式。

entries.definition: relating to a business corporation, often with a tone of large-scale commercial identity. Organizational is wider and applies to schools, charities, and unions too.
entries.definitionCN: 指商业公司，常带大型商业主体的语气。organizational 范围更广，也适用于学校、慈善机构与工会。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: organon 'tool', ergon 'work', the -ize/-ation/-al chain, the organ that gives the family its name, and the ornare trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：organon“工具”、ergon“工作”、-ize/-ation/-al 词缀链、给整个词族命名的 organ，以及 ornare 陷阱。

normal.en: Organon is Greek for 'tool'; an organization is a tool made of people, and organizational describes whatever belongs to that tool.
normal.cn: organon 是希腊语“工具”；organization 是一件由人做成的工具，organizational 则描述属于这件工具的一切。

normal.en: Organon comes from ergon 'work', the root behind energy: a tool is what does work, and an institution is a tool that does work through people.
normal.cn: organon 出自 ergon“工作”，也就是 energy 的词根：工具就是干活的东西，而机构是通过人来干活的工具。

normal.en: The suffixes stack in order: organ → organize (verb) → organization (noun) → organizational (adjective) → organizationally (adverb).
normal.cn: 后缀按顺序叠加：organ → organize（动词）→ organization（名词）→ organizational（形容词）→ organizationally（副词）。

normal.en: An organ is a body part that works like a tool; the same word moved from the body to the body of people, which is why 'organizational structure' sounds anatomical.
normal.cn: organ 是像工具一样工作的身体部件；同一个词从身体挪到了人的集合体，所以 organizational structure 听起来像在讲解剖。

normal.en: Ornament looks close but comes from ornare 'to adorn'; a decoration adds beauty, while an organization adds order.
normal.cn: ornament 看起来相近，但出自 ornare“装饰”；装饰增添美，而组织增添秩序。

abstract.en: A chart on a wall is only ink, yet people arrive at nine and leave at six because the boxes on it agree with one another.
abstract.cn: 墙上的架构图只是墨水，可人们九点来、六点走，只因图上的方框彼此对得上。

abstract.en: An orchestra needs a score, chairs, and a conductor; none of them makes music, but together they let the players do it.
abstract.cn: 管弦乐团需要总谱、座椅和指挥；这些东西都不演奏音乐，但合在一起才让乐手奏出音乐。

abstract.en: A library's shelf numbers do not read the books, but without them no reader finds a book; structure is invisible work.
abstract.cn: 图书馆的架号不读任何一本书，但没有它读者就找不到书；结构是一种看不见的劳动。

examples.en: The study found that organizational culture mattered more than pay.
examples.cn: 研究发现，组织文化比薪酬更重要。

examples.en: She was praised for her organizational skills during the conference.
examples.cn: 会议期间，她的统筹安排能力受到了称赞。

examples.en: The software stores each department as a separate organizational unit.
examples.cn: 该软件把每个部门存成一个独立的组织单元。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥格耐贼」——奥格把散乱的人“摁”进一张格子图，一人一格，谁向谁汇报都写清楚 → organizational 组织结构的；有组织能力的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 organizare「组织」，基础是 organum「工具、器官」，再上溯希腊语 organon「工具、器官」，由 ergon「工作」派生；后缀为 -ation 与 -al。核心是「把散开的部件装成一件能干活的工具」。同族的 organic、organism 走“活体”一支，ornament（ornare「装饰」）只是形近，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of organizational all point at one drawing: scattered people and tasks fitted into a chart. What shifts is where the eye lands — on the body itself, on the lines between its boxes, on the hand that draws them, or on the skill of drawing.
sensesIntro.cn: organizational 的九个义项都指向同一张图：散乱的人与任务被装进一张架构图。变化的是视线落点——落在机构本身、落在方框之间的连线、落在画图的那只手上，还是落在画图的本领上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered people and tasks fitted into a drawn chart, each box marked with the box it reports to.
core.cn: 核心意象：散乱的人与任务被装进一张画好的架构图，每个方框都标明它向哪个方框汇报。

chain: A BODY THAT ACTS AS ONE
AND THE SKILL OF DRAWING IT

branches.en: THE BODY AND ITS LINES: the institution as a whole, and the hierarchy of roles and units inside it.
branches.cn: 机构与连线：作为整体的机构，以及其内部角色与单元的层级。

branches.en: THE HAND: management and administration, and the planning labour that arranges an event before it happens.
branches.cn: 那只手：管理与行政，以及活动发生之前的筹备劳作。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE BRANCH: workers gathered into a union, the body as a bargaining unit.
branches.cn: 集体分支：工人聚成工会，机构成为谈判单位。

branches.en: THE STUDY OF THE BODY: organizational psychology, behaviour, and theory take the chart itself as the object.
branches.cn: 对机构的研究：组织心理学、组织行为学与组织理论把这张图本身当作研究对象。

branches.en: NESTED AND PERSONAL: levels of biological organization, a unit inside a directory, and the personal skill that produces order.
branches.cn: 嵌套与个人：生物组织层次、目录中的组织单元，以及产生秩序的个人能力。

intro.en: Organizational is not a Latin word: it is English organization plus the Latin adjective ending -alis. The Latin core sits underneath, organum < Greek organon 'tool'. The family is built by regular suffix stacking rather than by new prefixes.
intro.cn: organizational 不是拉丁词：它是英语 organization 加拉丁形容词词尾 -alis。拉丁内核在其下方，即 organum < 希腊语 organon“工具”。这个词族靠规则的后缀叠加而建成，没有另加新前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer contains organum 'instrument', organizare 'to arrange into a working body', and organizatio 'arrangement'. Behind organum is Greek organon 'tool', from ergon 'work'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层包含 organum“工具”、organizare“安排成能运转的整体”、organizatio“安排”。organum 背后是希腊语 organon“工具”，再上溯 ergon“工作”。

items.meaning: of or belonging to an organized body
items.meaningCN: 属于某个被组织起来的机构的（-al 形容词后缀）
items.example: The organizational chart lists every reporting line.
items.exampleCN: 组织架构图列出了每一条汇报线。

items.meaning: the act of arranging parts, or the body so arranged
items.meaningCN: 安排各部分的行为，或由此形成的机构（-ation 动作／结果名词）
items.example: The organization has three regional offices.
items.exampleCN: 这个机构有三个地区办事处。

items.meaning: to furnish with parts and set them working together
items.meaningCN: 给事物配备部件并使其协同运转；组织（-ize 动词后缀）
items.example: They organized the files by year and by author.
items.exampleCN: 他们按年份和作者整理文件。

items.meaning: a person who arranges an event, or a container that keeps things in order
items.meaningCN: 安排活动的人，或使物品有条理的收纳盒（-er 施动者）
items.example: The conference organizer sent the schedule by email.
items.exampleCN: 会议组织者通过邮件发来了日程。

items.meaning: a body part with a special function, or a musical instrument
items.meaningCN: 有特定功能的器官，或乐器
items.example: The liver is the largest internal organ.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏是最大的内部器官。

items.meaning: of living bodies, or grown without chemical inputs
items.meaningCN: 与生物体有关的，或不用化学投入物种植的（-ic 形容词）
items.example: The farm sells organic vegetables.
items.exampleCN: 这个农场出售有机蔬菜。

items.meaning: in terms of the way an institution is arranged
items.meaningCN: 从机构安排的角度来说（-ly 副词后缀）
items.example: The two units are organizationally separate.
items.exampleCN: 这两个单位在组织上是分开的。

items.meaning: a fresh arranging of an existing body
items.meaningCN: 对现有机构重新进行安排；改组（re- 再次）
items.example: The reorganization merged two departments.
items.exampleCN: 这次改组把两个部门合并了。

items.meaning: lacking order, with parts not fitted together
items.meaningCN: 缺少秩序、各部分未配合好的（dis- 否定）
items.example: His desk was disorganized but his notes were exact.
items.exampleCN: 他的书桌很乱，笔记却很精确。

latinEntries.meaning: to furnish with organs, to arrange into a working body
latinEntries.meaningCN: 装备器官；安排成能运转的整体

latinEntries.meaning: an arranging, the state of being arranged
instrument, implement, musical instrument, organ of the body

definition_zh: 朝向；方位；方向感；迎新介绍；取向；定位；定向能力；（材料的）取向
definition_en: the direction in which something faces, the ability to know where you are, an introduction to a new place or role, or the aim toward which a person or policy is turned
core_image: 指南针的针在罗盘上找到自己的北，随后所有方向都从这一指算起
scene: 新生报到第一天，老师带大家绕校园走一圈，把食堂、图书馆和宿舍一一指出来。The campus tour on the first day is the orientation for new students.
sceneCN: 这里 orientation 是「迎新介绍」（第 3 个义项：帮助刚到新环境的人熟悉地方与流程的介绍活动）；句意：第一天的校园参观就是给新生的迎新介绍。

pos.zh: 朝向；方位；方向感；迎新介绍；取向；定向

collocations.zh: 迎新项目；入职培训计划

derivatives.zh: 东方的；东方人（旧称，今多含争议）

senses.title: The direction a thing faces
senses.definition: the direction in which a building, object, or structure is placed or turned relative to its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物、物体或结构相对于周围环境被放置或转向的方向
senses.example: The orientation of the chapel windows lets the morning sun fall on the altar.
senses.exampleCN: 小教堂窗户的朝向让晨光正好落在祭坛上。
senses.why: Latin oriens is the rising sun, the east. The first orientation was literally a turning toward the east; any facing direction is that same needle settling on a point.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 oriens 是“升起的太阳”，也就是东方。最早的 orientation 字面上就是“朝东”；任何朝向都是同一根指针停在某个点上。

senses.title: Knowing where you are
senses.titleCN: 知道自己在哪的方向感
senses.definition: the ability to judge your position and the direction you are facing, especially after a change of place
senses.definitionCN: 判断自己所在位置与所面方向的能力，尤其是在换了地方之后
senses.example: He lost his orientation in the unlit stairwell and climbed the wrong way.
senses.exampleCN: 他在没有灯的楼梯井里失去了方向感，爬错了方向。
senses.why: The compass needle inside you has to find north before the body can move. When that inner needle fails, the word names the missing skill rather than the direction of any object.
senses.whyCN: 身体移动之前，你心里那根罗盘针必须先找到北。当这根内心的针失灵时，这个词命名的是缺失的能力，而不是某个物体所朝的方向。

senses.title: An introduction to a new place
senses.definition: an organized introduction that helps new students, employees, or members learn where things are and how they work
senses.definitionCN: 帮助新学生、新员工或新成员了解地方与流程的有组织介绍活动
senses.example: Orientation week ends with a tour of the library and the health center.
senses.exampleCN: 迎新周以参观图书馆和医疗中心结束。
senses.why: A newcomer has no needle yet. Orientation hands them one: a map, a schedule, and the names of the rooms, so that they can face the right way on their first Monday.
senses.whyCN: 新来的人还没有自己的针。迎新介绍递给他们一根：一张地图、一份日程、各个房间的名字，好让他们在第一个周一就朝向正确的方向。

senses.title: The set of beliefs that directs a person
senses.titleCN: 指导一个人的那套信念
senses.definition: the beliefs, values, or interests that set the direction of a person's thinking, politics, or desire
senses.definitionCN: 决定一个人思想、政治立场或情感指向的信念、价值观或兴趣
senses.example: The survey asked about religious orientation but not about party affiliation.
senses.exampleCN: 调查询问了宗教取向，却没有询问党派归属。
senses.why: The needle no longer points north but toward a value. Orientation here means the direction a mind has settled on, which explains why the word works for politics, religion, and sexuality alike.
senses.whyCN: 指针不再指向北，而是指向某种价值。这里的 orientation 指思想已经落定的方向，这解释了为什么它同时适用于政治、宗教与性取向。

senses.title: Turning something toward a purpose
senses.definition: the act of aiming a policy, institution, or product toward a particular purpose, audience, or market
senses.definitionCN: 把政策、机构或产品对准某个目的、受众或市场的行动
senses.example: The new funding rules mark a clear orientation toward basic research.
senses.exampleCN: 新的资助规则明显转向了基础研究。
senses.why: This is orientation as an action: someone physically turns the object so that its face is toward the goal. Policy language borrows the gesture and calls the resulting aim an orientation.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 orientation 是一个动作：有人把物体实际转过来，让它的正面朝向目标。政策语言借用了这个动作，并把由此形成的目标称为“导向”。

senses.title: Aligning a map or instrument
senses.titleCN: 把地图或仪器对齐方位
senses.definition: the act of turning a map, instrument, or device so that its markings agree with the points of the compass
senses.definitionCN: 转动地图、仪器或装置，使其标记与罗盘方位一致的动作
senses.example: Check the orientation of the map before you trust the trail markers.
senses.exampleCN: 在相信路标之前，先检查地图有没有定向。
senses.why: The original technical sense survives here in its purest form: the paper must be turned until its north matches the world's north. Orientation is that turning, not the direction that results.
senses.whyCN: 最初的技术义在这里以最纯粹的形式保留下来：必须转动纸面，直到图上的北与世界的北对上。orientation 指的是这个转动动作，而不是转出来的方向。

senses.title: How animals find their way
senses.definition: the way animals determine and maintain a direction during migration, homing, or daily movement
senses.definitionCN: 动物在迁徙、归巢或日常移动中判断并保持方向的方式
senses.example: Sea turtles rely on magnetic orientation to cross open water.
senses.exampleCN: 海龟依靠磁定向穿越开阔海域。
senses.why: Biology applies the compass to a living body. The animal carries its own needle — magnetic, solar, or chemical — and orientation names the process by which that needle is read.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把这根罗盘用到了活的躯体上。动物自带一根针——磁的、太阳的或化学的——orientation 命名的是读取这根针的过程。

senses.title: The alignment of molecules or fibres
senses.titleCN: 分子或纤维的排列取向
senses.definition: the arrangement of molecules, fibres, or crystals along a common axis, which changes the strength or behaviour of a material
senses.definitionCN: 分子、纤维或晶体沿同一轴线排列的方式，这种排列会改变材料的强度或性能
senses.example: Pulling the polymer through a die increases the orientation of its chains.
senses.exampleCN: 把聚合物拉过模口会增加其分子链的取向程度。
senses.why: At the micro-scale the needle is a long molecule. When all of them lie the same way, the material gains strength, so orientation moves from 'which way it faces' to 'how its parts are lined up'.
senses.whyCN: 在微观尺度上，指针就是一根长分子。当所有分子都朝同一方向躺下时，材料就获得强度，于是 orientation 从“朝哪边”转成“内部如何排列”。

senses.title: Finding a vocational direction
senses.definition: the process of helping a person identify the kind of study or work that suits their interests and abilities
senses.definitionCN: 帮助一个人找出适合其兴趣与能力的学习或工作方向的过程
senses.example: The careers service offers vocational orientation in the second year.
senses.exampleCN: 就业服务中心在二年级提供职业定向辅导。
senses.why: A young person without a direction is like a traveller without a compass. The counsellor supplies readings — interests, aptitudes, values — until one bearing feels like north.
senses.whyCN: 没有方向的年轻人就像没有罗盘的旅人。辅导员提供各种读数——兴趣、性向、价值观——直到某个方位读起来像“北”。

intro.en: Orientation is English orient plus the Latin action suffix -ation (-ationem). Orient goes back to Latin oriens, orientem, 'the east, the rising sun', the present participle of oriri 'to rise'. The word first named the act of turning a church or building toward the east, then any facing, then a map's alignment, and only in the 20th century an introduction for newcomers. The same oriri underlies origin, original, and originality.
intro.cn: orientation 是英语 orient 加拉丁动作后缀 -ation（-ationem）。orient 上溯拉丁语 oriens、orientem“东方、升起的太阳”，即 oriri“升起”的现在分词。这个词最早指把教堂或建筑朝东，之后指任何朝向，再指地图定向，直到 20 世纪才指对新来者的介绍。同一个 oriri 也是 origin、original、originality 的源头。

items.en: Oriens, orientem is 'the east' and literally 'the rising one', from oriri 'to come up, rise', used of the sun. The noun orient entered English in the 14th century as the east.
items.cn: oriens、orientem 意为“东方”，字面是“升起者”，出自 oriri“升起”，专用于太阳。名词 orient 在 14 世纪以“东方”进入英语。

items.en: Orientation first appears in English in the 17th century for the action of turning toward the east, especially the ritual placement of a church altar, and for the arrangement of a building relative to the compass.
items.cn: orientation 在 17 世纪首次出现在英语中，指“转向东方”的动作，尤指教堂祭坛的仪式性朝向，也指建筑物相对罗盘的布置。

items.en: The sense widens from east to any direction, and then to the act of aligning a map or instrument with the compass. The figurative sense of a person's political or intellectual bearing follows.
items.cn: 词义从“东”扩大到任何方向，再扩大到把地图或仪器与罗盘对齐的动作。随后出现比喻义，指一个人的政治或思想方位。

items.en: American colleges and employers begin to call the introduction for newcomers an orientation, because it teaches them which way everything faces. The usage spreads to vocational and psychological guidance.
items.cn: 20 世纪 40 年代，美国高校与雇主开始把对新来者的介绍称为 orientation，因为它教人认清一切事物的朝向。这一用法随后扩展到职业与心理辅导。

items.en: The -ation ending is Latin -ationem, an action noun. It makes orientation name the act of turning and, by transference, the resulting direction — which is why one word covers both 'the turning' and 'the bearing'.
items.cn: -ation 词尾是拉丁 -ationem，构成动作名词。它让 orientation 既命名“转”的动作，又转指转出来的方向——所以一个词同时覆盖“转向”与“方位”。

items.en: Ornament comes from Latin ornare 'to adorn' and shares nothing with oriri. Orientation, origin, original, and abortive's oriri branch form one family; ornament's orn- is decoration, not rising.
items.cn: ornament 来自拉丁语 ornare“装饰”，与 oriri 毫无关系。orientation、origin、original 属同一词族；ornament 的 orn- 表示装饰，与“升起”无关。

note.en: The first group follows the family from the verb orient through the noun origin and one spelling trap. The second group separates the words used for direction, for a sense of place, for an induction, and for a line-up.
note.cn: 第一组沿着词族从动词 orient 走到名词 origin，并区分一个拼写陷阱。第二组分辨用于“方向”“方位感”“入职引导”“对齐”的几个词。

entries.definition: to turn or place something so that it faces a particular direction, or the east as a noun. Orientation is the action noun built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物转向或置于某个方向；作名词时指东方。orientation 是在它之上构成的动作名词。

entries.definition: the point where something begins or comes from. It shares oriri 'to rise' with orientation, but its image is the source of a river, not the needle of a compass.
entries.definitionCN: 事物开始或来源的那一点。它与 orientation 共享 oriri“升起”，但意象是河流的源头，而不是罗盘的指针。

entries.definition: a decorative object or addition. Its root is ornare 'to adorn'; the shared or- is a coincidence of spelling, not of meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰物或装饰性的添加。它的词根是 ornare“装饰”；相同的 or- 只是拼写巧合，意义无关。

entries.definition: a sport in which runners find their way across unknown ground with a map and compass. It is built on orient plus -eer and -ing, and keeps the literal compass sense.
entries.definitionCN: 参赛者凭地图和罗盘在陌生地形中找路的运动。它由 orient 加 -eer 与 -ing 构成，保留了字面的罗盘义。

entries.definition: the line along which something moves or faces. It is the bare geometric word, with no image of a needle finding north.
entries.definitionCN: 事物移动或朝向的那条线。它是纯几何词，没有“指针找到北”的画面。

entries.definition: your position relative to surrounding places, chiefly in the phrase to get your bearings. It is the personal sense of orientation, not the formal act of aligning.
entries.definitionCN: 你相对于周围地点的位置，主要用于短语 to get your bearings。它偏指个人的方位感，而非正式的定向动作。

entries.definition: the formal process of introducing a new employee or member to rules and duties. It stresses procedure, while orientation stresses learning where things are.
entries.definitionCN: 把新员工或新成员正式引入规则与职责的过程。它强调程序，而 orientation 强调了解事物在何处。

entries.definition: the state of being arranged in a straight line or in agreement. It is the physical or strategic lining-up, not the compass-facing that orientation names.
entries.definitionCN: 排成直线或达成一致的状态。它指物理或战略上的对齐，而不是 orientation 所指的朝向罗盘。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: oriri 'to rise', oriens 'east', the 17th-century church use, the 1940s campus use, and the ornare trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：oriri“升起”、oriens“东方”、17 世纪的教堂用法、20 世纪 40 年代的校园用法，以及 ornare 陷阱。

normal.en: Oriens is the rising sun: orientation began as turning a church toward the east, so every later 'facing' keeps the sunrise in it.
normal.cn: oriens 是升起的太阳：orientation 最初指把教堂转向东方，所以后来每一种“朝向”里都留着那个日出。

normal.en: Oriri 'to rise' also gives origin and original: the place where the sun comes up and the place where a thing begins are one idea.
normal.cn: oriri“升起”也产生 origin 与 original：太阳升起的地方和事物开始的地方，是同一个想法。

normal.en: A map is oriented when its north matches the world's north; the word names the turning, and the direction is what the turning produces.
normal.cn: 地图定向，就是让图上的北与世界上的北对齐；这个词命名的是转的动作，方向是转出来的结果。

normal.en: In the 1940s American campuses gave newcomers an orientation: a tour that points their inner compass at the right buildings.
normal.cn: 20 世纪 40 年代的美国校园给新生安排 orientation：一趟把内心罗盘指到正确楼房的参观。

normal.en: Ornament is from ornare 'to adorn'; decoration changes how a thing looks, orientation changes which way it faces.
normal.cn: ornament 出自 ornare“装饰”；装饰改变事物的外观，orientation 改变事物的朝向。

abstract.en: A needle does not know north; it only refuses to rest anywhere else. Orientation is the refusal that becomes a direction.
abstract.cn: 指针并不认识北；它只是拒绝停在别处。orientation 就是这种拒绝变成的方向。

abstract.en: Standing in a new city at dusk, you turn your body until the map and the streets agree; that small turn is the whole word.
abstract.cn: 黄昏站在陌生城市里，你转动身体，直到地图与街道对上；这个小小的转动就是这个词的全部。

abstract.en: A molecule lying the same way as its neighbours is a compass needle at the scale of the invisible.
abstract.cn: 一个与邻居躺向相同的分子，就是一根存在于不可见尺度上的罗盘针。

examples.en: The orientation of the solar panels was adjusted for the winter sun.
examples.cn: 太阳能板的朝向按冬季日照做了调整。

examples.en: New employees spend their first morning in orientation.
examples.cn: 新员工第一个上午参加入职介绍。

examples.en: The fibres show strong orientation along the direction of the draw.
examples.cn: 纤维沿拉伸方向表现出很强的取向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥瑞恩泰申」——奥瑞恩（太阳神）一升起来，罗盘就知道哪边是东，所有方向都从这一点算 → orientation 朝向；方位；迎新介绍（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 oriens/orientem「东方、升起的太阳」，出自 oriri「升起」；后缀 -ation 为拉丁动作名词词尾。核心是「让一根针找到北，其他方向都由它算起」。同族含 orient、origin、original，均出自 oriri；ornament（ornare「装饰」）只是形近，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of orientation all begin with a needle finding north. What changes is what is being turned — a building, a map, a mind, a policy, a molecule, or a newcomer — and whether we name the turning or the bearing it produces.
sensesIntro.cn: orientation 的九个义项都从“一根针找到北”开始。变化的是被转的是什么——建筑、地图、思想、政策、分子或新来的人——以及我们命名的是转的动作，还是转出来的方位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a compass needle finding its north, with every other direction measured from that one point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根罗盘针找到自己的北，其他所有方向都从这一点量起。

branches.en: PHYSICAL FACING: a building's placement, a map turned to the compass, and molecules lined along one axis.
branches.cn: 物理朝向：建筑的布置、地图与罗盘对齐，以及分子沿同一轴线排列。

branches.en: LIVING DIRECTION-FINDING: a person's sense of place and an animal's magnetic or solar navigation.
branches.cn: 生命体的定向：人的方位感，以及动物依靠磁场或太阳导航。

branches.en: THE GIVEN COMPASS: an introduction that hands a newcomer a map, a schedule, and room names.
branches.cn: 被递来的罗盘：一份把地图、日程与房间名交给新来者的介绍。

branches.en: THE INWARD NEEDLE: beliefs and values that direct a person, and the act of aiming a policy or product at a purpose.
branches.cn: 内心的针：指导一个人的信念与价值观，以及把政策或产品对准某个目的的行动。

branches.en: VOCATIONAL BEARING: guidance that helps a young person read their interests as a direction.
branches.cn: 职业方位：帮助年轻人把兴趣读成一个方向的辅导。

intro.en: Orientation is orient plus -ation, a Latin action-noun suffix. Orient is not a suffix-built word: it comes whole from Latin oriens, the rising sun. English then added -al for the adjective and -ation for the noun, and re- and dis- for the two reversals.
intro.cn: orientation 是 orient 加 -ation（拉丁动作名词后缀）。orient 不是靠后缀造出来的：它整体来自拉丁语 oriens“升起的太阳”。英语随后加 -al 构成形容词、加 -ation 构成名词，并用 re- 与 dis- 表示两种反向。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is oriri 'to rise', oriens/orientem 'the east', and the derived noun ortus 'a rising'. The compass sense is English, not Latin: Latin had no orientation in the modern sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 oriri“升起”、oriens/orientem“东方”，以及派生名词 ortus“升起”。罗盘义是英语自己发展出来的，拉丁语并没有现代意义上的 orientation。

items.meaning: the act of turning toward a point, and the bearing that results
items.meaningCN: 转向某一点的动作，以及由此形成的方位（-ation 动作名词）
items.example: The orientation of the antenna must match the transmitter.
items.exampleCN: 天线的朝向必须与发射机一致。

items.structure: Latin oriens, orientem 'east, rising sun' (from oriri)
items.meaning: to turn toward a direction; the east
items.meaningCN: 使朝向某方向；东方
items.example: Orient the map before you read the trail.
items.exampleCN: 读路标之前先把地图定向。

items.meaning: turned toward, or built around, a particular aim
items.meaningCN: 朝向某物的，或以某个目标为核心的（-ed 分词形容词）
items.example: The course is oriented toward laboratory work.
items.exampleCN: 这门课以实验室工作为导向。

items.meaning: of the east; now often avoided as a label for people
items.meaningCN: 东方的；今用于指人时常被视为不当标签
items.example: The museum's oriental collection is being renamed.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆的东方藏品正在被重新命名。

items.meaning: relating to orientation as a property
items.meaningCN: 与取向或朝向这一属性有关的
items.example: The study measured orientational order in the crystal.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究测量了晶体中的取向有序度。

items.meaning: a turning to a new direction
items.meaningCN: 转向新的方向；重新定向（re- 再次）
items.example: The firm announced a reorientation toward services.
items.exampleCN: 公司宣布向服务业重新定位。

items.meaning: loss of one's sense of direction or place
items.meaningCN: 失去方向感或位置感；定向障碍（dis- 去除）
items.example: Jet lag left her with a mild disorientation.
items.exampleCN: 时差让她有点失去方向感。

items.meaning: the sport of finding one's way with map and compass
items.meaningCN: 凭地图和罗盘找路的运动（-eer 人 + -ing 活动名词）
items.example: Orienteering requires both speed and map reading.
items.exampleCN: 定向越野既需要速度，也需要读图能力。

items.meaning: the British variant of orient as a verb
items.meaningCN: 英式英语中 orient 作动词的变体
items.example: New staff are orientated to the building layout.
items.exampleCN: 新员工会被告知楼内布局。

latinEntries.meaning: to rise, come up, be born

latinEntries.structure: present participle of oriri, genitive orientis

definition_zh: 独创性；原创性；新颖；创造力；真迹性；独到见解；（版权法上的）独创性
definition_en: the quality of being new and made by the author rather than copied, the ability to produce such work, or the state of being the first of its kind
core_image: 同一块地里长出第一株从未见过的苗，而不是照着别人开过的花再描一遍
scene: 评审翻开投稿，先看论文里有没有属于作者自己的东西，还是只把别人的结论换了说法。The editor first asks whether the paper has any originality.
sceneCN: 这里 originality 是「原创贡献」（第 5 个义项：研究中属于作者自己的新发现）；句意：评审首先问这篇论文有没有原创贡献。

pos.zh: 独创性；原创性；新颖；创造力；真迹性

derivatives.zh: 最初的；原创的；原作；原件

senses.title: Made by its author, not copied
senses.titleCN: 由作者自己写出而非抄袭的
senses.definition: the quality of a work that comes from its author's own making rather than from imitation or copying
senses.definitionCN: 作品出自作者自己的创作，而不是模仿或抄袭而来的品质
senses.example: The committee questioned the originality of the passage, not its accuracy.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会质疑的是这段文字是否原创，而不是它是否准确。
senses.why: Oriri is 'to rise'. The first sprout in a field rises from the soil itself; a traced flower rises from another drawing. Originality names the first kind of rising.
senses.whyCN: oriri 是“升起”。田里第一株新芽是从土壤里自己升起来的；照着描的花是从另一张画上升起来的。originality 命名的是前一种升起。

senses.title: The quality of being new
senses.definition: the quality of being fresh and unlike what has been done before, even if the parts are familiar
senses.definitionCN: 新鲜、不同于以往所做之事的品质，即使各个组成部分本身并不陌生
senses.example: The design borrows old materials but arranges them with real originality.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计借用了旧材料，却以真正新颖的方式把它们组织起来。
senses.why: Newness is the sprout seen from a distance: you cannot yet say what it is, only that nothing in the field looked like it before. Originality is that visible difference.
senses.whyCN: 新颖是从远处看到的那株新芽：你还说不出它是什么，只知道田里从前没有东西像它。originality 就是这种看得见的差别。

senses.title: The power to invent
senses.definition: a person's ability to produce new ideas, designs, or works rather than only to improve existing ones
senses.definitionCN: 一个人产生新想法、新设计或新作品，而不只是改良现有事物的能力
senses.example: Her originality showed in the questions she asked, not in the answers.
senses.exampleCN: 她的创造力体现在她提出的问题上，而不是她给出的答案上。
senses.why: Here originality moves from the work to the maker. The field does not grow sprouts by itself; someone must decide to plant something that was not in the seed catalogue.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 originality 从作品转到了创作者身上。田地不会自己长出新芽；必须有人决定种下种子目录里没有的东西。

senses.title: The authenticity of an original
senses.definition: the quality of being the actual work made by the artist, as opposed to a copy, print, or reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 作品确为艺术家本人所作，而非复制品、印制品或仿制品的品质
senses.example: Experts verified the painting's originality before the auction.
senses.exampleCN: 拍卖前专家鉴定了这幅画是否为真迹。
senses.why: The original is the first rising; a copy is a second rising from the same source. This sense asks not whether the work is new but whether it is the very first one.
senses.whyCN: 原作是第一次升起；复制品是从同一源头第二次升起。这个义项问的不是作品新不新，而是它是不是最初那一件。

senses.title: A contribution that is the author's own
senses.titleCN: 属于作者自己的学术贡献
senses.definition: the element in research or scholarship that is newly contributed by its author rather than restated from earlier work
senses.definitionCN: 研究或学术成果中由作者新近贡献、而非复述前人工作的那部分
senses.example: The thesis is sound, but its originality lies in one chapter only.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文站得住脚，但真正的原创贡献只在一章里。
senses.why: Scholarship is a field already full of plants. Originality here is the one seedling the author actually brought, as distinct from the careful transplanting of everyone else's.
senses.whyCN: 学术领域是一片已经长满植物的田。这里的 originality 指作者真正带来的那一株苗，区别于对别人植株的精心移栽。

senses.title: An independent turn of mind
senses.definition: the habit of thinking for oneself and reaching conclusions that are not simply borrowed from the group
senses.definitionCN: 自己动脑思考、不直接把群体结论拿来用的习惯
senses.example: He answered with an originality that annoyed the panel and convinced it.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答带着一种独到的思路，既让评审不快，又说服了他们。
senses.why: A mind can also face a direction of its own. When it does not simply align with the crowd's compass, we call the resulting bearing originality of thought.
senses.whyCN: 思想也能有自己的朝向。当它不单纯与人群的罗盘对齐时，我们把由此形成的方位称为思想的独创性。

senses.title: The threshold required by copyright
senses.titleCN: 版权法要求的独创性门槛
senses.definition: the minimal degree of independent creative effort that a work must show to be protected by copyright
senses.definitionCN: 作品要获得版权保护，必须表现出的最低限度的独立创造性投入
senses.example: A phone book may fail the originality test even if it took months to compile.
senses.exampleCN: 电话簿即使编了几个月，也可能通不过独创性检验。
senses.why: Law needs a measurable line between a new plant and a copied one. Originality here is not genius but a threshold: enough of the author's own arrangement to count as a rising.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要在“新长出的植株”与“复制来的植株”之间划一条可量化的线。这里的 originality 不是天才，而是一道门槛：作者自己的安排要足够多，才算一次“升起”。

senses.title: How original a work is
senses.definition: the degree to which a particular work departs from existing models, used in comparisons and evaluations
senses.definitionCN: 某件作品偏离现有范本的程度，用于比较与评价
senses.example: The two novels differ less in theme than in originality of treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 这两部小说在主题上差别不大，差别在于处理方式的原创程度。
senses.why: Once originality is a quality, it can be measured like height. This sense treats it as a variable — a little, a lot, none — rather than as a yes-or-no label.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 originality 成为一种品质，它就能像高度一样被测量。这个义项把它当作一个变量——一点、很多、没有——而不是是或否的标签。

senses.title: A distinctly personal style
senses.definition: the quality of a person's manner or style that is recognizably their own and not a copy of a current fashion
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的举止或风格明显属于自己、而非照搬当下流行的品质
senses.example: The director's originality is visible in the silence she leaves in a scene.
senses.exampleCN: 这位导演的独特性体现在她在一场戏里留下的沉默中。
senses.why: The sprout does not merely differ from other plants; it could only have grown from this soil. Originality in style is that signature which no other field would produce.
senses.whyCN: 新芽不只是与其他植株不同；它只可能从这块土里长出来。风格上的 originality 就是那种别的田地长不出来的签名。

intro.en: Originality is original plus the Latin noun suffix -ity (-itatem). Original goes back to Latin originalis, from origo, originem 'beginning, source, birth', which derives from oriri 'to rise' — the same verb behind orient and orientation. The word therefore carries a sunrise inside it: something original is where a thing first comes up. English first used originality for the fact of deriving from a source, and only later for the power of producing something new.
intro.cn: originality 是 original 加拉丁名词后缀 -ity（-itatem）。original 上溯拉丁语 originalis，出自 origo、originem“开始、源头、诞生”，而后者来自 oriri“升起”——也就是 orient 与 orientation 背后的同一个动词。因此这个词内部装着一次日出：original 的事物就是事物最初升起来的地方。英语最早用 originality 指“源自某处”这一事实，后来才指“产生新事物的能力”。

items.en: Origo, originem means 'a beginning, source, birth, descent'. It comes from oriri 'to rise', whose participle oriens gives the east and the sunrise; origin is where a river or family rises.
items.cn: origo、originem 意为“开始、源头、诞生、出身”。它出自 oriri“升起”，其分词 oriens 产生“东方”与“日出”；origin 就是河流或家族升起的地方。

items.en: Original enters English as 'first, earliest, initial', and soon also as a noun meaning the first model or text from which copies are made.
items.cn: original 以“最初的、最早的”进入英语，很快又作名词，指据以复制的最初范本或原文。

items.en: Originality is recorded in the 18th century for the quality of being original in the modern sense. An older, now rare sense named the fact of being derived from a particular source.
items.cn: originality 在 18 世纪被记录，指现代意义上的“原创性”。更早一个今已罕用的义项指“源自某一特定出处”这一事实。

items.en: Romantic criticism makes originality a virtue of the artist rather than a property of texts, and the word shifts from source-tracking to creative praise.
items.cn: 浪漫主义批评把 originality 说成艺术家的美德，而不只是文本的属性，这个词于是从“追溯来源”转向“赞扬创造”。

items.en: Copyright law adopts the term as a threshold of independent creative effort, while research funding adopts it as a criterion for novelty. Both keep the image of a first rising.
items.cn: 版权法把这个词采纳为独立创造性投入的门槛，科研资助则把它采纳为新意标准。两者都保留了“第一次升起”的意象。

items.en: Origin, original, originality, orient, and orientation all descend from oriri. Ornament, by contrast, comes from ornare 'to adorn' and is not related, since decoration is not a rising.
items.cn: origin、original、originality、orient、orientation 都出自 oriri。相反，ornament 来自 ornare“装饰”，并不相关，因为装饰不是一次升起。

note.en: The first group follows the oriri family and marks the one spelling trap. The second group separates the words for new work, new ideas, new methods, and a distinct personal character.
note.cn: 第一组沿着 oriri 词族，并标出一个拼写陷阱。第二组分辨表示“新作品”“新想法”“新方法”与“个人特质”的几个词。

entries.definition: the point from which something starts. It shares oriri 'to rise' with originality but names the source, not the newness of what came from it.
entries.definitionCN: 事物开始的那一点。它与 originality 共享 oriri“升起”，但命名的是源头，而不是从源头生出之物有多新。

entries.definition: first in time, or produced by the maker rather than copied; also the first version itself. Originality is the abstract noun built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 时间上最早的，或由创作者自己做出而非复制的；也指最初的版本本身。originality 是在它之上构成的抽象名词。

entries.definition: to begin in a place or from a cause, or to create something new. It describes the act of rising, while originality names the quality of the thing that rises.
entries.definitionCN: 在某处开始或由某原因产生，或创造新事物。它描述“升起”的动作，而 originality 命名升起之物的品质。

entries.definition: a decoration. Its root is ornare 'to adorn', not oriri 'to rise'; the shared or- is spelling only, so it never means novelty or source.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰物。它的词根是 ornare“装饰”，而不是 oriri“升起”；相同的 or- 只是拼写，所以它从不表示新颖或来源。

entries.definition: the quality of being new or unusual, or a small new thing. It stresses freshness only and says nothing about who made it or how much effort it took.
entries.definitionCN: 新颖或不同寻常的品质，也指新奇的小物件。它只强调新鲜，不说明是谁做的、花了多少功夫。

entries.definition: the ability to produce original and imaginative work. It names the capacity of the maker, while originality can also name the quality of the work itself.
entries.definitionCN: 产生原创且富想象力作品的能力。它命名创作者的能力，而 originality 也可以命名作品本身的品质。

entries.definition: a new method, product, or idea that is actually adopted. It stresses practical introduction, whereas originality may never leave the studio.
entries.definitionCN: 真正被采用的新方法、新产品或新想法。它强调实际引入，而 originality 可能从未走出工作室。

entries.definition: the qualities that make one person or thing different from all others. It is about distinct identity, while originality is about not copying a model.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物区别于其他一切的特性。它关乎独特身份，而 originality 关乎没有照抄范本。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: oriri 'to rise', origo 'source', the -ity suffix, the 18th-century shift from source to praise, and the ornare trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：oriri“升起”、origo“源头”、-ity 后缀、18 世纪从“来源”到“赞扬”的转变，以及 ornare 陷阱。

normal.en: Oriri is 'to rise': an original work is a new sprout rising from the soil, not a tracing of a flower that rose earlier.
normal.cn: oriri 是“升起”：原创作品是从土里升起的新芽，而不是对更早开过的花的描摹。

normal.en: Origo is the source: origin, original, originality and orient all come from the same verb, so the sunrise and the beginning are one image.
normal.cn: origo 是源头：origin、original、originality 与 orient 都出自同一个动词，所以日出与开端是同一个意象。

normal.en: -ity turns the adjective original into a noun, the same way -ity turns active into activity: the suffix names a quality, not a person.
normal.cn: -ity 把形容词 original 变成名词，就像把 active 变成 activity：这个后缀命名的是品质，不是人。

normal.en: Romantic critics moved the word from 'where it came from' to 'how new it is'; the older sense survives only in technical writing.
normal.cn: 浪漫主义批评把这个词从“它来自哪里”挪到“它有多新”；旧义今天只在技术性文字里残留。

normal.en: Ornament is from ornare 'to adorn': decorations imitate nothing and originate nothing, so the similar spelling is a false friend.
normal.cn: ornament 出自 ornare“装饰”：装饰既不模仿什么，也不创始什么，所以相似的拼写是假朋友。

abstract.en: Two seeds in the same soil: one grows into a plant no one has seen, the other is a photograph of a plant. Only the first is original.
abstract.cn: 同一块土里的两粒种子：一粒长成谁也没见过的植物，另一粒是一张植物的照片。只有第一粒是原创的。

abstract.en: A signature is valuable not because the letters are pretty but because no other hand could have made them.
abstract.cn: 签名的价值不在于字好看，而在于没有第二只手能写出同样的字。

abstract.en: Copyright asks a modest question: did this rise from its author, or was it lifted whole from somewhere else?
abstract.cn: 版权只问一个很朴素的问题：它是从作者那里升起来的，还是整个从别处搬来的？

examples.en: The judges praised the film for its visual originality.
examples.cn: 评委称赞这部影片在视觉上的独创性。

examples.en: Her research shows originality in both method and question.
examples.cn: 她的研究在方法与问题两方面都显出原创性。

examples.en: The court found that the logo lacked the originality required for protection.
examples.cn: 法院认定该标志缺乏受保护所需的独创性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥瑞吉纳勒提」——奥瑞吉（origin 的源头）一个人第一次把种子撒进田里，长出的苗别人都没见过 → originality 独创性；原创性（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 origo/originem「开始、源头、诞生」，出自 oriri「升起」；后缀 -ity（拉丁 -itatem）构成抽象名词。核心是「同一块田里自己长出的第一株新苗，而不是描下来的花」。同族含 origin、original、originate、orient、orientation；ornament（ornare「装饰」）只是形近，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of originality all look at one sprout rising from its own soil. What changes is whether we judge the sprout (newness, authenticity, degree), the gardener (ability, independence, style), or the field's rule for calling something new (copyright, research).
sensesIntro.cn: originality 的九个义项都在看同一株从自己的土里升起的苗。变化的是我们评判的对象：苗本身（新颖、真迹、程度）、种它的人（才能、独立、风格），还是领域里判定“新”的规则（版权、学术）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first sprout rising from its own soil, rather than a flower traced from someone else's drawing.
core.cn: 核心意象：从自己的土里升起来的第一株苗，而不是照着别人的画描下来的花。

chain: A SIGNATURE ONLY THIS SOIL GIVES

branches.en: THE SPROUT: a work made by its author and visibly new against what came before.
branches.cn: 那株苗：由作者自己写出、相对先前作品明显新颖的作品。

branches.en: THE GARDENER: the ability to invent, and the independent turn of mind that refuses the crowd's compass.
branches.cn: 种苗的人：发明创造的才能，以及拒绝随大流的独立思考。

branches.en: THE FIRST PLANT: authenticity, the very object the artist made rather than a later copy.
branches.cn: 最初的植株：真迹性，即艺术家亲手所做的那一件，而非后来的复制品。

branches.en: THE FIELD'S RULES: the author's own contribution in research, and the legal threshold of creative effort.
branches.cn: 领域的规则：研究中属于作者自己的贡献，以及法律上的创造性投入门槛。

branches.en: MEASURE AND MANNER: how far a work departs from models, and a personal style only this maker could produce.
branches.cn: 程度与风格：作品偏离范本多远，以及只有这位创作者才能产生的个人风格。

intro.en: Originality is original plus -ity, from Latin -itatem, a suffix that makes a quality noun. Original itself carries -al (Latin -alis) on the stem origin-. The Latin base is origo, originem, from oriri 'to rise'; no English prefix is added.
intro.cn: originality 是 original 加 -ity（拉丁 -itatem），这个后缀构成表品质的名词。original 本身在词干 origin- 上带 -al（拉丁 -alis）。拉丁基础是 origo、originem，出自 oriri“升起”；英语没有另加前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is oriri 'to rise', origo/originem 'beginning, source', and originalis 'belonging to the beginning'. The abstract noun -itas is Latin, but originality as a word is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 oriri“升起”、origo/originem“开始、源头”、originalis“属于开端的”。抽象名词后缀 -itas 是拉丁的，但 originality 这个词本身是英语造出来的。

items.meaning: the quality of rising from one's own source rather than copying
items.meaningCN: 从自身源头升起而非抄袭的品质；独创性（-ity 品质名词）
items.example: The panel doubted the originality of the second chapter.
items.exampleCN: 评审小组怀疑第二章的原创性。

items.meaning: belonging to the beginning; made first, not copied
items.meaningCN: 属于开端的；最先做出而非复制的
items.example: The original manuscript has three extra pages.
items.exampleCN: 原稿多出三页。

items.meaning: the point where something begins
items.meaningCN: 事物开始的那一点；起源
items.example: The origin of the custom is unknown.
items.exampleCN: 这个习俗的起源不明。

items.meaning: to begin or to bring into being
items.meaningCN: 发源；创始（-ate 动词词尾）
items.example: The technique originated in southern China.
items.exampleCN: 这项技术发源于中国南方。

items.meaning: the act of beginning something
items.meaningCN: 创始、发源的行为（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: The origination fee is charged when the loan is made.
items.exampleCN: 贷款发放时会收取发起费。

items.meaning: present from the beginning; the first inhabitants of a land
items.meaningCN: 自始就存在的；某地的原住民（ab- 从 + origin + -al）
items.example: The park protects aboriginal rock art.
items.exampleCN: 这座公园保护原住民岩画。

items.meaning: to turn toward a direction; the east
items.meaningCN: 使朝向；东方
items.example: The nave is oriented toward the sunrise.
items.exampleCN: 中殿朝向日出方向。

items.meaning: a turning toward a point, and the bearing produced
items.meaningCN: 转向某一点的动作及其形成的方位
items.example: The antenna's orientation affects reception.
items.exampleCN: 天线的朝向会影响接收效果。

items.meaning: the doctrine of reading a text by its original intent
items.meaningCN: 按文本原初意图解读的主义（-ism 学说）
items.example: Originalism divides American constitutional scholars.
items.exampleCN: 原旨主义让美国宪法学者分成两派。

latinEntries.meaning: to rise, come up, be born

definition_zh: 参与；参加；参与人数；参与权；份额参与；员工参与；政治参与；课堂参与；费用分担
definition_en: the act of taking part in an activity, the number or degree of people taking part, the right or share gained by taking part, or a formal arrangement in which members share in decisions, costs, or profits
core_image: 一只脚踏进正在转动的圈子里，圈里的节奏因为这双脚发生了变化
scene: 社区开会讨论新公园的选址，会议室里的折叠椅都坐满了。The meeting saw participation double compared with last time.
sceneCN: 这里 participation 是「参与人数」（第 2 个义项：实际参加某项活动的人数或比例）；句意：这次会议的参与人数比上次翻了一倍。

pos.zh: 参与；参加；参与人数；参与权；份额；分担

senses.title: The act of taking part
senses.definition: the act of joining in an activity, event, or process together with others
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起加入某项活动、事件或过程的行为
senses.example: Participation in the survey was voluntary and anonymous.
senses.exampleCN: 参与这项调查是自愿且匿名的。
senses.why: Latin particeps means 'part-taker': pars 'part' plus capere 'to take'. Participation is literally taking a part for yourself in something others are already doing, one foot entering the circle.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 particeps 意为“拿取一份的人”：pars“部分”加 capere“拿取”。participation 字面上就是在一件别人已经在做的事里为自己拿一份，一只脚踏进那个圈。

senses.title: How many take part
senses.definition: the number of people who take part, or the proportion of a group that does so, often expressed as a rate
senses.definitionCN: 参加的人数，或群体中参加者的比例，通常以比率表示
senses.example: Voter participation fell below forty percent in the off-year election.
senses.exampleCN: 这次非大选年的选举中，选民参与率跌到四成以下。
senses.why: Once the act is countable, it can be measured. The circle is drawn, and the question becomes how many feet are inside it, not what each foot is doing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个行为可以被计数，它就能被测量。圈画好了，问题变成圈里有多少只脚，而不是每只脚在做什么。

senses.title: The right to have a part
senses.definition: the recognized right or opportunity of a person or group to take part in decisions that affect them
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体参与影响自身决策的被承认的权利或机会
senses.example: The treaty guarantees public participation in land-use planning.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约保障公众参与土地利用规划的权利。
senses.why: Here the emphasis moves from the fact of joining to the door being open. Participation is the standing permission to put your foot in the circle, not merely the step itself.
senses.whyCN: 这里重点从“加入的事实”转到“门是否开着”。participation 是允许你把脚踏进圈子的长期资格，而不只是那一步动作。

senses.title: A share in money or rights
senses.titleCN: 在金钱或权益中的一份
senses.definition: a share in profits, ownership, or a financial arrangement, gained by taking part in an enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 通过参与某项事业而获得的利润、所有权或财务安排中的份额
senses.example: The fund takes a participation in the port operator's revenue.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金在这家港口运营商的收入中占有一份权益。
senses.why: The 'part' inside the word becomes literal and countable: you take a part of the money, not just a part of the work. The circle now has shares marked on it.
senses.whyCN: 词里的“部分”在这里变成字面、可数的东西：你拿的是钱的一部分，而不只是工作的一部分。圈上现在标着份额。

senses.title: Workers sharing in decisions
senses.definition: a management arrangement in which employees take part in decisions, often through councils, shares, or consultation
senses.definitionCN: 一种管理安排，让员工通过委员会、持股或协商参与到决策中
senses.example: Employee participation schemes raised retention but slowed decisions.
senses.exampleCN: 员工参与方案提高了留任率，却拖慢了决策。
senses.why: Industry applies the political circle to the workplace. Those who previously only followed instructions are given a place where the rules are decided, so the word gains an institutional sense.
senses.whyCN: 工业界把政治上的圈子搬进工作场所。原先只执行指令的人获得了一个参与定规则的位置，这个词于是多了一层制度义。

senses.title: Citizens taking part in public life
senses.definition: the involvement of citizens in elections, civic organizations, protests, or public deliberation
senses.definitionCN: 公民在选举、市民组织、抗议或公共商议中的参与
senses.example: Civic participation includes voting, volunteering, and attending hearings.
senses.exampleCN: 公民参与包括投票、志愿服务和出席听证会。
senses.why: The circle is now the city. Participation measures whether people treat public decisions as theirs to make, rather than as something done to them.
senses.whyCN: 这时的圈子是城市。participation 衡量的是人们是否把公共决策当作自己该做的事，而不是别人施加给他们的事。

senses.title: Speaking up in class
senses.definition: a student's contribution to a class through questions, answers, and discussion, often part of the grade
senses.definitionCN: 学生通过提问、回答与讨论对课堂做出的贡献，常计入成绩
senses.example: Class participation counts for a fifth of the final mark.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂参与占期末成绩的五分之一。
senses.why: The smallest circle is a seminar room. Here participation is not attendance but visible contribution: the foot must not only enter, it must move.
senses.whyCN: 最小的圈子是研讨室。这里的 participation 不是到场，而是看得见的贡献：脚不仅要踏进去，还得动起来。

senses.title: Sharing a cost or loss
senses.definition: a share of a cost, loss, or obligation that a party accepts as part of an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 某一方在安排中接受承担的费用、损失或义务份额
senses.example: The insurer's participation in the loss is limited to ten percent.
senses.exampleCN: 保险人对该损失的承担份额限于百分之十。
senses.why: Taking part can mean taking part of the burden. The same pars appears, but now the part is a liability, and the circle is a contract.
senses.whyCN: 参与也可以意味着承担一部分负担。同一个 pars 又出现了，但这次这份是责任，圈子是一纸合同。

senses.title: How deeply one is involved
senses.definition: the degree of a person's engagement in an activity, ranging from passive presence to active commitment
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在活动中的投入程度，从被动在场到主动承诺
senses.example: The study distinguishes participation in name from participation in practice.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把名义上的参与和实际上的参与区分开来。
senses.why: Being inside the circle is not the same as dancing. This sense measures depth rather than count, which is why the same word can describe both a crowd and a single committed member.
senses.whyCN: 站在圈里和在圈里跳舞不是一回事。这个义项衡量的是深度而非数量，所以同一个词既能描述一大群人，也能描述一个真正投入的成员。

intro.en: Participation comes from Latin participatio, an action noun from participare 'to share, to partake', built on particeps 'sharing, partaking'. Particeps is a compound of pars 'part' and the -ceps form of capere 'to take, seize'. The literal image is 'taking a part'. English took the word in the 14th century for 'the state of sharing in something', and only later built the modern senses of civic, employee, and financial participation.
intro.cn: participation 来自拉丁语 participatio，是 participare“分享、参与”的动作名词，其基础是 particeps“分享的、参与的”。particeps 由 pars“部分”与 capere“拿取、抓取”的 -ceps 形式复合而成。字面意象是“拿取一份”。英语在 14 世纪借入这个词，指“分享某物的状态”，后来才发展出公民参与、员工参与与财务份额等现代义项。

items.en: Pars means 'part, piece, share'. Capere means 'to take, seize, capture'. Particeps, literally 'part-taking', describes someone who has a share in something, including a partner or an accomplice.
items.cn: pars 意为“部分、份额”。capere 意为“拿取、抓取、俘获”。particeps 字面是“拿取一份的”，描述在某事中占有一份的人，也可指同伴或同谋。

items.en: Participare develops from particeps with the sense 'to give a share of, to make someone a partner', then 'to have a share in, to take part'. Participatio is its action noun.
items.cn: participare 从 particeps 发展而来，先表示“分出份额、使某人成为伙伴”，再表示“在其中占一份、参与”。participatio 是它的动作名词。

items.en: English participation first means 'the fact of sharing or having a part in something', especially in theology, where the creature participates in the divine. The civic sense is later.
items.cn: 英语 participation 最早指“分享或在某事物中占有一份的事实”，尤用于神学，说受造物分有神性。公民参与义出现较晚。

items.en: Political economy and politics extend the word to voting, office-holding, and shares in profits. 'Participation in government' becomes a standard phrase of reform debates.
items.cn: 政治经济学与政治学把这个词扩展到投票、担任公职与利润份额。“参与政府”成为改革辩论中的标准说法。

items.en: Management theory coins employee participation; development agencies speak of participatory projects; education grades class participation. The abstract noun now covers nearly every circle a person can enter.
items.cn: 管理学提出员工参与；发展机构谈论参与式项目；教育把课堂参与计入成绩。这个抽象名词如今几乎覆盖人可能进入的每一个圈子。

items.en: Perception also contains capere, but its prefix is per- 'thoroughly', so it means 'seize completely' — grasp with the senses. Participation has pars 'part', not per-, so it means 'take a share'. The two words share a hand but not a purpose.
items.cn: perception 也含 capere，但前缀是 per-“彻底”，所以意为“彻底抓住”——用感官把握。participation 里是 pars“部分”，不是 per-，所以意为“拿一份”。两个词共享同一只手，目的却不同。

note.en: The first group follows the pars + capere family and marks the one neighbour that shares capere with a different prefix. The second group compares the words for joining in, being engaged, being present, and giving something.
note.cn: 第一组沿着 pars 加 capere 的词族，并标出一个共享 capere 但前缀不同的邻居。第二组比较表示“加入”“投入”“到场”“贡献”的几个词。

entries.definition: to take part in an activity. It is the verb behind participation, and it keeps the literal 'take a part' image.
entries.definitionCN: 参加某项活动。它是 participation 背后的动词，保留了“拿取一份”的字面意象。

entries.definition: a person who takes part. The ending -ant marks the person, while -ation marks the act or the share.
entries.definitionCN: 参加的人。-ant 词尾标记人，而 -ation 标记行为或份额。

entries.definition: a verb form used as an adjective or noun. It comes from Latin participium, 'a sharing', because it shares in the nature of both verb and adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 用作形容词或名词的动词形式。它出自拉丁语 participium“分享”，因为它同时兼有动词与形容词的性质。

entries.definition: the act of becoming aware through the senses. It shares capere 'take' but uses per- 'thoroughly', so it means 'seize completely', not 'take a share'.
entries.definitionCN: 通过感官觉察事物的行为。它共享 capere“拿取”，但用 per-“彻底”，所以意为“完全抓住”，而不是“拿一份”。

entries.definition: the state of being connected with or emotionally caught up in something. It stresses commitment and entanglement, while participation stresses taking a part.
entries.definitionCN: 与某事有联系或情感上被卷入的状态。它强调投入与牵连，而 participation 强调拿取一份。

entries.definition: active commitment of attention or effort, or a formal arrangement to meet. It is the depth sense of participation, often with a tone of deliberate choice.
entries.definitionCN: 注意力或努力的主动投入，也指正式的会面约定。它接近 participation 的深度义，常带“有意选择”的语气。

entries.definition: the fact of being present at an event. It counts bodies in the room and says nothing about whether they do anything.
entries.definitionCN: 出席某场活动的事实。它数的是房间里的身体，不说明这些人做了什么。

entries.definition: something given to a common pool, such as money, work, or ideas. It stresses what is put in, while participation stresses the act of joining.
entries.definitionCN: 投入公共池的东西，如钱、劳动或想法。它强调投入了什么，而 participation 强调加入的行为。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: pars 'part', capere 'take', particeps 'part-taker', the participle cousin, and the perception contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：pars“部分”、capere“拿取”、particeps“拿取一份的人”、同源的分词、以及与 perception 的对比。

normal.en: Pars is 'part' and capere is 'take': participation literally means taking a part, so the word always contains a share.
normal.cn: pars 是“部分”，capere 是“拿取”：participation 字面上就是拿取一份，所以这个词里永远装着份额。

normal.en: Particeps is the Latin noun for a sharer, and English partner comes from the same idea of someone who has a part with you.
normal.cn: particeps 是拉丁语里“分享者”的名词，英语 partner 也来自同一想法：一个与你共有一份的人。

normal.en: The grammatical participle is called a 'sharing' word because it shares in two parts of speech, which is participation inside grammar.
normal.cn: 语法里的分词被称为“分享”之词，因为它兼有两类词性，这就是语法内部的 participation。

normal.en: Perception has the same capere but the prefix per- 'thoroughly': perception grabs the whole object, participation takes only a part of it.
normal.cn: perception 有同一个 capere，但前缀是 per-“彻底”：感知抓住整个对象，参与只拿其中一份。

normal.en: The suffix chain is -ate, -ant, -ation: participate the act, participant the person, participation the state or share.
normal.cn: 后缀链是 -ate、-ant、-ation：participate 是动作，participant 是人，participation 是状态或份额。

abstract.en: A circle of dancers has a gap; one pair of feet fills it, and the pattern changes for everyone inside.
abstract.cn: 一圈跳舞的人留着一个缺口；一双脚填进去，圈里每个人的图案都随之改变。

abstract.en: Attendance counts chairs; participation counts what the chairs are doing.
abstract.cn: 到场数的是椅子；参与数的是椅子上的动作。

abstract.en: A shareholder owns a piece of paper that says 'a part'; a citizen owns a voice that says 'my part'.
abstract.cn: 股东持有一张写着“一份”的纸；公民拥有一个说着“我这一份”的声音。

examples.en: Public participation slowed the project but improved its design.
examples.cn: 公众参与拖慢了项目，却改进了设计。

examples.en: The participation rate among first-time voters rose sharply.
examples.cn: 首次投票者的参与率大幅上升。

examples.en: She holds a small participation in the family business.
examples.cn: 她在这家家族企业里持有少量股份。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕提西佩申」——帕提把一只脚“踏”进圈里，顺手拿走了其中的一份 → participation 参与；份额（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 participare「分享、参与」，出自 particeps「拿取一份的人」，由 pars「部分」+ capere「拿取」的 -ceps 形式复合；后缀 -ation 为动作名词词尾。核心是「在一件别人已经在做的事里拿取属于自己的一份」。同族含 participate、participant、participle；perception 共享 capere 但前缀为 per-，词根组合不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of participation all begin with one foot entering a circle and taking a part. What changes is what is being shared — the activity, the count, the right, the money, the decisions, the cost, or the depth of commitment.
sensesIntro.cn: participation 的九个义项都从一只脚踏进圈子、拿走一份开始。变化的是被分享的东西——活动本身、人数、权利、金钱、决策、成本，还是投入的深度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one foot entering a circle already in motion, taking a part and changing the pattern.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚踏进已经在转动的圈子，拿走一份，并改变整体图案。

chain: THE SHARE CAN BE MONEY OR BURDEN

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS DEPTH: joining in, and how far a person actually commits once inside.
branches.cn: 行为与深度：加入其中，以及进入之后真正投入多深。

branches.en: THE COUNT: a participation rate in an election or a grade for speaking in class.
branches.cn: 计数：选举中的参与率，或课堂发言的成绩。

branches.en: THE OPEN DOOR: the right of citizens or groups to take part in decisions that affect them.
branches.cn: 敞开的门：公民或群体参与影响自身决策的权利。

branches.en: THE SHARE: a portion of profit or ownership, and a portion of cost or loss.
branches.cn: 那一份：利润或所有权的份额，以及费用或损失的份额。

branches.en: THE WORKPLACE CIRCLE: employees given a place at the table where rules are decided.
branches.cn: 工作场所的圈子：员工在决定规则的那张桌旁获得一个位置。

intro.en: Participation is participation-, the stem of Latin participatio, plus English -ion from Latin -io/-ionem. The Latin compound is pars 'part' + -ceps (from capere 'take'). The family grows by changing the suffix: -ate verb, -ant person, -ation action, -atory adjective.
intro.cn: participation 是拉丁 participatio 的词干 participat- 加英语 -ion（拉丁 -io/-ionem）。拉丁复合词是 pars“部分”+ -ceps（出自 capere“拿取”）。词族通过换后缀生长：-ate 动词、-ant 人、-ation 动作、-atory 形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is pars 'part', capere 'take', particeps 'part-taker', participare 'to share', and participatio 'a sharing'. The same capere, with different prefixes, gives perception, reception, and capture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 pars“部分”、capere“拿取”、particeps“拿取一份的人”、participare“分享”、participatio“分享”。同一个 capere 配上不同前缀，还产生表示“感知”“接收”与“捕获”的词。

items.meaning: the act or state of taking a part
items.meaningCN: 拿取一份的行为或状态；参与（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Participation in the trial is open to all residents.
items.exampleCN: 所有居民都可以参与这项试验。

items.meaning: to take a part in something
items.meaningCN: 在某事中拿取一份；参加（pars 部分 + capere 拿取 + -ate）
items.example: Ten schools participated in the study.
items.exampleCN: 十所学校参与了这项研究。

items.meaning: one who takes part
items.meaningCN: 参加者（-ant 表人）
items.example: Each participant received a numbered card.
items.exampleCN: 每位参与者都领到一张编号卡。

items.meaning: organized so that people take part
items.meaningCN: 被安排成让人参与的（-ory 功能形容词）
items.example: The council runs a participatory budget.
items.exampleCN: 该委员会实行参与式预算。

items.meaning: marked by shared decision-making
items.meaningCN: 以共同决策为特征的（-ive 倾向形容词）
items.example: Participative management suits small teams.
items.exampleCN: 参与式管理适合小团队。

items.meaning: a verb form that shares in two parts of speech
items.meaningCN: 兼有两类词性的动词形式；分词
items.example: A participle borrows its ending from a verb and its job from an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 分词借用动词的词尾，又承担形容词的职能。

items.structure: Old French parçonier, from Latin partitionem 'a dividing'
items.meaning: one who shares an activity or a business with another
items.meaningCN: 与他人共同从事活动或经营的人；伙伴
items.example: She became a partner in the firm last year.
items.exampleCN: 她去年成了这家公司的合伙人。

items.meaning: a piece of a whole, or a share in something
items.meaningCN: 整体中的一块，或某物中的一份
items.example: Each student reads a different part.
items.exampleCN: 每个学生读不同的部分。

items.meaning: a taking in through the senses
items.meaningCN: 通过感官彻底拿取；知觉（per- 彻底 + capere 拿取）
items.example: Color perception varies between individuals.
items.exampleCN: 颜色知觉因人而异。

latinEntries.meaning: to give a share of, to take part in

definition_zh: 参与式的；让人参与的；参与性民主的；参与式管理的；参与式研究的；参与式艺术的；参与式预算的；参与式体育的；参与式文化的
definition_en: organized so that members of a group take part in decisions, activities, or creation, rather than receiving them from above or watching them from outside
core_image: 圈子的门敞开着，里面的人都能伸手去改正在用的规则
scene: 社区花园不请设计师画定稿，而是让每户居民投票决定哪块地种什么。Every household votes on what to plant, so the planning is participatory.
sceneCN: 这里 participatory 是「参与式的」（第 1 个义项：决策由成员共同做出，而非由上方定好）；句意：每户居民投票决定种什么，所以这种规划是参与式的。

pos.zh: 参与式的；让人参与的；共同参与的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 参与性的（更强调共同决策特征）

senses.title: Decisions made with the members
senses.titleCN: 由成员共同作出决定的
senses.definition: describing a process in which the people affected take part in making the decision rather than receiving it from above
senses.definitionCN: 指受影响的人参与作出决定、而不是从上方接受决定的流程
senses.example: The housing council adopted a participatory model for allocating flats.
senses.exampleCN: 住房委员会采用参与式模式分配住房。
senses.why: The suffix -ory means 'serving to' or 'having the function of'. Participatory marks a system whose function is to let feet enter the circle and move the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ory 意为“起……作用的”。participatory 标记的是一种制度，它的功能就是让脚踏进圈子并改变图案。

senses.title: Open to anyone affected
senses.definition: open in structure, so that outsiders and ordinary members can join, speak, and influence the outcome
senses.definitionCN: 结构上是开放的，外人与普通成员都能加入、发言并影响结果
senses.example: The planning meeting was unusually participatory for a city office.
senses.exampleCN: 对市政部门而言，这次规划会议开放得不同寻常。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes the door, not the decision. A participatory forum is one whose walls are low enough that a passer-by can lean in.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词描述的是门，而不是决定。参与式论坛的墙足够低，路过的人也能探身进来。

senses.title: Of participatory democracy
senses.definition: relating to a model of democracy in which citizens take part directly in decisions, not only in periodic elections
senses.definitionCN: 指公民直接参与决策、而不只在定期选举中投票的民主模式
senses.example: Participatory democracy requires time that representative systems do not.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式民主需要代议制所不需要的时间。
senses.why: The circle is the polity. Where representative democracy asks citizens to choose who decides, this model asks them to sit in the circle themselves, so the word becomes a political label.
senses.whyCN: 这时的圈子是政治共同体。代议制民主请公民选择由谁决定，这种模式则请公民自己坐进圈里，于是这个词成了一个政治标签。

senses.title: Of shared management
senses.definition: relating to management in which employees help set goals, solve problems, and shape working rules
senses.definitionCN: 指员工参与设定目标、解决问题并制定工作规则的管理方式
senses.example: Participatory management failed here because no one owned the final call.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式管理在这里失败了，因为没有人对最终决定负责。
senses.why: A factory floor is also a circle. The adjective turns the org chart sideways: the boxes at the bottom are given lines back up into the decision.
senses.whyCN: 车间也是一个圈子。这个形容词把架构图横过来：底部的方框获得了指回决策的连线。

senses.title: Of research done with participants
senses.titleCN: 与参与者共同做的研究
senses.definition: relating to research in which the people studied help design the questions, collect data, and interpret results
senses.definitionCN: 指被研究者参与设计问题、收集数据与解释结果的研究方式
senses.example: Participatory research gave the village a say in what counted as success.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式研究让村民对“什么算成功”有了发言权。
senses.why: Researchers once stood outside the circle and measured it. This sense puts them inside, so the people being studied become co-authors of the finding.
senses.whyCN: 研究者从前站在圈外测量圈子。这个义项把他们放进圈内，于是被研究的人成了研究结论的共同作者。

senses.title: Of art that needs the audience
senses.definition: relating to art whose meaning or existence depends on the audience doing something, not only looking
senses.definitionCN: 指意义或存在依赖观众动手做事、而不只是观看的艺术
senses.example: The participatory installation asked visitors to write on the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这件参与式装置请参观者在墙上写字。
senses.why: A painting can be finished by the artist. A participatory work is unfinished until a foot enters the circle, which makes the viewer a material of the piece.
senses.whyCN: 一幅画可以由艺术家完成。参与式作品在有人踏进圈子之前都未完成，这使观众成了作品的材料。

senses.title: Of budgeting by residents
senses.definition: relating to a budget process in which residents decide how part of a public budget is spent
senses.definitionCN: 指由居民决定部分公共预算如何使用的预算流程
senses.example: Participatory budgeting moved the playground repair to the top of the list.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式预算把操场维修提到了清单最前面。
senses.why: Money is the clearest test of the open door. If residents can move a real sum, the participation is not a consultation but a hand on the lever.
senses.whyCN: 钱是检验门是否敞开的最清楚方式。如果居民能挪动一笔真实的款项，参与就不是征询意见，而是手真的握上了操纵杆。

senses.title: Of sport played, not watched
senses.titleCN: 亲自参与而非观看的体育
senses.definition: relating to sport that people play themselves, as opposed to professional sport watched by spectators
senses.definitionCN: 指人们亲自从事的体育运动，相对于观众观看的职业赛事
senses.example: Funding shifted from stadiums to participatory sport in schools.
senses.exampleCN: 资金从体育场转向了学校的参与性体育。
senses.why: Here the contrast is between feet in the circle and eyes outside it. The word classifies an activity by who is doing it, not by how organized it is.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对比是圈里的脚与圈外的眼。这个词按“谁在做”来分类活动，而不是按组织程度。

senses.title: Of a culture that remakes its content
senses.titleCN: 会改写自身内容的文化
senses.definition: relating to a culture in which fans and users produce, remix, and circulate content rather than only consuming it
senses.definitionCN: 指粉丝与用户生产、混编并传播内容、而不只是消费内容的文化
senses.example: Fan translation is a participatory culture in its purest form.
senses.exampleCN: 粉丝翻译是参与式文化最纯粹的形式。
senses.why: The suffix now attaches to culture itself. When readers become writers, the circle stops having a clear outside, and the adjective marks that blurred boundary.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀现在挂到了文化本身上。当读者变成作者，圈子不再有清楚的外面，这个形容词标记的正是那条模糊的边界。

intro.en: Participatory is the adjective of participate, formed with -ory from Latin -orius, a suffix meaning 'serving for, having the function of'. The base is Latin participare, from particeps 'part-taking', itself pars 'part' plus capere 'take'. English built the adjective in the 19th century; it first described political arrangements and later spread to management, research, art, and digital culture.
intro.cn: participatory 是 participate 的形容词，由 -ory（拉丁 -orius，意为“用于……的、具有……功能的”）构成。基础是拉丁语 participare，出自 particeps“拿取一份的”，而 particeps 又是 pars“部分”加 capere“拿取”。英语在 19 世纪造出这个形容词，最初描述政治安排，后来扩展到管理、研究、艺术与数字文化。

items.en: The suffix -orius in Latin forms adjectives of function, as in amatorius 'serving for love' and obligatorius 'binding'. English -ory keeps that sense of 'designed to do this'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 -orius 构成表功能的形容词，如 amatorius“用于爱的”、obligatorius“有约束力的”。英语 -ory 保留了“被设计来做这件事”的含义。

items.en: The adjective appears in English in the 19th century, mainly in political writing about schemes in which citizens share in government.
items.cn: 这个形容词在 19 世纪进入英语，主要用于讨论公民共同参与治理的政治写作。

items.en: Management theory, development practice, and adult education all adopt it: participatory management, participatory research, participatory rural appraisal.
items.cn: 管理学、发展实践与成人教育都采用了它：参与式管理、参与式研究、参与式农村评估。

items.en: Participatory democracy becomes a slogan of student and civic movements, fixing the word as a positive political label.
items.cn: 20 世纪 60 至 70 年代，参与式民主成为学生运动与公民运动的口号，使这个词固定为一个正面的政治标签。

items.en: Media studies apply it to fan production and online platforms: participatory culture, participatory media. The suffix now marks a blurring line between producer and audience.
items.cn: 20 世纪 90 年代至 2000 年代，媒介研究把它用于粉丝生产与网络平台：参与式文化、参与式媒介。这个后缀此时标记的是生产者与受众之间正在模糊的界线。

items.en: The -ory here is not the -ory of 'laboratory' (a place) or the -ory of 'sensory' (belonging to). It is the function suffix: a participatory system is one whose function is participation.
items.cn: 这里的 -ory 不是 laboratory（地点）的 -ory，也不是 sensory（属于）的 -ory，而是表功能的后缀：参与式制度的功用就是“参与”。

note.en: The first group follows the particip- family and marks the near neighbour that only shares the suffix. The second group compares adjectives for things opened to members, to the public, to collaborators, or to users.
note.cn: 第一组沿着 particip- 词族，并标出一个只是共享后缀的近邻。第二组比较表示“对成员开放”“对公众开放”“协作的”“动手的”几个形容词。

entries.definition: to take part in something. The adjective participatory adds -ory to describe a system built to make this happen.
entries.definitionCN: 参加某事。形容词 participatory 加 -ory，用来描述一个被设计成让这种事发生的体系。

entries.definition: the act or share of taking part. It names what happens, while participatory names the design that invites it.
entries.definitionCN: 参与的行为或份额。它命名发生的事，而 participatory 命名邀请这件事发生的设计。

entries.definition: a person who takes part. It is a countable role, whereas participatory is a property of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 参与的人。它是可数的角色，而 participatory 是流程的属性。

entries.definition: relating to a participle. It looks close to participatory but belongs to grammar, not to decision-making.
entries.definitionCN: 与分词有关的。它看起来接近 participatory，却属于语法领域，与决策无关。

entries.definition: deliberately taking in all groups, especially those usually excluded. It stresses who is admitted, while participatory stresses what they do once admitted.
entries.definitionCN: 有意把一切群体纳入，尤其是不常被纳入的群体。它强调谁被接纳，而 participatory 强调被接纳后他们做了什么。

entries.definition: based on the principle that power belongs to the people, usually through voting. It is the wider constitutional idea; participatory names one method of realizing it.
entries.definitionCN: 基于权力属于人民的原则，通常通过投票实现。它是更宽的宪制理念，participatory 是实现它的一种方法。

entries.definition: involving two or more parties working jointly on a task. It stresses joint labour, while participatory stresses shared authority over decisions.
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同完成一项任务。它强调共同劳动，而 participatory 强调决策权的共享。

entries.definition: involving direct practical activity. It describes the mode of work, not the distribution of decision-making power.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及直接的实践活动。它描述工作方式，而不描述决策权的分配。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: -ory as a function suffix, participare, particeps, the 19th-century political origin, and the four -ory words that are not this -ory.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：-ory 作功能后缀、participare、particeps、19 世纪的政治来源，以及四个不属于这个 -ory 的词。

normal.en: -ory means 'serving to': a participatory system is a system whose job is to let people take part.
normal.cn: -ory 意为“用于……”：参与式体系就是一个以让人参与为职责的体系。

normal.en: The base is particeps, 'part-taker': participatory design gives every member a part to take.
normal.cn: 基础是 particeps“拿取一份的人”：参与式设计给每个成员一份可以拿的东西。

normal.en: The word rose in 19th-century political writing about citizens sharing in government, then moved into offices, clinics, and studios.
normal.cn: 这个词兴起于 19 世纪关于公民共同治理的政治写作，之后进入办公室、诊所与工作室。

normal.en: Do not confuse -ory here with the -ory of laboratory (a place) or sensory (belonging to): this one says 'designed for'.
normal.cn: 不要把这里的 -ory 与 laboratory（地点）或 sensory（属于）的 -ory 混同：这里是“为……而设计”。

normal.en: Participatory democracy, management, research, art, and culture are five arenas where the same open door is installed.
normal.cn: 参与式民主、管理、研究、艺术与文化，是同一扇敞开的门被装进去的五个场所。

abstract.en: A door that is open is not the same as a room that is shared; the adjective names the hinge, not the furniture.
abstract.cn: 门开着不等于房间被共享；这个形容词命名的是合页，而不是家具。

abstract.en: A rule written by everyone is slower to finish and harder to overturn.
abstract.cn: 由所有人写成的规则完成得更慢，也更难被推翻。

abstract.en: When the audience holds the brush, the painting no longer has an outside.
abstract.cn: 当观众握住画笔，这幅画就不再有一个“外面”。

examples.en: The school adopted a participatory approach to curriculum design.
examples.cn: 学校在课程设计上采用了参与式方法。

examples.en: Participatory budgeting gave residents control over a fifth of the budget.
examples.cn: 参与式预算让居民掌控了五分之一的预算。

examples.en: The exhibition is participatory: visitors build part of the work.
examples.cn: 这场展览是参与式的：参观者会搭建作品的一部分。
