dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕提西破特瑞」——帕提把门推开，让圈里每个人都“破”例伸手改规则 → participatory 参与式的；让人参与的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 participare「分享、参与」，出自 particeps「拿取一份的人」（pars「部分」+ capere「拿取」）；后缀 -ory（拉丁 -orius）表功能，意为“用于……的”。核心是「把圈子的门敞开，让成员的手伸进规则里」。同族含 participate、participation、participant；perception 共享 capere 但前缀不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of participatory all describe an open door in a circle. What changes is the circle — a council, a workplace, a research team, a gallery, a budget, a playing field, or a fandom — and whether the adjective describes the decision, the openness, or the culture.
sensesIntro.cn: participatory 的九个义项都描述圈子上的一扇敞开的门。变化的是圈子本身——议事会、工作场所、研究团队、美术馆、预算、球场或粉丝社群——以及形容词描述的是决定、开放程度，还是文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle whose door is open, so that members can reach in and change the rules while they are being used.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个门敞开的圈子，成员可以在规则还在使用时伸手进去修改。

chain: THE DESIGN IS NAMED FOR THIS

branches.en: THE OPEN PROCESS: decisions made with members, and a structure open to anyone affected.
branches.cn: 开放的流程：与成员共同作出决定，以及向所有受影响者开放的结构。

branches.en: GOVERNANCE AND WORK: participatory democracy in the polity, participatory management at the workplace.
branches.cn: 治理与工作：政治共同体中的参与式民主，工作场所中的参与式管理。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: research in which the studied help design the questions and read the results.
branches.cn: 知识：由被研究者参与设计问题与解读结果的研究。

branches.en: CULTURE AND MONEY: art that needs the audience to act, and budgets that residents can move.
branches.cn: 文化与金钱：需要观众行动的艺术，以及居民可以挪动的预算。

branches.en: PLAY AND PRODUCTION: sport played rather than watched, and a culture that remakes its own content.
branches.cn: 游戏与生产：亲自从事而非观看的体育，以及会改写自身内容的文化。

intro.en: Participatory is participate plus -ory, from Latin -orius. The stem is participat-, from participare, which rests on particeps (pars 'part' + capere 'take'). The adjective is a 19th-century English formation; the Latin language had no participatory.
intro.cn: participatory 是 participate 加 -ory（拉丁 -orius）。词干是 participat-，出自 participare，其基础为 particeps（pars“部分”+ capere“拿取”）。这个形容词是 19 世纪英语的构词，拉丁语本身并没有 participatory。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is pars 'part', capere 'take', particeps 'part-taker', participare 'to share'. Latin -orius formed adjectives of function, the source of English -ory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 pars“部分”、capere“拿取”、particeps“拿取一份的人”、participare“分享”。拉丁 -orius 构成表功能的形容词，是英语 -ory 的来源。

items.meaning: designed so that people take part
items.meaningCN: 被设计成让人参与的（-ory 功能形容词）
items.example: The workshop used a participatory method.
items.exampleCN: 工作坊采用了参与式方法。

items.meaning: to take a part
items.meaningCN: 拿取一份；参加（pars + capere + -ate）
items.example: All residents may participate.
items.exampleCN: 所有居民都可以参与。

items.meaning: the act or share of taking part
items.meaningCN: 参与的行为或份额（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Participation was higher than expected.
items.exampleCN: 参与程度高于预期。

items.meaning: one who takes part
items.meaningCN: 参与者（-ant 表人）
items.example: Every participant signed the form.
items.exampleCN: 每位参与者都签了表。

items.meaning: marked by shared decision-making
items.meaningCN: 以共同决策为特征的（-ive 倾向形容词）
items.example: The team prefers a participative style.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队偏好参与性的风格。

items.meaning: a person who takes part
items.meaningCN: 参加者（-or 施动者）
items.example: He was a silent participator in the debate.
items.exampleCN: 他是这场辩论中沉默的参加者。

items.meaning: a piece of a whole, or a share
items.meaningCN: 整体的一块，或一份
items.example: Each part has its own label.
items.exampleCN: 每一部分都有自己的标签。

items.structure: Old French parçonier, from Latin partitionem
items.meaning: one who shares an activity or business
items.meaningCN: 共同从事活动或经营的人；伙伴
items.example: The two firms became partners in 2010.
items.exampleCN: 这两家公司在 2010 年成为合作伙伴。

items.meaning: a taking in through the senses
items.meaningCN: 通过感官拿取；知觉
items.example: Depth perception develops early in infancy.
items.exampleCN: 深度知觉在婴儿期很早就发展起来。

latinEntries.meaning: serving for, having the function of

definition_zh: 知觉；感知；看法；观念；洞察力；感知能力；印象；公众认知；机器感知
definition_en: the act or result of becoming aware of something through the senses or the mind, the view a person or public holds, keen insight, or the process by which a system interprets input
core_image: 眼睛和耳朵把外面的世界收进一张内部地图，再给上面的每样东西写上名字
scene: 同一场雨，有人只听见噪音，有人听出雨势在变小。Two people hear the same rain differently, and the difference lies in perception.
sceneCN: 这里 perception 是「感知能力」（第 4 个义项：感官对细微差别作出分辨的能力）；句意：两个人听同一场雨听到的不一样，差别就在感知能力。

pos.zh: 知觉；感知；看法；观念；洞察力；印象

derivatives.zh: 有洞察力的；感知敏锐的

senses.title: Awareness through the senses
senses.definition: the act or result of becoming aware of objects and events through sight, hearing, touch, taste, or smell
senses.definitionCN: 通过视觉、听觉、触觉、味觉或嗅觉觉察物体与事件的行为或结果
senses.example: Perception of the low hum came before any conscious thought.
senses.exampleCN: 对那阵低鸣的知觉出现在任何有意识的想法之前。
senses.why: Percipere is per- 'thoroughly' plus capere 'to take': the senses take the world in and hold it. Perception is that grasping, the moment the outer world becomes an inner object.
senses.whyCN: percipere 是 per-“彻底”加 capere“拿取”：感官把世界拿进来并握住。perception 就是这一抓，是外部世界变成内部对象的那一刻。

senses.title: The grasp the mind forms
senses.definition: the mental understanding or interpretation a person forms about a situation, often beyond bare sensory data
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对某种情况形成的理解或解释，常超出纯粹的感官材料
senses.example: Her perception of the risk was sharper than the numbers suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 她对风险的判断比数字显示的更敏锐。
senses.why: The hand that takes can also sort and name. Once the inner map is drawn, perception means not only seeing the shape but understanding what it is.
senses.whyCN: 拿取的那只手也会分类和命名。内部地图画好之后，perception 不仅指看见形状，还指明白它是什么。

senses.title: The view people hold
senses.definition: the opinion, image, or belief that a person or the public holds about someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 某个人或公众对某人某事持有的看法、形象或信念
senses.example: Public perception of the agency improved after the open day.
senses.exampleCN: 开放日之后，公众对该机构的看法有所改善。
senses.why: Many inner maps can agree. When they do, perception becomes a social fact: not what is out there, but what a group has taken in and agreed to see.
senses.whyCN: 许多内部地图可以彼此一致。一旦一致，perception 就成了社会事实：不是外面有什么，而是一个群体拿进来并同意看见什么。

senses.title: Keenness of sensing
senses.definition: the acuity or fineness of a person's or animal's senses in detecting small differences
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物的感官在察觉细微差别时的敏锐程度
senses.example: A dog's perception of scent far exceeds a human's.
senses.exampleCN: 狗对气味的感知能力远远超过人。
senses.why: The same hand can be strong or weak. This sense speaks of the instrument rather than the object: a fine net takes more of the sea than a coarse one.
senses.whyCN: 同一只手可以有力或无力。这个义项说的是工具本身而不是对象：细网比粗网能从海里捞起更多东西。

senses.title: Insight into what is hidden
senses.definition: the ability to notice and understand things that are not obvious to others, especially motives or patterns
senses.definitionCN: 察觉并理解他人不易看到之事的能力，尤指动机或规律
senses.example: With unusual perception, she named the fear behind his joke.
senses.exampleCN: 她以不寻常的洞察力，说出了他玩笑背后的恐惧。
senses.why: Perception can go through the surface to the structure beneath it. The eye does not just receive; it reads the map for what the map is hiding.
senses.whyCN: 感知可以穿过表层看到下面的结构。眼睛不只是接收，它还读地图，读出地图藏起来的东西。

senses.title: The field that studies sensing
senses.definition: the branch of psychology and neuroscience that studies how organisms organize and interpret sensory information
senses.definitionCN: 心理学与神经科学中研究生物如何组织并解释感官信息的分支
senses.example: The paper reviews fifty years of research on visual perception.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文回顾了视觉知觉五十年的研究。
senses.why: When the act becomes a subject, perception turns into a field with methods and experiments. The word no longer names one grasping but the laws of grasping in general.
senses.whyCN: 当这个行为成为研究对象时，perception 变成一门有方法与实验的学科。这个词不再命名某一次抓取，而是抓取的一般规律。

senses.title: What is sensed versus what is real
senses.titleCN: 所感与所实之间的距离
senses.definition: in philosophy, the relation between sensory appearance and the object or reality that is believed to cause it
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中感官显现与被认为是其成因的对象或实在之间的关系
senses.example: The argument turns on whether perception gives us the object itself.
senses.exampleCN: 这一论证的关键在于：知觉是否把对象本身给了我们。
senses.why: The inner map may not match the land. Philosophy uses perception for the whole problem of whether the copy in the mind is faithful to what lies outside it.
senses.whyCN: 内部地图未必与真实地形相符。哲学用 perception 指整个问题：心里的副本是否忠实地对应外面的东西。

senses.title: The impression others receive
senses.definition: the impression a person or organization creates in others, especially through appearance, tone, and manner
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或组织在他人心中造成的印象，尤指通过外表、语气与举止
senses.example: His calm voice shaped the jury's perception of him as honest.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静的声音让陪审团觉得他是个诚实的人。
senses.why: Here the map is drawn in another person's head. Perception is the image you did not write but caused, and it can diverge sharply from what you intended.
senses.whyCN: 这里的地图画在别人的头脑里。perception 是你没有亲手写、却由你造成的形象，它可以与你原本的意图相差很远。

senses.title: A machine interpreting input
senses.definition: the process by which a computer system detects, classifies, and interprets signals from cameras, microphones, or other sensors
senses.definitionCN: 计算机系统检测、分类并解释来自摄像头、麦克风或其他传感器的信号的过程
senses.example: Machine perception lets the car read the road markings.
senses.exampleCN: 机器感知让汽车能读懂路面标线。
senses.why: Engineers build the same loop with silicon: a sensor takes in, a model names. The word keeps its shape even when the eye is a camera and the mind is an algorithm.
senses.whyCN: 工程师用硅片搭出同样的回路：传感器拿进来，模型来命名。即使眼睛变成摄像头、头脑变成算法，这个词的形状也没有变。

intro.en: Perception comes from Latin perceptio, an action noun from percipere 'to take in, grasp, perceive'. Percipere is per- 'thoroughly' plus capere 'to take, seize'. English borrowed perception in the 14th century first for the taking in of knowledge or the receiving of impressions, and the modern sensory sense settled in the 19th century with the rise of experimental psychology.
intro.cn: perception 来自拉丁语 perceptio，是 percipere“拿进来、把握、感知”的动作名词。percipere 由 per-“彻底”加 capere“拿取、抓取”构成。英语在 14 世纪借入 perception，最初指“接受知识或接收印象”，现代感官义则在 19 世纪随着实验心理学兴起而定型。

items.en: Capere means 'to take, seize, capture'. With per- 'through, thoroughly', percipere means 'to take hold of completely', and by extension 'to grasp with the mind'.
items.cn: capere 意为“拿取、抓取、俘获”。加上 per-“穿过、彻底”，percipere 意为“完全抓住”，引申为“用头脑把握”。

items.en: Perceptio in Latin covers receiving, collecting, and comprehension. The word already lives on the border between the senses and the mind.
items.cn: 拉丁语 perceptio 同时涵盖接收、收集与理解。这个词从一开始就住在感官与心智的边界上。

items.en: English perception first means the receiving of impressions or the act of understanding, especially in religious and legal prose.
items.cn: 英语 perception 最早指接收印象或理解的行为，尤见于宗教与法律文字。

items.en: Philosophy makes perception a central term in the debate over what the mind directly knows: ideas, impressions, or external objects.
items.cn: 哲学使 perception 成为争论的核心术语，争论的问题是心智直接知道什么：观念、印象，还是外部对象。

items.en: Experimental psychology separates sensation from perception: sensation is raw input, perception is the organized interpretation of it.
items.cn: 实验心理学把感觉与知觉分开：感觉是原始输入，知觉是对它的有组织解释。

items.en: The word extends to social perception in politics and to machine perception in computing, keeping the same loop of taking in and naming.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到政治中的社会认知与计算中的机器感知，保留着同一个“拿进来再命名”的回路。

note.en: The first group separates the percept family from two words that look close but have different roots. The second group compares sensation, cognition, view, and insight, the four words most often put in perception's place.
note.cn: 第一组把 percept 词族与两个形近但词根不同的词分开。第二组比较感觉、认知、看法与洞察力，这四个词最常被用来替代 perception。

entries.definition: the object or content of a perception, the thing as sensed rather than as thought. Perception names the act, percept names what is taken in.
entries.definitionCN: 知觉的对象或内容，即被感觉到而非被思考的东西。perception 命名行为，percept 命名被拿进来的东西。

entries.definition: quick to notice and understand things. It describes a person's ability, while perception can name the act, the view, or the field of study.
entries.definitionCN: 善于察觉与理解的。它描述人的能力，而 perception 可以命名行为、看法或学科。

entries.definition: a point of view or the art of drawing depth. Its root is specere 'to look', not capere 'to take', so it names where you look from, not what you take in.
entries.definitionCN: 观点，或描绘深度的技法。它的词根是 specere“看”，不是 capere“拿取”，所以它命名的是你从哪里看，而不是你拿进了什么。

entries.definition: a rate per hundred. Its per- is the same, but the root is centum 'hundred', so it has nothing to do with taking or sensing.
entries.definitionCN: 以百为基数的比率。它的 per- 相同，但词根是 centum“一百”，与拿取或感知毫无关系。

entries.definition: a feeling or impression produced by stimulation of a sense organ. It is the raw input that perception organizes and interprets.
entries.definitionCN: 感觉器官受刺激产生的感受或印象。它是知觉加以组织与解释的原始输入。

entries.definition: the mental processes of knowing, remembering, and reasoning. It is the wider mental side, of which perception is the entry stage.
entries.definitionCN: 知道、记忆与推理的心理过程。它是更宽的心智面，而知觉是其中的入口阶段。

entries.definition: an opinion held and usually expressed. It is the social sense of perception made explicit and arguable.
entries.definitionCN: 持有并通常会表达的意见。它是 perception 社会义的外显、可争论版本。

entries.definition: a deep and accurate understanding of something hidden or complex. It is the sharpest end of perception, where the map reveals its own structure.
entries.definitionCN: 对隐藏或复杂事物的深刻而准确的理解。它是感知最锐利的一端，此时地图显露出自身的结构。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: per- 'thoroughly', capere 'take', perceptio, the sensation/perception split in 19th-century psychology, and the specere/centum traps.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：per-“彻底”、capere“拿取”、perceptio、19 世纪心理学对感觉与知觉的划分，以及 specere 与 centum 两个陷阱。

normal.en: Per- is 'thoroughly' and capere is 'take': perception is the senses taking the world in completely enough to hold it.
normal.cn: per- 是“彻底”，capere 是“拿取”：perception 就是感官把世界拿进来，拿得足够完整以便握住。

normal.en: Cavere and capture share the same capere family; perception is capture without a fight, the world seized by the eye.
normal.cn: cavere 与 capture 同属 capere 词族；perception 是一场没有搏斗的俘获，世界被眼睛抓走。

normal.en: The percept is what is taken in; the perception is the taking; perceptive is the person who takes quickly.
normal.cn: percept 是被拿进来的东西；perception 是拿的行为；perceptive 是拿得快的人。

normal.en: Perspective looks from a place, perception takes something in: the first is about the eye's position, the second about the mind's grasp.
normal.cn: perspective 从某处看出去，perception 把东西拿进来：前者关于眼睛的位置，后者关于头脑的把握。

normal.en: Percentage shares the per- but not the root: centum is 'hundred', so a percentage is a count, not a grasp.
normal.cn: percentage 共享 per- 却不共享词根：centum 是“一百”，所以百分比是计数，不是把握。

abstract.en: The eye is a net; the world is a sea. What you call reality is the catch you happened to bring up.
abstract.cn: 眼睛是一张网，世界是一片海。你称为现实的东西，只是你碰巧捞上来的那一网。

abstract.en: Two people stand in the same rain; one hears noise, one hears the storm weakening. The rain did not change.
abstract.cn: 两个人站在同一场雨里；一个听见噪音，一个听见暴风雨在减弱。雨并没有变。

abstract.en: A public image is a map drawn by strangers, and you cannot revise it with a pen you do not hold.
abstract.cn: 公众形象是陌生人画的地图，你手里没有那支笔，就改不动它。

examples.en: Depth perception depends on having two eyes that work together.
examples.cn: 深度知觉依赖于两只眼睛协同工作。

examples.en: The campaign tried to change public perception of the tax.
examples.cn: 这场宣传活动试图改变公众对这项税收的看法。

examples.en: Her perception of the room's mood was immediate and accurate.
examples.cn: 她对房间气氛的感知既迅速又准确。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破塞普申」——眼睛像一只手“破”开外面的世界，把看到的东西“塞”进脑子里 → perception 知觉；看法；洞察力（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 percipere「拿进来、把握、感知」，由 per-「彻底」+ capere「拿取」构成，动作名词为 perceptio。核心是「感官把外面的世界彻底拿进来，在内里画成一张地图」。同族含 perceive、percept、perceptive、perceptual、perceptible；perspective（specere「看」）与 percentage（centum「一百」）只是形近，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of perception all describe a hand taking the world in and drawing a map inside. What changes is what is taken (sensory data, meaning, public opinion), how sharp the hand is, or whether we are naming the act, the field, or the machine that now does the taking.
sensesIntro.cn: perception 的九个义项都描述一只手把世界拿进来、在内里画成地图。变化的是拿进来的东西（感官材料、意义、公众意见）、这只手有多敏锐，以及我们命名的是行为、学科，还是如今承担这件事的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes and ears take the outer world in and draw an inner map with names written on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛和耳朵把外面的世界收进一张内部地图，并在上面写下名字。

branches.en: TAKING IN: sensory awareness and the acuity of the instrument that does the taking.
branches.cn: 拿进来：感官觉察，以及执行拿取的那件仪器的敏锐度。

branches.en: READING THE MAP: mental understanding of a situation, and insight into what the map hides.
branches.cn: 读地图：对情境的心智理解，以及看穿地图所藏之物的洞察力。

branches.en: SHARED MAPS: the view a public holds, and the impression one person creates in another's head.
branches.cn: 共享的地图：公众持有的看法，以及一个人在他人头脑中造成的印象。

branches.en: THE STUDY OF THE MAP: experimental psychology of perception, and the philosophical question of whether the map matches the land.
branches.cn: 对地图的研究：实验心理学中的知觉研究，以及地图是否与真实地形相符的哲学问题。

branches.en: THE SILICON EYE: a machine takes in signals and names what it finds.
branches.cn: 硅做的眼睛：机器接收信号并命名它所发现的东西。

intro.en: Perception is percept- plus -ion (Latin -ionem). Percept- comes from Latin percipere, per- 'thoroughly' + capere 'take'. The family splits neatly: -ion the act, -ive the person, -ual the property, -ible the possibility, and percept the object.
intro.cn: perception 是 percept- 加 -ion（拉丁 -ionem）。percept- 出自拉丁 percipere，即 per-“彻底”+ capere“拿取”。词族分工整齐：-ion 行为、-ive 人、-ual 属性、-ible 可能性，percept 则是对象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is capere 'take', percipere 'take in thoroughly', perceptio 'a taking in', and perceptum 'the thing taken in'. The same capere with other prefixes gives receive, accept, intercept, and participate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 capere“拿取”、percipere“彻底拿进来”、perceptio“拿进来这件事”、perceptum“被拿进来之物”。同一个 capere 配上其他前缀，还产生表示“接收”“接受”“拦截”与“参与”的词。

items.meaning: the act or result of taking in through the senses or mind
items.meaningCN: 通过感官或心智拿进来的行为或结果（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Perception of the signal dropped in the fog.
items.exampleCN: 雾中对该信号的感知减弱了。

items.meaning: to become aware of, to take in
items.meaningCN: 察觉；把……收入感知（per- 彻底 + capere 拿取）
items.example: They perceived a change in his tone.
items.exampleCN: 他们察觉到他的语气变了。

items.structure: Latin perceptum, neuter past participle of percipere
items.meaning: the object or content of a perception
items.meaningCN: 知觉的对象或内容
items.example: The percept is the red patch, not the apple itself.
items.exampleCN: 知觉对象是那块红色，而不是苹果本身。

items.meaning: quick to notice and understand
items.meaningCN: 察觉与理解敏捷的；有洞察力的（-ive 倾向形容词）
items.example: A perceptive reader notices the repeated image.
items.exampleCN: 有洞察力的读者会注意到反复出现的意象。

items.meaning: relating to perception as a process
items.meaningCN: 与知觉过程有关的（-ual 形容词）
items.example: Perceptual learning improves with practice.
items.exampleCN: 知觉学习会随练习而提高。

items.meaning: able to be noticed
items.meaningCN: 能被察觉的（-ible 可……的）
items.example: There was a perceptible drop in temperature.
items.exampleCN: 温度有可察觉的下降。

items.meaning: too slight to be noticed
items.meaningCN: 太轻微而察觉不到的（im- 否定）
items.example: The change was imperceptible at first.
items.exampleCN: 起初这一变化察觉不到。

items.meaning: a wrong understanding or impression
items.meaningCN: 错误的知觉或印象（mis- 错误）
items.example: The misperception persisted for years.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误印象持续了好多年。

items.meaning: a point of view; the art of showing depth
items.meaningCN: 观点；透视法（per- + specere 看 + -ive）
items.example: The drawing uses one-point perspective.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画使用单点透视。

latinEntries.meaning: that which has been taken in

definition_zh: 知觉的；感知的；感官层面的；知觉心理学的；与概念相对的；视觉感知的；言语感知的；知觉障碍的；知觉阶段的
definition_en: relating to perception, to the way the senses take in and organize information, as opposed to abstract reasoning or conceptual thought
core_image: 地图的绘制方式本身，而不是地图上写着的那些地名
scene: 同一张格子图，有人先看见整体轮廓，有人先数清小方块。One sees the whole shape first, the other counts the squares: this is a perceptual difference.
sceneCN: 这里 perceptual 是「知觉层面的」（第 1 个义项：与感官如何接收并组织信息有关）；句意：有人先看见整体轮廓、有人先数清小方块，这是知觉层面的差异。

pos.zh: 知觉的；感知的；感官层面的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Of the perceiving process
senses.definition: relating to perception as a process, especially how sensory information is received, selected, and organized
senses.definitionCN: 与知觉这一过程有关，尤指感官信息如何被接收、筛选与组织
senses.example: Perceptual processing begins before conscious attention arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 知觉加工在有意识的注意到来之前就开始了。
senses.why: Percept- is the thing taken in, and -ual (Latin -alis) means 'belonging to'. Perceptual therefore names the belonging: not the object seen, but the way it is taken in.
senses.whyCN: percept- 是被拿进来之物，-ual（拉丁 -alis）意为“属于……的”。所以 perceptual 命名的是这种归属：不是被看见的对象，而是看见它的方式。

senses.title: Of the senses rather than the mind
senses.definition: relating to sensory experience as distinct from reasoning, memory, or abstract thought
senses.definitionCN: 与感官经验有关，以区别于推理、记忆或抽象思维
senses.example: The task measured perceptual speed, not verbal reasoning.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任务测量的是知觉速度，而不是言语推理。
senses.why: The word draws a line down the mind: on one side sit the senses with their maps, on the other the concepts built from them. Perceptual marks the first side.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在心灵中划下一道线：一边是感官和它们的地图，另一边是由此建起的概念。perceptual 标记的是前一边。

senses.title: Contrasted with conceptual
senses.definition: describing information that comes through the senses, as opposed to information organized by categories and definitions
senses.definitionCN: 描述通过感官而来的信息，相对于按类别与定义组织的信息
senses.example: Infants begin with perceptual categories before they form concepts.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿先有知觉类别，之后才形成概念。
senses.why: A concept is taken together and held still; a percept is taken in and kept moving. The adjective marks the difference between the map as drawn and the map as reasoned about.
senses.whyCN: 概念是被聚在一起并固定住的东西，而知觉对象是被拿进来且仍在变动的东西。这个形容词标记的就是“画出来的地图”与“对地图进行推理”之间的差别。

senses.title: Of the psychology of perception
senses.definition: relating to the branch of psychology that studies how organisms detect patterns, depth, colour, and motion
senses.definitionCN: 属于心理学中研究生物如何辨别图案、深度、颜色与运动的分支
senses.example: Perceptual psychology explains why the lines seem to bend.
senses.exampleCN: 知觉心理学解释了这些线条为什么看起来是弯的。
senses.why: When a discipline takes the taking-in as its object, its adjective becomes part of its name. Perceptual psychology studies the drawing of the map, not the land it represents.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学科把“拿进来”当作研究对象，它的形容词就进入了学科名称。知觉心理学研究的是地图怎么画，而不是它代表的那片土地。

senses.title: Of visual illusions and constancy
senses.definition: relating to visual effects in which the eye's interpretation differs from the measured reality, or stays constant despite changes
senses.definitionCN: 指眼睛的解释与实测现实不符，或在变化中仍保持恒常的视觉效应
senses.example: The Müller-Lyer figure is a classic perceptual illusion.
senses.exampleCN: 缪勒—莱尔图形是经典的视觉错觉。
senses.why: The eye draws its map quickly and confidently, and sometimes draws it wrong. The adjective marks the gap between the quick drawing and the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛画地图又快又自信，有时会画错。这个形容词标记的就是“快速画出的图”与“尺子”之间的差距。

senses.title: Of hearing speech sounds
senses.titleCN: 与言语声音的听辨有关的
senses.definition: relating to the way listeners segment and identify speech sounds, often before any meaning is assigned
senses.definitionCN: 指听者切分并识别言语声音的方式，通常发生在赋予意义之前
senses.example: Perceptual training helps learners separate two similar vowels.
senses.exampleCN: 知觉训练帮助学习者区分两个相近的元音。
senses.why: The map here is drawn by the ear. Perceptual work is the parsing of a continuous stream into units, long before the mind asks what the units mean.
senses.whyCN: 这里的地图由耳朵来画。知觉工作是先把连续的声音流切分成单位，远在头脑追问这些单位是什么意思之前。

senses.title: Of a disorder in perceiving
senses.definition: relating to a disturbance in the way the senses register or interpret information, as in clinical diagnosis
senses.definitionCN: 与感官登记或解释信息的方式出现紊乱有关，见于临床诊断
senses.example: The patient showed a perceptual deficit after the stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 中风之后，患者表现出知觉缺陷。
senses.why: The instrument can break. When the hand no longer takes in properly, the adjective names the fault in the apparatus rather than in the world.
senses.whyCN: 工具是会坏的。当那只手无法正常拿取时，这个形容词命名的是器械的故障，而不是世界的问题。

senses.title: The first stage of cognition
senses.definition: relating to the early stage of information processing that precedes memory, reasoning, and decision
senses.definitionCN: 指先于记忆、推理与决策的信息加工早期阶段
senses.example: The model separates a perceptual stage from a decision stage.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型把知觉阶段与决策阶段分开。
senses.why: Information passes through rooms. The first room is where the senses draft the map; later rooms annotate it. Perceptual names the drafting room.
senses.whyCN: 信息要经过一个个房间。第一个房间是感官起草地图的地方，后面的房间才在上面加注。perceptual 命名的就是起草的那个房间。

senses.title: Of an effect on the senses
senses.definition: relating to the immediate sensory impression made by a design, artwork, or environment, before interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 指设计、艺术品或环境在解释之前造成的直接感官印象
senses.example: The building's perceptual impact comes from its low contrast, not its size.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑的知觉冲击来自低对比度，而不是体量。
senses.why: Designers work on the drawing before meaning arrives. A perceptual effect is what the map does to the eye before anyone asks what the map is of.
senses.whyCN: 设计者在意义到来之前先处理这张图。知觉效果就是地图在任何人追问“这是什么”之前，先对眼睛做了什么。

intro.en: Perceptual is percept plus -ual, from Latin -alis 'belonging to'. Percept is Latin perceptum, the neuter past participle of percipere 'to take in', itself per- 'thoroughly' plus capere 'take'. The adjective is a modern psychological term: it appears in English in the 19th century, when experimental psychology separated sensation from perception and needed a word for the process itself.
intro.cn: perceptual 是 percept 加 -ual（拉丁 -alis“属于……的”）。percept 是拉丁 perceptum，即 percipere“拿进来”的中性过去分词，而 percipere 是 per-“彻底”加 capere“拿取”。这个形容词是现代心理学术语：19 世纪实验心理学把感觉与知觉分开、需要一个词指知觉过程本身时，它才在英语中出现。

items.en: Perceptum is the neuter past participle of percipere: literally 'that which has been taken in'. Latin already used perceptio for both the receiving and the understanding.
items.cn: perceptum 是 percipere 的中性过去分词，字面即“已经被拿进来之物”。拉丁语早已用 perceptio 同时表示接收与理解。

items.en: Experimental psychology distinguishes sensation (raw stimulation) from perception (organized interpretation) and adopts perceptual for everything belonging to the second term.
items.cn: 实验心理学把感觉（原始刺激）与知觉（有组织的解释）区分开，并采用 perceptual 指属于后者的全部内容。

items.en: The -ual ending is the English form of Latin -alis, the same suffix that gives manual, visual, and conceptual. It marks belonging, so perceptual means 'of perception', never 'able to perceive'.
items.cn: -ual 词尾是拉丁 -alis 的英语形式，也是 manual、visual、conceptual 使用的同一个后缀。它表示归属，所以 perceptual 意为“知觉的”，绝不是“能感知的”。

items.en: The adjective spreads from psychology to design, music, and human factors research: perceptual load, perceptual salience, perceptual speed.
items.cn: 这个形容词从心理学扩散到设计、音乐与人因研究：知觉负荷、知觉显著性、知觉速度。

items.en: Perceptive means the person is quick to notice; perceptible means the thing can be noticed; perceptual means the process of noticing. The three share the -cept- stem but split by the suffix.
items.cn: perceptive 指人察觉得快；perceptible 指事物可被察觉；perceptual 指察觉这一过程。三者共享 -cept- 词干，靠后缀分工。

items.en: Conceptual looks like perceptual but its stem is concept, from concipere 'take together' (con- + capere). It is the companion term, not the same branch: concept holds, percept takes in.
items.cn: conceptual 看起来像 perceptual，但词干是 concept，出自 concipere“聚在一起拿取”（con- + capere）。它是配套术语，却不是同一分支：概念握着，知觉拿进来。

note.en: The first group separates three adjectives from the same -cept- stem, then adds the conceptual companion and one different-root trap. The second group compares the adjectives for sensory input, thinking, observing, and what appears.
note.cn: 第一组分开同出 -cept- 词干的三个形容词，再补上 conceptual 这个配套词与一个不同词根的陷阱。第二组比较表示“感官输入”“思维”“观察”“显现”的几个形容词。

entries.definition: quick to notice and understand. It describes a person, while perceptual describes the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉与理解敏捷的。它描述人，而 perceptual 描述过程本身。

entries.definition: able to be seen, heard, or noticed at all. It is a possibility, not a property of the process.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被看见、听见或察觉的。它表示的是一种可能性，而非过程的属性。

entries.definition: relating to concepts, the categories made by taking things together. It is the usual partner and opposite of perceptual in psychology.
entries.definitionCN: 与概念有关的，即把事物聚在一起所形成的类别。在心理学里，它常与 perceptual 配对并相对。

entries.definition: a point of view or the art of showing depth. Its root is specere 'to look', not capere 'to take', so it belongs to the eye's position, not to the intake of information.
entries.definitionCN: 观点或表现深度的技法。它的词根是 specere“看”，不是 capere“拿取”，所以属于眼睛的位置，而非信息的接收。

entries.definition: relating to the sense organs and their input. It names the hardware, while perceptual names the organizing work done with that input.
entries.definitionCN: 与感觉器官及其输入有关的。它命名硬件，而 perceptual 命名对这些输入所做的组织工作。

entries.definition: relating to mental processes such as memory, reasoning, and problem-solving. It covers the whole mind, of which the perceptual stage is the entry.
entries.definitionCN: 与记忆、推理、解决问题等心理过程有关的。它覆盖整个心智，而知觉阶段是其中的入口。

entries.definition: based on watching and recording events, often deliberately. It is an activity of a researcher, not a process of the nervous system.
entries.definitionCN: 基于观看并记录事件的，常带有刻意性。它是研究者的活动，而不是神经系统的过程。

entries.definition: relating to experience as it appears to a subject, or simply extraordinary. The philosophical sense is close to perceptual experience, but the everyday sense is 'remarkable'.
entries.definitionCN: 与主体所经验到的显现有关的，或仅指非凡的。其哲学义接近知觉经验，但日常义是“了不起的”。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: -alis 'belonging to', perceptum, the 19th-century psychology split, the three -cept- adjectives, and the con- 'together' contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：-alis“属于”、perceptum、19 世纪心理学的划分、三个 -cept- 形容词，以及 con-“一起”的对比。

normal.en: -ual means 'belonging to': perceptual belongs to perception, just as conceptual belongs to concept and visual to sight.
normal.cn: -ual 意为“属于”：perceptual 属于 perception，就像 conceptual 属于 concept、visual 属于 sight。

normal.en: Perceptum is 'what has been taken in'; perceptual describes the machinery that does the taking.
normal.cn: perceptum 是“已经被拿进来之物”；perceptual 描述执行拿取的那套机制。

normal.en: Perceptive is the person, perceptible is the thing, perceptual is the process: one stem, three suffixes, three jobs.
normal.cn: perceptive 是人，perceptible 是物，perceptual 是过程：一个词干，三个后缀，三种职责。

normal.en: Conceptual has con- 'together' inside: a concept holds things together, while a percept merely brings them in.
normal.cn: conceptual 里面有 con-“一起”：概念把事物握在一起，而知觉只是把它们拿进来。

normal.en: Psychology split sensation from perception in the 19th century, and perceptual became the adjective of the second half.
normal.cn: 19 世纪心理学把感觉与知觉分开，perceptual 成为后半部分的形容词。

abstract.en: A map is not the land, and the drawing style is not the landscape; perceptual is the style of the drawing.
abstract.cn: 地图不是土地，画法也不是风景；perceptual 指的是那种画法。

abstract.en: Two people read the same page: one sees letters, one sees words. The page never moved; the organizing did.
abstract.cn: 两个人读同一页：一个看见字母，一个看见单词。纸页没动，组织方式动了。

abstract.en: An illusion is a map drawn with confidence before the ruler is consulted.
abstract.cn: 错觉就是在还没问尺子之前，就被自信地画出来的地图。

examples.en: Perceptual learning lets the eye recognize the pattern faster.
examples.cn: 知觉学习让眼睛更快认出这个图案。

examples.en: The study compares perceptual and conceptual categories in children.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较儿童的知觉类别与概念类别。

examples.en: Perceptual judgments vary more than the physical measurements do.
examples.cn: 知觉判断的差异比物理测量值的差异更大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破塞普图尔」——眼睛“破”开外面的世界，把东西“塞”进去，画成一张图，这张图的画法就是 perceptual → 知觉的；感知的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 perceptum「被拿进来之物」，出自 percipere「拿进来、把握」（per-「彻底」+ capere「拿取」）；后缀 -ual（拉丁 -alis）表归属。核心是「地图的画法本身，而不是地图上的地名」。同族含 perceive、perception、percept、perceptive、perceptible；conceptual 共享 capere 但用 con-「一起」，perspective 的词根则是 specere「看」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of perceptual all describe the drawing of an inner map rather than the land it shows. What changes is which part of the drawing is in view: the process, the sensory side, the contrast with concepts, the psychology, the illusion, the disorder, or the effect on a viewer.
sensesIntro.cn: perceptual 的九个义项都描述内部地图的画法，而不是它所显示的土地。变化的是画法中哪一部分进入视野：过程本身、感官一侧、与概念的对照、心理学、错觉、障碍，还是对观看者的效果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the drawing style of the inner map, not the place names written on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：内部地图的画法本身，而不是写在地图上的地名。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: the receiving and organizing itself, and its place as the first stage of cognition.
branches.cn: 过程：接收与组织本身，以及它作为认知第一阶段的地位。

branches.en: THE SENSORY SIDE: experience through the senses, defined against conceptual thinking.
branches.cn: 感官一侧：通过感官获得的经验，以概念思维为对照来界定。

branches.en: THE STUDY AND ITS SURPRISES: perceptual psychology and the illusions it explains.
branches.cn: 研究及其意外：知觉心理学，以及它所解释的错觉。

branches.en: EARS AND CLINICS: the parsing of speech sounds, and deficits in the perceiving apparatus.
branches.cn: 耳朵与临床：言语声音的切分，以及知觉器械的缺陷。

branches.en: THE DESIGNED EFFECT: what a visual or spatial arrangement does to the eye before interpretation.
branches.cn: 被设计的效果：视觉或空间安排在任何解释之前对眼睛做了什么。

intro.en: Perceptual is percept plus -ual, the English form of Latin -alis. Percept is Latin perceptum, from percipere (per- 'thoroughly' + capere 'take'). The whole family is built by suffix change on one stem: -ion, -ive, -ible, -ual, and the bare -t.
intro.cn: perceptual 是 percept 加 -ual，即拉丁 -alis 的英语形式。percept 是拉丁 perceptum，出自 percipere（per-“彻底”+ capere“拿取”）。整个词族都在同一个词干上换后缀：-ion、-ive、-ible、-ual，以及零后缀的 -t。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is capere 'take', percipere 'take in', perceptum 'the thing taken in'. Latin had no perceptual; the adjective is a modern extension of the participle stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 capere“拿取”、percipere“拿进来”、perceptum“被拿进来之物”。拉丁语并没有 perceptual，这个形容词是分词词干在现代的延伸。

items.meaning: belonging to the process of perceiving
items.meaningCN: 属于知觉过程的（-ual 表归属）
items.example: Perceptual errors are common in low light.
items.exampleCN: 光线不足时知觉错误很常见。

items.meaning: the act or result of perceiving
items.meaningCN: 知觉的行为或结果（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Her perception of the tone was accurate.
items.exampleCN: 她对语气的感知是准确的。

items.meaning: to take in through the senses or mind
items.meaningCN: 通过感官或心智拿进来；察觉
items.example: We perceived a slight shift in the light.
items.exampleCN: 我们察觉到光线有轻微变化。

items.meaning: the content taken in by the senses
items.meaningCN: 感官所拿进来的内容；知觉对象
items.example: The percept is not the object but the object as sensed.
items.exampleCN: 知觉对象不是物本身，而是被感觉到的物。

items.meaning: quick to notice
items.meaningCN: 察觉敏捷的（-ive 倾向形容词）
items.example: She is perceptive about other people's moods.
items.exampleCN: 她对别人的情绪很敏锐。

items.meaning: able to be noticed
items.meaningCN: 可被察觉的（-ible 可……的）
items.example: The difference was barely perceptible.
items.exampleCN: 这一差别几乎察觉不到。

items.meaning: in terms of perception
items.meaningCN: 从知觉角度来说（-ly 副词）
items.example: The two colours are perceptually identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两种颜色在知觉上是相同的。

items.meaning: belonging to concepts formed by taking things together
items.meaningCN: 属于把事物聚在一起所形成的概念的（con- 一起 + capere 拿取）
items.example: Conceptual models guide the experiment.
items.exampleCN: 概念模型指导这项实验。

items.meaning: relating to the sense organs
items.meaningCN: 与感觉器官有关的（sentire 感觉 + -ory）
items.example: Sensory overload makes concentration hard.
items.exampleCN: 感官过载会让注意力难以集中。

latinEntries.meaning: that which has been taken in

definition_zh: 表演；演出；表现；业绩；执行；履行；性能；语言运用；（仪式的）进行；表演性
definition_en: the act of staging a work for an audience, the way a person, team, or machine carries out a task, the fulfilling of a duty, or the actual use of language as opposed to underlying knowledge
core_image: 舞台上的动作被观众看见并打分，或机器被推到极限，看它到底能跑多快
scene: 年终评审会上，经理把三条产品线的曲线投在墙上，逐条解释哪一条达标。The manager put the performance curves of three product lines on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 performance 是「业绩」（第 2 个义项：个人或组织在工作上取得的成果与表现）；句意：经理把三条产品线的业绩曲线投在墙上。

pos.zh: 表演；演出；表现；业绩；执行；履行；性能

derivatives.zh: 表现不佳；业绩低于预期

senses.title: A work staged for an audience
senses.definition: the staging of a play, concert, dance, or other work before an audience, taken as an event or an art
senses.definitionCN: 在观众面前上演戏剧、音乐会、舞蹈或其他作品，作为事件或艺术看待
senses.example: The evening performance sold out two weeks in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 晚场演出提前两周售罄。
senses.why: The Old French source meant 'to complete, to carry through'. A play is complete only when it is carried through in front of people: the script is the plan, performance is the doing.
senses.whyCN: 古法语来源意为“完成、贯彻到底”。一部戏只有在人前贯彻到底才算完成：剧本是计划，performance 是做出来。

senses.title: How well a person or group does
senses.definition: the measured quality of a person's, team's, or organization's work against a standard or expectation
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团队或组织的工作相对于标准或预期的可衡量质量
senses.example: Her performance improved once the targets were made clear.
senses.exampleCN: 目标明确之后，她的表现有所提升。
senses.why: The same carrying-through is now watched by a manager rather than an audience. What matters is not whether the work is beautiful but whether it reaches the mark.
senses.whyCN: 同样是贯彻到底，只是这次看的是经理而不是观众。关键不再是作品美不美，而是它有没有达到标准。

senses.title: The carrying out of a task
senses.definition: the act of executing a task, duty, or function, often with attention to whether it was done at all and done correctly
senses.definitionCN: 执行任务、职责或功能的行为，常关注是否完成以及是否正确完成
senses.example: The performance of the repair took longer than the estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项维修的执行比预估花了更长时间。
senses.why: This is the plainest sense: the plan is carried through. No audience and no score, only the difference between what was supposed to happen and what happened.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的义项：计划被贯彻到底。没有观众也没有评分，只有“本该发生什么”与“实际发生了什么”之间的差别。

senses.title: What a machine can do
senses.definition: the speed, power, or efficiency with which a machine, vehicle, or system operates under test or load
senses.definitionCN: 机器、车辆或系统在测试或负载下运转的速度、功率或效率
senses.example: The engine's performance drops at high altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机在高海拔地区性能会下降。
senses.why: A machine has no will, but it can still be pushed to its limit. Performance becomes the measure of that limit, the carrying-through of metal instead of muscle.
senses.whyCN: 机器没有意志，但仍可被推到极限。performance 成了对这种极限的度量，是金属而非肌肉的贯彻到底。

senses.title: Actual use of language
senses.definition: in linguistics, the actual production and comprehension of speech in real situations, as opposed to the speaker's underlying competence
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中指真实情境中话语的实际产生与理解，相对于说话者底层的语言能力
senses.example: Errors in performance do not prove a lack of competence.
senses.exampleCN: 语言运用中的错误并不能证明缺乏语言能力。
senses.why: Chomsky borrowed the word for the difference between knowing a grammar and using it under pressure. The plan inside the head is competence; the carrying-through in time is performance.
senses.whyCN: 乔姆斯基借这个词区分“懂语法”与“在压力下使用语法”。头脑里的计划是语言能力，时间中的贯彻到底是语言运用。

senses.title: One particular show
senses.definition: a single instance of presenting a work, countable and datable, as in the third performance of a run
senses.definitionCN: 呈现某作品的一次具体实例，可计数、可定时，如巡演中的第三场
senses.example: The Saturday performance was recorded for the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 周六那场演出被录入了档案。
senses.why: A run of a play is many carryings-through. This sense counts them, which is why the word takes a plural and a date while the art sense does not.
senses.whyCN: 一部戏的连演是许多次贯彻到底。这个义项把它们数出来，所以这个词可以有复数和日期，而艺术义则不行。

senses.title: The carrying out of a ritual
senses.definition: the enactment of a ceremony, rite, or formal role according to prescribed words and actions
senses.definitionCN: 按规定的言语与动作进行仪式、典礼或正式角色
senses.example: The performance of the wedding rite lasted forty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼仪式的进行持续了四十分钟。
senses.why: A rite exists only when it is done. Here performance is not entertainment but the condition of the thing existing at all, which shows how wide the 'carry through' sense is.
senses.whyCN: 仪式只有在被做出来时才存在。这里的 performance 不是娱乐，而是事物得以存在的条件，可见“贯彻到底”这一义项有多宽。

senses.title: The financial results of a business
senses.definition: the financial results of a company, fund, or economy over a period, measured in profit, growth, or return
senses.definitionCN: 公司、基金或经济在一段时间内的财务结果，以利润、增长或回报衡量
senses.example: The fund's performance trailed the index for three quarters.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金连续三个季度的业绩落后于指数。
senses.why: Money is the scoreboard of the market. Performance here is the carrying-through of a strategy expressed as a number that can be compared with rivals.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是市场的记分牌。这里的 performance 是把战略贯彻到底后，用可与对手比较的数字表达出来的结果。

senses.title: Doing that makes what it says
senses.definition: the quality of an utterance or act that brings about what it describes, as when saying 'I promise' is itself the promise
senses.definitionCN: 话语或行为在说出或做出时同时实现其所描述之事的性质，例如说“我保证”本身就是保证
senses.example: The philosopher studied the performative side of promises and apologies.
senses.exampleCN: 这位哲学家研究承诺与道歉的施为性一面。
senses.why: If a promise is completed by being spoken, then the saying is the doing. This sense pushes the 'carry through' idea to its limit: the performance is the only thing there is.
senses.whyCN: 如果承诺因被说出而完成，那么说就是做。这个义项把“贯彻到底”推到极限：表演本身就是唯一存在的东西。

intro.en: Performance comes from perform plus -ance (Latin -antia). Perform is not built on form: it comes from Anglo-French parformer, from Old French parfournir 'to accomplish, complete', literally per- 'thoroughly' + fournir 'to provide, furnish'. The original sense is 'to carry something through to the end'. English added the theatre sense in the 16th century, the machine sense in the 19th, and the linguistic sense in the 20th.
intro.cn: performance 来自 perform 加 -ance（拉丁 -antia）。perform 并不是由 form 构成的：它来自盎格鲁法语 parformer，再上溯古法语 parfournir“完成、贯彻”，字面是 per-“彻底”+ fournir“提供、供给”。本义是“把某事贯彻到底”。英语在 16 世纪加入戏剧义，19 世纪加入机器义，20 世纪加入语言学义。

items.en: Parfournir means 'to complete, to carry out fully'. The prefix par- is the French form of Latin per- 'thoroughly'; fournir 'to furnish, provide' is from the reconstructed Frankish form *frumjan.
items.cn: parfournir 意为“完成、彻底执行”。前缀 par- 是拉丁 per-“彻底”的法语形式；fournir“供给、提供”出自法兰克语的重构形式 *frumjan。

items.en: English perform first means 'to carry out, accomplish, execute' a task, promise, or duty. The spelling has no connection with form, despite the shared letters.
items.cn: 英语 perform 最早意为“执行、完成、履行”任务、承诺或职责。尽管拼写共享 form 几个字母，它与 form 毫无词源关系。

items.en: The theatre sense develops: to perform a play is to carry the script through into sound and action before an audience.
items.cn: 戏剧义在 16 世纪发展出来：演一部戏，就是把剧本贯彻成观众面前的声与动作。

items.en: Industry applies the word to machines and horses: performance is what an engine or animal can actually deliver under load.
items.cn: 19 世纪工业把这个词用于机器与马匹：performance 是发动机或牲畜在负载下实际能交付的东西。

items.en: Chomsky contrasts performance with competence in linguistics (1965), and management makes performance a measurable target.
items.cn: 20 世纪乔姆斯基在语言学中用 performance 与 competence 相对（1965），管理学则把 performance 变成可测量的指标。

items.en: Form, formal, and formative come from Latin forma 'shape'. Perform has no forma inside it: its fournir is 'provide'. The shared form- is spelling only, so performance is completion, not shaping.
items.cn: form、formal、formative 来自拉丁 forma“形状”。perform 里面没有 forma：它的 fournir 是“提供”。共享的 form- 只是拼写，所以 performance 是完成，不是塑形。

note.en: The first group separates perform's true family from the form trap. The second group compares execution, achievement, a show, and efficiency, the four words most often used in place of performance.
note.cn: 第一组把 perform 真正的词族与 form 陷阱分开。第二组比较执行、成就、演出与效率，这四个词最常被用来替代 performance。

entries.definition: to carry out an action, duty, or work before others. Performance is the noun of that carrying-through.
entries.definitionCN: 执行某项行动、职责或在他人面前呈现作品。performance 是这一贯彻过程的名称。

entries.definition: a person who performs, especially on stage. It names the doer, while performance names the deed or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 表演的人，尤指舞台上的人。它命名做的人，而 performance 命名行为或其结果。

entries.definition: shape, structure, or a document with blanks. It comes from Latin forma 'shape' and has no connection with perform's fournir 'provide'.
entries.definitionCN: 形状、结构，或带空格的表格。它来自拉丁 forma“形状”，与 perform 的 fournir“提供”毫无关系。

entries.definition: shaping someone's development, as in formative years. It belongs to the forma family, so it is about shaping, not about completing a task.
entries.definitionCN: 塑造人成长的，如“形成期”。它属于 forma 词族，讲的是塑形，不是完成任务。

entries.definition: the act of putting a plan, order, or law into effect. It is close to performance in the task sense but carries no audience or score.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划、命令或法律付诸实施的行为。它在任务义上接近 performance，但不带观众或评分。

entries.definition: something accomplished, especially after effort. It names the result that stands, while performance can name the ongoing doing.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力而完成的事。它命名留下来的结果，而 performance 可以命名正在进行的做。

entries.definition: a public entertainment, or a display. It is the event sense of performance, but it can also mean an insincere display.
entries.definitionCN: 公开的娱乐演出，或展示。它对应 performance 的事件义，但也可以指不真诚的做样子。

entries.definition: the ratio of useful output to the resources used. It is one measured part of performance, not the whole judgement of it.
entries.definitionCN: 有用产出与所耗资源之比。它是 performance 中被测量的一部分，而不是对它的整体判断。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: Old French parfournir, fournir 'provide', the 16th-century stage sense, the 19th-century machine sense, and the form trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：古法语 parfournir、fournir“提供”、16 世纪的舞台义、19 世纪的机器义，以及 form 陷阱。

normal.en: Parfournir is 'to complete': a performance is a plan carried through to the end, whether on a stage, in a factory, or under a test load.
normal.cn: parfournir 是“完成”：performance 就是被贯彻到底的计划，无论是在舞台上、车间里，还是在测试负载下。

normal.en: Perform has no form inside it; its fournir means 'provide'. The resemblance to form is a spelling accident.
normal.cn: perform 里面没有 form；它的 fournir 意为“提供”。与 form 的相似只是拼写上的偶然。

normal.en: Theatre gave the word its audience, industry gave it a dial, and linguistics gave it a contrast with competence.
normal.cn: 戏剧给了它观众，工业给了它仪表盘，语言学给了它与“语言能力”的对照。

normal.en: The suffix chain is perform → performer → performance → performative, with -ance naming the act or result.
normal.cn: 后缀链是 perform → performer → performance → performative，其中 -ance 命名行为或结果。

normal.en: A performance review, a live performance, and an engine's performance are the same noun doing three jobs: judgement, event, and limit.
normal.cn: 绩效评估、现场演出与发动机性能，是同一个名词在做三件事：评判、事件与极限。

abstract.en: A score is only a plan for sound; the concert exists for one hour and then cannot be returned to.
abstract.cn: 乐谱只是声音的计划；音乐会存在一小时，然后就再也回不去了。

abstract.en: A machine has no ambition, yet we ask it to perform, as if the dial could be proud.
abstract.cn: 机器没有野心，我们却要求它“表现”，仿佛仪表盘会骄傲。

abstract.en: Saying 'I promise' does not describe the promise; it is the promise, made in the air between two people.
abstract.cn: 说“我保证”并不是在描述承诺；它就是承诺本身，在两个人口之间的空气里做成。

examples.en: The orchestra's performance was broadcast to a million listeners.
examples.cn: 乐团的演出被播给上百万听众。

examples.en: The company reported strong performance in the third quarter.
examples.cn: 公司报告第三季度业绩强劲。

examples.en: The contract requires the performance of the work by June.
examples.cn: 合同要求这项工程在六月前完成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破佛曼斯」——演员“破”开剧本，把计划“佛”系地贯彻到底，站在台上做完 → performance 表演；表现；性能（只借音，不表词源）

root: 盎格鲁法语 parformer、古法语 parfournir「完成、贯彻到底」，由 per-「彻底」+ fournir「提供」构成；后缀 -ance（拉丁 -antia）构成名词。核心是「把计划贯彻到底，做到最后」。与 form（拉丁 forma「形状」）只是拼写相似，词根不同；四个主要义项分别是演出、表现、执行、性能。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of performance all describe a plan carried through to the end. What changes is who watches and what counts: an audience, a manager, a contract, a test bench, a grammar, a ritual, a market, or the very act of speaking.
sensesIntro.cn: performance 的九个义项都描述一个被贯彻到底的计划。变化的是谁在看、什么算数：观众、经理、合同、试验台、语法、仪式、市场，还是说话这一行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plan driven through to the end while others watch and judge the result.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个计划在他人注视与评判下被贯彻到底。

branches.en: THE STAGE AND THE RITE: a work or ceremony carried through before witnesses, and one countable instance of it.
branches.cn: 舞台与仪式：在见证者面前完成的艺术作品或典礼，以及其中可计数的一次。

branches.en: THE SCOREBOARD: a person's or firm's results measured against a standard, including financial results.
branches.cn: 记分牌：个人或公司相对标准的成果，包括财务结果。

branches.en: THE PLAIN DEED: a task or duty actually executed, with no audience beyond the contract.
branches.cn: 朴素的行为：实际执行的任务或职责，除合同外没有别的观众。

branches.en: THE MACHINE'S LIMIT: what an engine or system can deliver under load.
branches.cn: 机器的极限：发动机或系统在负载下能交付的东西。

branches.en: LANGUAGE AS DOING: actual speech use in contrast to competence, and utterances that accomplish what they say.
branches.cn: 作为行动的语言：与语言能力相对的实际言语运用，以及说出即做成的话语。

intro.en: Performance is perform plus -ance, from Latin -antia. Perform comes from Old French parfournir, not from form. The family is regular: -er the person, -ance the act or result, -ative the adjective, -ativity the abstract quality.
intro.cn: performance 是 perform 加 -ance（拉丁 -antia）。perform 来自古法语 parfournir，而不是 form。词族很规则：-er 人、-ance 行为或结果、-ative 形容词、-ativity 抽象性质。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is per- 'thoroughly' and the noun suffix -antia, which forms nouns of state or action. The verb itself is French, from Frankish *frumjan 'to provide'; Latin had no performare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 per-“彻底”与名词后缀 -antia（构成状态或动作名词）。动词本身是法语的，出自法兰克语 *frumjan“提供”；拉丁语并没有 performare 这个动词。

items.meaning: the carrying out of a task, or its public result
items.meaningCN: 任务的执行，或其公开的结果（-ance 动作／结果名词）
items.example: The performance of the pump was tested at low temperature.
items.exampleCN: 这台泵的性能在低温下接受了测试。

items.meaning: to carry out, complete, or present
items.meaningCN: 执行、完成或呈现
items.example: The team performed the test twice.
items.exampleCN: 团队把这项测试做了两次。

items.meaning: one who performs, especially on stage
items.meaningCN: 表演的人，尤指舞台上的人（-er 施动者）
items.example: The performer left the stage in silence.
items.exampleCN: 表演者在沉默中离开舞台。

items.meaning: of an utterance that does what it says
items.meaningCN: 指说出即做成之话语的；施为性的（-ative 功能形容词）
items.example: A performative utterance changes the world by being said.
items.exampleCN: 施为性话语通过被说出而改变世界。

items.meaning: the capacity of acts or words to bring about what they name
items.meaningCN: 行为或言语产生其所命名之事的能力；表演性（-ity 性质名词）
items.example: Gender performativity is a key concept in that field.
items.exampleCN: 性别表演性是该领域的一个核心概念。

items.meaning: results below the expected standard
items.meaningCN: 低于预期标准的表现（under- 低于）
items.example: Underperformance cost the division its bonus.
items.exampleCN: 表现不佳让该部门失去了奖金。

items.meaning: to do better than another
items.meaningCN: 比对手做得更好（out- 超过）
items.example: The fund outperformed its benchmark.
items.exampleCN: 该基金跑赢了基准。

items.meaning: shape or structure; not related to perform
items.meaningCN: 形状或结构；与 perform 不同源
items.example: The form of the roof follows the wind.
items.exampleCN: 屋顶的形状顺着风向。

items.meaning: to supply or provide
items.meaningCN: 供给、提供
items.example: They furnished the room before the guests arrived.
items.exampleCN: 客人到达前他们布置好了房间。

latinEntries.meaning: state or action, forming abstract nouns
latinEntries.meaningCN: 状态或动作，构成抽象名词
形状、模子、形式（与 perform 无关）

definition_zh: 周期性的；定期的；元素周期表的；周期函数的；周期性发作的；天体周期性回归的；掉尾句的；周期性结构的；间歇反复的
definition_en: repeating at fixed intervals of time or space, happening at regular planned intervals, or relating to a cycle such as the table of elements or a mathematical function
core_image: 钟摆每回到同一个位置就敲一下，每两下之间的间隔都一样长
scene: 实验室的仪器每隔六小时自动校准一次，值班表上记着这件事。The instrument calibrates itself at periodic intervals of six hours.
sceneCN: 这里 periodic 是「定期的」（第 2 个义项：按计划在固定间隔重复进行）；句意：这台仪器按六小时的固定间隔定期自行校准。

pos.zh: 周期性的；定期的；周期的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Repeating at equal intervals
senses.definition: recurring after the same interval of time or space, so that each cycle resembles the one before
senses.definitionCN: 在相同的时间或空间间隔之后再次出现，使每个周期都与前一个相似
senses.example: The signal is periodic, with one peak every two seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这个信号是周期性的，每两秒出现一个峰。
senses.why: Greek periodos is 'a going around', from peri- 'around' plus hodos 'way'. A pendulum goes around its arc and returns: periodic means the return happens at the same interval every time.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 periodos 是“绕行一圈”，由 peri-“绕”加 hodos“路”构成。钟摆沿弧线绕一圈又回来：periodic 意为每次都在同样的间隔后回来。

senses.title: Done at planned intervals
senses.definition: carried out at regular planned intervals as part of maintenance, inspection, or routine
senses.definitionCN: 作为维护、检查或例行工作的一部分，按固定的计划间隔执行
senses.example: Periodic maintenance prevents most of these failures.
senses.exampleCN: 定期维护能防止这类故障中的大部分。
senses.why: A schedule is a pendulum drawn on paper. The word marks the planned return of a task, not the physical swinging, so routine work acquires the sense.
senses.whyCN: 日程表是画在纸上的钟摆。这个词标记的是任务按计划返回，而不是物理的摆动，例行工作于是获得这一义项。

senses.title: Of the table of elements
senses.definition: relating to the arrangement of chemical elements by increasing atomic number, in which properties repeat in rows and columns
senses.definitionCN: 指化学元素按原子序数递增排列、性质在行与列中重复的排布方式
senses.example: Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table for elements not yet found.
senses.exampleCN: 门捷列夫在周期表里为尚未发现的元素留下了空格。
senses.why: Chemistry found that properties come back after a certain number of elements, like a pendulum returning. The table is literally a map of returns, hence the periodic table.
senses.whyCN: 化学发现性质在经过一定数目的元素之后会重新出现，就像钟摆回来。这张表字面上就是一张“回归地图”，所以叫元素周期表。

senses.title: Of a function that repeats
senses.definition: of a mathematical function, having the property that its value repeats after a fixed interval of the variable
senses.definitionCN: 指数学函数在自变量经过固定间隔后取值重复的性质
senses.example: Sine is a periodic function with a period of two pi.
senses.exampleCN: 正弦是周期为二π的周期函数。
senses.why: Mathematics strips the image to its skeleton: a value returns to the same height after the same step. The word then names pure repetition, with no clock or pendulum required.
senses.whyCN: 数学把这个意象剥到骨架：经过同样的步长之后，数值回到同样的高度。此时这个词命名的是纯然的重复，不需要钟或钟摆。

senses.title: Of symptoms that return
senses.definition: of a medical condition, recurring in episodes at intervals rather than staying constant
senses.definitionCN: 指医学症状以间隔性的发作形式反复出现，而不是持续不变
senses.example: Periodic fever brings chills every few weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 周期性发热每隔几周就会带来寒战。
senses.why: The body can behave like a clock: healthy between attacks, then returning to the same state. Medicine uses the word for that rhythm, which is why it appears in names of syndromes.
senses.whyCN: 身体也能像钟一样运行：发作之间是健康的，然后又回到同样的状态。医学用这个词描述这种节律，所以它出现在多种综合征的名称里。

senses.title: Of a comet or orbit that returns
senses.definition: of a comet, orbit, or astronomical event, returning at intervals that can be predicted
senses.definitionCN: 指彗星、轨道或天文事件以可预测的间隔回归
senses.example: Halley's comet is periodic, returning roughly every seventy-six years.
senses.exampleCN: 哈雷彗星是周期性的，大约每七十六年回归一次。
senses.why: The earliest scientific sense is astronomical: a body goes around and comes back. The sky provided the first proof that some returns can be predicted exactly.
senses.whyCN: 最早的科学义项是天文学的：天体绕行一圈又回来。天空提供了最早的证据，证明有些回归可以被精确预测。

senses.title: Of a sentence that delays its point
senses.titleCN: 把重点留到句末的掉尾句
senses.definition: of a sentence whose main clause is held back until the end, so that the meaning arrives with a closing turn
senses.definitionCN: 指主要从句被留到句末、意义在收尾处才落下的句子
senses.example: A periodic sentence keeps the reader waiting for the verb.
senses.exampleCN: 掉尾句让读者一直等到动词才落地。
senses.why: Rhetoric borrowed the word for a shape that returns: the sentence suspends, then closes on the point. The period at the end is the pendulum's click.
senses.whyCN: 修辞学借这个词形容一种“回归”的形状：句子先悬着，最后落在重点上。句末的句号就是钟摆那一声。

senses.title: Of a repeating structure in matter
senses.titleCN: 物质中重复排列的结构
senses.definition: of a crystal, lattice, or material, having a structure that repeats at regular spacings
senses.definitionCN: 指晶体、晶格或材料具有按规则间距重复的结构
senses.example: The alloy has a periodic lattice that diffracts X-rays.
senses.exampleCN: 这种合金具有能衍射 X 射线的周期性晶格。
senses.why: Atoms can stand in rows like the marks on a ruler. The same equal spacing that makes a sound periodic makes a crystal periodic, and diffraction is the proof.
senses.whyCN: 原子可以像尺子上的刻度一样排成行。使声音成为周期性的那种等间距，也使晶体成为周期性的，衍射就是证据。

senses.title: Coming back in waves
senses.definition: of events such as outbreaks, shortages, or protests, appearing again after quiet intervals rather than steadily
senses.definitionCN: 指疫情、短缺或抗议等事件在平静间隔之后再次出现，而非持续不断
senses.example: Periodic droughts shaped the history of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 周期性的干旱塑造了这座山谷的历史。
senses.why: The clock is social or ecological rather than mechanical. The word still promises a return, but the interval may be irregular and the cause unknown.
senses.whyCN: 这时的钟是社会或生态的，而不是机械的。这个词仍承诺会回来，但间隔可能不规律，原因也可能不明。

intro.en: Periodic comes from Greek periodikos 'of a period', from periodos 'a going around, circuit', built on peri- 'around' and hodos 'way, journey'. English took it in the 17th century for things that recur at fixed intervals, first in medicine and astronomy. The chemical sense dates from Mendeleev's periodic law of 1869, and the grammatical sense from the same century's study of sentence shape.
intro.cn: periodic 来自希腊语 periodikos“周期的”，出自 periodos“绕行一圈、循环”，由 peri-“绕”与 hodos“路、行程”构成。英语在 17 世纪借入，指按固定间隔重现的事物，最早用于医学与天文学。化学义来自 1869 年门捷列夫的元素周期律，语法义则来自同一世纪对句子形态的研究。

items.en: Hodos means 'way, road, journey'. With peri- 'around', periodos is 'a going around', used of a circuit, a cycle of time, or the path of a heavenly body.
items.cn: hodos 意为“路、道路、行程”。加上 peri-“绕”，periodos 就是“绕行一圈”，用于环路、时间循环或天体路径。

items.en: English periodic first describes diseases and orbits that return at set intervals. The word inherits the Greek image of a circuit rather than the modern clock.
items.cn: 英语 periodic 最早描述按固定间隔回归的疾病与轨道。这个词继承的是希腊语“绕行”的意象，而不是现代的钟表。

items.en: Mendeleev's periodic law states that elemental properties repeat after certain intervals of atomic weight, and the periodic table becomes the standard name for its chart.
items.cn: 门捷列夫的元素周期律指出元素性质在一定的原子量间隔后重复，periodic table 成为这张表的标准名称。

items.en: Mathematics adopts periodic for functions whose values repeat, and rhetoric adopts periodic sentence for a sentence whose point is withheld to the close.
items.cn: 数学用 periodic 指取值重复的函数，修辞学用 periodic sentence 指把重点留到句末的句子。

items.en: The -ic ending is Greek -ikos 'of, relating to'. The noun period itself had entered English earlier from the same Greek word, which is why the adjective and the noun share a stem across two languages.
items.cn: -ic 词尾是希腊 -ikos“关于……的”。名词 period 本身更早从同一个希腊词进入英语，所以形容词与名词在两种语言之间共享词干。

items.en: Periodontal also begins with peri-, but its second element is odous, odont- 'tooth', so it means 'around the tooth'. Periodic's second element is hodos 'way'. The shared peri- is a prefix, not a family.
items.cn: periodontal 也以 peri- 开头，但第二部分是 odous、odont-“牙”，所以意为“牙周”。periodic 的第二部分是 hodos“路”。共享的 peri- 只是前缀，不是同一词族。

note.en: The first group separates period's family from the peri- prefix that looks like kinship. The second group compares regular, recurrent, cyclical, and intermittent, the four words closest to periodic.
note.cn: 第一组把 period 的词族与看起来像亲戚、其实只是共享 peri- 前缀的词分开。第二组比较 regular、recurrent、cyclical、intermittent，这四个词最接近 periodic。

entries.definition: a length of time, a cycle, a full stop, or a class hour. Periodic is the adjective of its repeating sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间、一个周期、一个句号或一节课。periodic 是其重复义的形容词。

entries.definition: a magazine or journal published at regular intervals, or an adjective meaning 'recurring'. The noun sense belongs to publishing, not to science.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔出版的杂志或期刊，或作形容词表示“周期性发生的”。名词义属于出版业，不属于科学。

entries.definition: the quality of being periodic, often measured as a rate. It names the property, while periodic names the thing that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 具有周期性的性质，常以比率测量。它命名属性，而 periodic 命名具有该属性的事物。

entries.definition: relating to the tissue around the teeth. Its second element is odont- 'tooth', so only the prefix matches periodic.
entries.definitionCN: 与牙齿周围组织有关的。它的第二部分是 odont-“牙”，所以只有前缀与 periodic 相同。

entries.definition: occurring at even, predictable intervals. It stresses the evenness of the spacing, while periodic stresses the return itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以均匀、可预测的间隔发生。它强调间隔的均匀，而 periodic 强调“回来”这件事本身。

entries.definition: occurring again, often repeatedly and sometimes without a fixed interval. It is weaker than periodic on timing.
entries.definitionCN: 再次发生的，常反复出现，有时没有固定间隔。它在时间规律性上比 periodic 弱。

entries.definition: following a repeating sequence of stages, as in a business cycle. It stresses the order of phases; periodic stresses the equal spacing.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循重复的阶段序列，如商业周期。它强调阶段的顺序，而 periodic 强调相等的间隔。

entries.definition: stopping and starting at irregular intervals. It lacks the promise of equal spacing that periodic carries.
entries.definitionCN: 以不规律间隔时断时续。它没有 periodic 所带的“间隔相等”这一承诺。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: peri- 'around', hodos 'way', periodos, Mendeleev's 1869 law, the Fourier sense, and the odont- trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：peri-“绕”、hodos“路”、periodos、1869 年门捷列夫周期律、傅里叶的数学义，以及 odont- 陷阱。

normal.en: Periodos is a going around: peri- 'around' plus hodos 'way', so periodic means the thing comes back by the same road.
normal.cn: periodos 是绕行一圈：peri-“绕”加 hodos“路”，所以 periodic 指事物沿同一条路回来。

normal.en: A pendulum returns to the same point after the same time: that return is the whole image behind periodic.
normal.cn: 钟摆经过同样的时间回到同一点：这个回归就是 periodic 背后的全部意象。

normal.en: Mendeleev's table is called periodic because properties come back after a fixed number of elements, exactly like a returning swing.
normal.cn: 门捷列夫的表被称为周期表，因为性质在固定数目的元素之后重新出现，就像摆回来一样。

normal.en: Periodontal looks like a relative but its root is odont- 'tooth': peri- is only a prefix, not a family tie.
normal.cn: periodontal 看起来像亲戚，但词根是 odont-“牙”：peri- 只是前缀，不是血缘。

normal.en: The grammatical periodic sentence delays its point to the end, so the meaning clicks into place like the pendulum at the top of its swing.
normal.cn: 语法上的掉尾句把重点留到句末，意义像钟摆摆到最高点那样“咔”地落定。

abstract.en: A clock is a machine built to make the same moment happen again; periodic is the name of that promise.
abstract.cn: 钟表是一台让同一时刻再次发生的机器；periodic 就是这个承诺的名字。

abstract.en: The tide does not remember the last high water, yet it arrives on time; repetition needs no memory.
abstract.cn: 潮水不记得上一次高潮，却准时到来；重复不需要记忆。

abstract.en: A crystal is a silence made of equal spacing, and X-rays are the ears that hear it.
abstract.cn: 晶体是一片由等间距构成的沉默，X 射线就是听见它的耳朵。

examples.en: The doctor ordered periodic blood tests over the next year.
examples.cn: 医生要求在未来一年里定期做血检。

examples.en: Sodium and potassium sit in the same column of the periodic table.
examples.cn: 钠和钾位于元素周期表的同一列。

examples.en: The waveform is periodic but not a simple sine wave.
examples.cn: 这个波形是周期性的，但不是简单的正弦波。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮瑞奥迪克」——皮瑞围着操场一圈一圈地跑，每圈都在同一个点“打卡” → periodic 周期性的；定期的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 希腊 periodos「绕行一圈、循环」，由 peri-「绕」+ hodos「路」构成，形容词为 periodikos；后缀 -ic（希腊 -ikos）表“关于……的”。核心是「沿同一条路绕一圈，又在同样的间隔后回到原点」。periodontal（peri- + odont-「牙」）只是共享前缀，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of periodic all describe a return after an interval. What changes is the road and the clock: a pendulum, a maintenance schedule, the table of elements, a function, a fever, a comet, a sentence, a crystal lattice, or a drought.
sensesIntro.cn: periodic 的九个义项都描述“经过一段间隔后回来”。变化的是那条路与那座钟：钟摆、维护日程、元素表、函数、发热、彗星、句子、晶格，还是干旱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pendulum that returns to the same point every time, with equal spacing between the clicks.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟摆每次都回到同一点，每两声之间的间隔相等。

branches.en: THE PURE RETURN: equal intervals in time or space, and the mathematical function that repeats its value.
branches.cn: 纯粹的回归：时间或空间上的相等间隔，以及取值重复的数学函数。

branches.en: HUMAN SHAPES: planned routines such as maintenance, and the sentence whose point waits until the end.
branches.cn: 人造的形状：维护等计划性例行工作，以及把重点留到句末的句子。

branches.en: MATTER ARRANGED: the table of elements and the repeating lattice of a crystal.
branches.cn: 排列起来的物质：元素周期表，以及晶体中重复的晶格。

branches.en: THE RETURN OF EVENTS: fevers that come back and droughts or outbreaks that arrive in waves.
branches.cn: 事件的回归：反复发作的发热，以及一波一波到来的干旱或疫情。

branches.en: THE SKY: comets and orbits whose returns can be predicted years ahead.
branches.cn: 天空：可以提前多年预测回归的彗星与轨道。

intro.en: Periodic is Greek periodikos, from periodos (peri- 'around' + hodos 'way') plus -ikos, the adjective suffix English renders as -ic. English also has the noun period, taken earlier from the same Greek word, and the derived adverb periodically.
intro.cn: periodic 是希腊语 periodikos，出自 periodos（peri-“绕”+ hodos“路”）加 -ikos，即英语写作 -ic 的形容词后缀。英语还有更早从同一个希腊词借入的名词 period，以及派生副词 periodically。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: the word is Greek through and through. Latin only supplied the connecting forms periodus and periodicus in scientific writing, which is why the spelling reached English unchanged.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁来源：它从头到尾都是希腊语。拉丁语只在科学写作中提供了连接形式 periodus 与 periodicus，所以拼写原样进入英语。

items.meaning: of a going around; recurring at intervals
items.meaningCN: 属于绕行一圈的；按间隔重现的（-ic 形容词后缀）
items.example: Periodic checks caught the leak early.
items.exampleCN: 定期检查及早发现了泄漏。

items.structure: Greek periodos 'a going around', via Latin periodus
items.meaning: a length of time, a cycle, a full stop
items.meaningCN: 一段时间、一个周期、一个句号
items.example: The period of the wave is 0.2 seconds.
items.exampleCN: 这个波的周期是 0.2 秒。

items.meaning: at regular intervals
items.meaningCN: 按固定间隔地；定期地（-ally 副词）
items.example: The database is backed up periodically.
items.exampleCN: 数据库会定期备份。

items.meaning: the quality of recurring at intervals
items.meaningCN: 按间隔重现的性质；周期性（-ity 性质名词）
items.example: The periodicity of the signal is not exact.
items.exampleCN: 这个信号的周期性并不精确。

items.meaning: a publication issued at regular intervals
items.meaningCN: 按固定间隔出版的刊物；期刊（-al 构成名词）
items.example: The library subscribes to forty periodicals.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆订阅了四十种期刊。

items.meaning: not repeating at fixed intervals
items.meaningCN: 不按固定间隔重复的；非周期的（a- 否定）
items.example: The aperiodic tiling never repeats itself.
items.exampleCN: 这种非周期拼贴永不自我重复。

items.meaning: way, road, journey
items.meaningCN: 路、道路、行程
items.example: The hodos inside period once meant a journey along a road.
items.exampleCN: “时期”一词里的 hodos 曾指沿路的一段行程。

items.meaning: around, about
items.meaningCN: 围绕、在……周围
items.example: Peri- appears in words describing a circuit, such as a perimeter.
items.exampleCN: peri- 出现在描述环行一周的词语里，例如表示“周长”的词。

items.meaning: around the teeth
items.meaningCN: 牙周的（peri- 绕 + odont- 牙）
items.example: Periodontal disease affects the gums.
items.exampleCN: 牙周病影响牙龈。

latinEntries.meaning: a circuit, a cycle, a period of time
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一圈、一个循环、一段时间

definition_zh: 定期地；周期性地；间歇地；按期地；定时地；有规律地；按周期回归地；一阵一阵地；循环往复地
definition_en: at intervals that repeat, whether fixed by a schedule, by a natural cycle, or by an irregular rhythm that keeps coming back
core_image: 钟摆每次摆到同一个位置时发出的那一下轻响
scene: 机房的管理员把备份任务设成每隔十二小时自动运行一次。The backup job runs periodically, every twelve hours.
sceneCN: 这里 periodically 是「定时地」（第 5 个义项：由设备按设定时间自动重复执行）；句意：备份任务定时运行，每十二小时一次。

pos.zh: 定期地；周期性地；间歇地

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: At planned intervals
senses.definition: at intervals set in advance by a plan, schedule, or rule, so that the action is repeated on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 按计划、日程或规则预先设定的间隔进行，使该行为被有意重复
senses.example: The committee meets periodically to review the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会定期开会复核预算。
senses.why: The adverb is the adjective turned into a rhythm. Where periodic names the return, periodically names the manner of returning: the same step, repeated on a calendar.
senses.whyCN: 副词是把形容词变成一种节律。periodic 命名“回来”，periodically 命名“以回来的方式”：同样的步子，按日历重复。

senses.title: By a natural cycle
senses.definition: according to a cycle in nature, such as tides, seasons, or orbits, rather than a human schedule
senses.definitionCN: 依照自然界的循环，如潮汐、季节或轨道，而不是人为日程
senses.example: The lake level rises periodically with the monsoon.
senses.exampleCN: 湖水水位随季风周期性上升。
senses.why: Here the clock is not on a wall. The pendulum is the planet or the season, and periodically marks the return that no one arranged.
senses.whyCN: 这里的钟不挂在墙上。钟摆是行星或季节，periodically 标记的是无人安排却仍然发生的回归。

senses.title: In waves, with quiet gaps
senses.titleCN: 一阵一阵、中间有间歇地
senses.definition: in bursts that come and go, with quiet intervals between them, often without an exact schedule
senses.definitionCN: 以来了又去的一阵阵方式出现，之间隔着平静的间隔，常无精确日程
senses.example: The old radio periodically crackles for no clear reason.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧收音机会时不时地无故发出噼啪声。
senses.why: The return does not have to be exact to count. This sense loosens the interval and keeps only the image of something coming back in waves.
senses.whyCN: 回归不必精确也算数。这个义项放宽了间隔，只保留“某物一波一波回来”的意象。

senses.title: On a publication schedule
senses.definition: at the intervals at which a journal, magazine, or report is issued
senses.definitionCN: 按期刊、杂志或报告发行的间隔进行
senses.example: The survey is published periodically, usually in spring and autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这份调查定期发布，通常在春季和秋季。
senses.why: Publishing gave the word one of its oldest homes: an issue appears, disappears, and appears again. The period between issues is the interval the adverb names.
senses.whyCN: 出版业给了这个词最古老的落脚点之一：一期出现、消失、再出现。两期之间的那段时间就是副词命名的间隔。

senses.title: On an automatic timer
senses.definition: at intervals triggered automatically by a device, program, or timer rather than by a person
senses.definitionCN: 由设备、程序或计时器自动触发，而不是由人触发
senses.example: The sensor periodically uploads its readings to the server.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器定时把读数上传到服务器。
senses.why: A timer is a pendulum without a pendulum: it counts equal steps and fires. Here periodically describes machine rhythm, the most literal survival of the clock image.
senses.whyCN: 计时器是没有摆锤的钟摆：它数着相等的步子然后触发。这里的 periodically 描述机器节律，是钟表意象最字面的存留。

senses.title: As routine review or care
senses.titleCN: 作为例行复查或保养地
senses.definition: at regular intervals as part of health checks, maintenance, or quality control
senses.definitionCN: 作为健康检查、维护或质量控制的一部分，按固定间隔进行
senses.example: Patients on the drug are monitored periodically for liver function.
senses.exampleCN: 服用该药的患者会定期接受肝功能监测。
senses.why: Routine is a promise that someone will look again. The adverb turns care into a rhythm, so that neglect cannot quietly accumulate between visits.
senses.whyCN: 例行工作是一个承诺：还会有人再看一次。这个副词把照护变成节律，使疏忽无法在两次检查之间悄悄堆积。

senses.title: As a predicted return in the sky
senses.titleCN: 按可预测的天文周期地
senses.definition: at intervals fixed by an orbit, so that the return can be calculated years in advance
senses.definitionCN: 按轨道固定的间隔出现，使回归可以提前多年计算出来
senses.example: The comet passes periodically through the inner solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗彗星周期性地穿过内太阳系。
senses.why: Astronomy is where the word earned its trust: a return that can be written down before it happens. The adverb here is almost a mathematical guarantee.
senses.whyCN: 天文学是这个词赢得信任的地方：回归可以在发生之前就被写下来。这里的副词几乎等于一个数学保证。

senses.title: In cycles of boom and bust
senses.titleCN: 以繁荣与衰退的循环方式
senses.definition: in recurring phases of growth and decline, as in markets, epidemics, or public attention
senses.definitionCN: 以增长与衰退反复交替的阶段出现，如市场、疫情或公众注意力
senses.example: Housing starts periodically overshoot and then collapse.
senses.exampleCN: 住房开工量周期性地冲高，随后崩塌。
senses.why: The cycle is now made of human decisions rather than orbits. The adverb still marks a return, but the period is measured in confidence and credit rather than in degrees.
senses.whyCN: 这时的循环由人的决定构成，而不是轨道。副词仍标记回归，但周期用信心与信贷来度量，而不是用角度。

senses.title: Over and over, back to the same state
senses.definition: repeatedly, in a manner that returns to the same condition, used when the repetition itself is the point
senses.definitionCN: 反复进行并回到同一状态，用于强调重复本身即是重点
senses.example: The argument periodically resurfaces in different words.
senses.exampleCN: 这个争论会周期性地以不同说法重新浮出水面。
senses.why: The strongest form of the image: not just many times, but back to the same place. The adverb says the system has a resting point it cannot leave for good.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个意象最强的形式：不只是很多次，而是回到同一个地方。副词表示这个系统有一个它永远无法彻底离开的停留点。

intro.en: Periodically is periodic plus -ally, the regular English adverb ending built from -al and -ly. Periodic is Greek periodikos, from periodos 'a going around', built on peri- 'around' and hodos 'way'. The adverb simply carries the Greek image into the manner of an action: it tells you that something comes back the way a pendulum does.
intro.cn: periodically 是 periodic 加 -ally，即由 -al 与 -ly 构成的规则英语副词词尾。periodic 是希腊语 periodikos，出自 periodos“绕行一圈”，由 peri-“绕”与 hodos“路”构成。这个副词只是把希腊意象带进行为方式里：它告诉你某事像钟摆一样回来。

items.en: Hodos is 'way, road'; periodos is a going around. The adjective periodikos describes whatever belongs to such a circuit.
items.cn: hodos 是“路、道路”；periodos 是绕行一圈。形容词 periodikos 描述属于这种循环的一切。

items.en: English periodic appears for fevers and orbits that return at set intervals; the adverb follows the adjective as soon as writers need to say how an action recurs.
items.cn: 英语 periodic 先用于按固定间隔回归的发热与轨道；一旦作者需要说明行为如何重现，副词就随形容词出现。

items.en: Periodically settles into the language of administration, science, and publishing: reports issued periodically, instruments checked periodically.
items.cn: periodically 在 18 至 19 世纪进入行政、科学与出版语言：定期发布的报告、定期检查的仪器。

items.en: The ending is transparent: periodic → periodical (adjective) → periodically (adverb), or periodic + -ally. No meaning is added beyond 'in this manner'.
items.cn: 词尾是透明的：periodic → periodical（形容词）→ periodically（副词），或直接 periodic + -ally。除了“以这种方式”，没有增加任何意义。

items.en: Computing makes the adverb routine: processes that run periodically, backups taken periodically, jobs scheduled periodically.
items.cn: 计算机让这个副词成为日常用语：周期性运行的进程、定期执行的备份、定时调度的任务。

items.en: Periodontal begins with the same peri- but continues with odont- 'tooth'; it has nothing to do with intervals. The shared prefix is not a family relation.
items.cn: periodontal 以同一个 peri- 开头，但后面接的是 odont-“牙”，与间隔毫无关系。共享前缀并不是亲缘关系。

note.en: The first group separates the adverb from the adjective, the publication noun, and the base noun. The second group compares regular, intermittent, sporadic, and occasional timing.
note.cn: 第一组把副词与形容词、刊物名词、基础名词分开。第二组比较“规律地”“间歇地”“零星地”“偶尔地”四种时间方式。

entries.definition: recurring at equal intervals. The adverb adds only manner: happening in that recurring way.
entries.definitionCN: 以相等间隔重现的。副词只增加方式：以那种重现的方式发生。

entries.definition: a magazine or journal issued at regular intervals. As a noun it names a thing, not a manner of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔发行的杂志或期刊。作名词时它命名事物，而不是行为方式。

entries.definition: a length of time, a cycle, or a full stop. The adverb is built on the adjective of its cycle sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间、一个周期或一个句号。副词建在其周期义的形容词之上。

entries.definition: relating to the tissue around the teeth. Only the prefix matches; the root is odont- 'tooth'.
entries.definitionCN: 与牙周组织有关的。只有前缀相同，词根是 odont-“牙”。

entries.definition: at even, predictable intervals. It is the broadest word for steady timing; periodically adds the image of a full cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 以均匀、可预测的间隔。它是表示稳定时间的最宽泛的词；periodically 多了“完整一圈”的意象。

entries.definition: in a way that stops and starts. It lacks the regularity that periodically usually implies.
entries.definitionCN: 以时断时续的方式。它缺少 periodically 通常暗示的规律性。

entries.definition: at scattered, unpredictable moments. It is the opposite of a schedule, while periodically suggests at least a loose rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 在零散、不可预测的时刻。它与日程相反，而 periodically 至少暗示一种宽松的节律。

entries.definition: from time to time, without any pattern. It says the frequency is low and says nothing about intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 有时、偶尔，没有规律。它说明频率低，却不对间隔作任何说明。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: peri- 'around', hodos 'way', the -al/-ly adverb chain, the publishing and computing homes of the word, and the odont- trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：peri-“绕”、hodos“路”、-al/-ly 副词链、这个词在出版与计算机领域的落脚点，以及 odont- 陷阱。

normal.en: Periodos is a going around; periodically says an action takes that road again and again.
normal.cn: periodos 是绕行一圈；periodically 表示一个行为一次次走那条路。

normal.en: The ending is just -al plus -ly: periodic makes the adjective, and -ally makes the adverb without adding meaning.
normal.cn: 词尾只是 -al 加 -ly：periodic 构成形容词，-ally 构成副词，不增加意义。

normal.en: Publishing gave it 'issued periodically'; computing gave it 'runs periodically' — two homes of the same pendulum.
normal.cn: 出版业给了它“定期发行”，计算机给了它“定期运行”——同一个钟摆的两个落脚点。

normal.en: Regularly is about even spacing; periodically is about coming back around, which is why a cycle can be mentioned.
normal.cn: regularly 讲间隔均匀；periodically 讲绕回来，所以它才能带上“一个周期”。

normal.en: Periodontal has peri- but not hodos: teeth, not time.
normal.cn: periodontal 有 peri- 却没有 hodos：是牙，不是时间。

abstract.en: A metronome does not care whether anyone is listening; it keeps marking the same interval.
abstract.cn: 节拍器不在乎有没有人在听；它一直标着同样的间隔。

abstract.en: The tide comes back whether the harbour is ready or not, which is what makes a schedule a comfort.
abstract.cn: 不管港口准备好没有，潮水都会回来，这正是日程让人安心的原因。

abstract.en: A machine that checks itself periodically is a machine that has learned to distrust its own last answer.
abstract.cn: 会定期自检的机器，是一台学会了不信任自己上一个答案的机器。

examples.en: The files are backed up periodically to an off-site server.
examples.cn: 文件会定期备份到异地服务器。

examples.en: She checks the greenhouse periodically during cold spells.
examples.cn: 寒潮期间她会不时检查温室。

examples.en: The journal appears periodically, twice a year.
examples.cn: 这份期刊定期出版，每年两期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮瑞奥迪克利」——皮瑞围着操场一圈圈跑，每到同一个点就“滴”一声打卡 → periodically 定期地；周期性地（只借音，不表词源）

root: 希腊 periodos「绕行一圈」，由 peri-「绕」+ hodos「路」构成，形容词 periodikos，英语作 periodic；副词后缀 -ally（-al + -ly）。核心是「钟摆每次摆到同一点的那一下轻响」。periodontal（peri- + odont-「牙」）只是共享前缀，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of periodically all describe an action that comes back on a rhythm. What changes is who keeps the rhythm: a committee, a season, a faulty radio, a publisher, a timer, a clinic, an orbit, a market, or an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: periodically 的九个义项都描述一个按节律回来的行为。变化的是谁在维持节律：委员会、季节、坏收音机、出版方、计时器、诊所、轨道、市场，还是一个争论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the small click a pendulum makes each time it returns to the same point.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟摆每次回到同一点时发出的那一下轻响。

branches.en: THE PLANNED CLICK: meetings, reviews, maintenance, and health checks set by people.
branches.cn: 计划好的那一下：由人设定的会议、复核、维护与健康检查。

branches.en: NATURE'S CLICK: seasons, tides, and orbits that return without a schedule.
branches.cn: 自然的那一下：没有日程却照样回归的季节、潮汐与轨道。

branches.en: THE LOOSE RHYTHM: bursts with quiet gaps, and repetition that keeps returning to the same state.
branches.cn: 宽松的节律：带平静间隔的一阵阵出现，以及不断回到同一状态的重复。

branches.en: THE PUBLISHED CLICK: issues that appear, vanish, and appear again.
branches.cn: 出版的那一下：出现、消失、再出现的期刊。

branches.en: MACHINE AND MARKET: timers firing automatically, and cycles of boom and bust.
branches.cn: 机器与市场：自动触发的计时器，以及繁荣与衰退的循环。

intro.en: Periodically is periodic + -ally, the standard English adverb ending. Periodic is Greek periodikos (periodos + -ikos). The word adds no new meaning; it moves the Greek image of a circuit into the manner of an action.
intro.cn: periodically 是 periodic 加 -ally，即标准英语副词词尾。periodic 是希腊语 periodikos（periodos + -ikos）。这个词不增加新意义，只是把希腊语“绕圈”的意象搬进行为方式。
