latinIntro.en: No Latin root: periodos and periodikos are Greek. Latin only passed the forms periodus and periodicus into scientific prose, from which English took them.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词根：periodos 与 periodikos 都是希腊语。拉丁语只是把 periodus 与 periodicus 这两个形式传进科学散文，英语再从那里取用。

items.meaning: in a recurring manner
items.meaningCN: 以重复回归的方式；定期地（-ally 副词词尾）
items.example: The pump is serviced periodically.
items.exampleCN: 这台泵定期保养。

items.meaning: of a cycle; recurring
items.meaningCN: 属于循环的；周期性重现的
items.example: A periodic signal repeats its shape.
items.exampleCN: 周期信号会重复自己的形状。

items.meaning: a cycle, an interval, a full stop
items.meaningCN: 周期、间隔、句号
items.example: The period of the orbit is 76 years.
items.exampleCN: 这条轨道的周期是七十六年。

items.meaning: a publication issued at intervals
items.meaningCN: 按间隔出版的刊物；期刊
items.example: The reading room keeps the periodicals on open shelves.
items.exampleCN: 阅览室把期刊放在开架上。

items.meaning: the property of recurring
items.meaningCN: 重复回归的属性；周期性
items.example: Researchers measured the periodicity of the rainfall.
items.exampleCN: 研究者测量了降雨的周期性。

items.meaning: not recurring at fixed intervals
items.meaningCN: 不按固定间隔重现的；非周期的
items.example: The aperiodic signal is harder to predict.
items.exampleCN: 非周期信号更难预测。

items.meaning: way, road, journey
items.meaningCN: 路、道路、行程
items.example: The hodos in period once meant the road of a journey.
items.exampleCN: “时期”一词里的 hodos 曾指一段行程所走的路。

items.meaning: around
items.meaningCN: 围绕
items.example: Peri- marks words that mean a circuit, such as a perimeter.
items.exampleCN: peri- 标记表示环行一周的词，例如表示“周长”的词。

items.meaning: around the teeth
items.meaningCN: 牙周的（peri- 绕 + odont- 牙）
items.example: Periodontal care prevents gum loss.
items.exampleCN: 牙周护理能防止牙龈流失。

definition_zh: 坚持不懈；毅力；持续存在；固执；数据的持久性；病原体的持续存在；环境残留的持久性；视觉暂留；长期存续
definition_en: the quality of continuing firmly despite difficulty, the state of something continuing to exist or remain, or a technical property such as stored data surviving or a substance remaining in the environment
core_image: 一只手一直按在同一颗按钮上，那盏灯始终没有灭
scene: 同一道题她算了三遍，草稿纸翻到背面还在写，最后终于算对。Her persistence paid off when the third attempt came out right.
sceneCN: 这里 persistence 是「坚持不懈」（第 1 个义项：面对困难仍持续用力、不放弃的品质）；句意：第三遍终于算对，她的坚持不懈有了回报。

pos.zh: 坚持不懈；毅力；持续存在；持久性；固执

derivatives.zh: 坚持不懈的；持续的；顽固的

senses.title: Continuing against difficulty
senses.definition: the quality of continuing firmly with an aim despite obstacles, discouragement, or repeated failure
senses.definitionCN: 面对障碍、打击或反复失败仍坚定继续追求目标的品质
senses.example: Her persistence in asking questions finally got an answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她坚持追问，最终得到了答案。
senses.why: Latin persistere is per- 'thoroughly' plus sistere 'to stand'. Persistence is standing your ground completely: the hand stays on the button while the light is still off.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 persistere 是 per-“彻底”加 sistere“站立”。persistence 就是彻底站住脚：灯还没亮，手也不离开按钮。

senses.title: The state of continuing to exist
senses.definition: the fact of something continuing to exist or occur over time, without disappearing
senses.definitionCN: 某事物随时间继续存在或发生、并未消失的事实
senses.example: The persistence of the tradition surprised the researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 这一传统延续至今，让研究者感到意外。
senses.why: Nothing is pushing back here; the thing simply fails to stop. The same standing image is used without the struggle, and persistence becomes duration.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有任何阻力，事物只是没有停下来。同一个“站住”的意象去掉了挣扎，persistence 于是变成了持续。

senses.title: Holding to an idea too long
senses.definition: the tendency to keep repeating or defending an idea, request, or belief after it should have been dropped
senses.definitionCN: 在某个想法、请求或信念本应放弃之后仍反复重复或辩护的倾向
senses.example: His persistence about the missing file began to annoy the office.
senses.exampleCN: 他没完没了地追问那份丢失的文件，让办公室的人开始厌烦。
senses.why: Standing too long in one place turns virtue into obstacle. This sense keeps the posture but withdraws the approval: the hand is still on the button, and now nobody wants the light.
senses.whyCN: 在同一个地方站得太久，美德就变成障碍。这个义项保留了姿势却撤回了赞许：手还按在按钮上，可这时没人想要那盏灯亮。

senses.title: Data that survives a restart
senses.definition: in computing, the property of data or an object remaining stored after a program, session, or device stops running
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中指数据或对象在程序、会话或设备停止运行后仍被保存的性质
senses.example: The framework handles persistence by writing records to disk.
senses.exampleCN: 这个框架通过把记录写入磁盘来实现数据持久化。
senses.why: Memory is a lamp that goes out when power stops. Persistence is the design that keeps the lamp lit across the gap, the button held down by code instead of by hand.
senses.whyCN: 内存是一盏断电就灭的灯。持久化是一种设计，让灯跨过断电的间隙继续亮着，由代码而不是由手按住按钮。

senses.title: An infection that will not clear
senses.definition: the continued presence of a pathogen, symptom, or condition in the body after the expected period
senses.definitionCN: 病原体、症状或病情在预期时间之后仍继续存在于体内
senses.example: The persistence of the virus after treatment required a second course.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗之后病毒仍然存在，需要再进行一轮疗程。
senses.why: The body is a room the invader will not leave. Here persistence is not heroic but clinical: something remains where it should have stopped.
senses.whyCN: 身体是一间入侵者不肯离开的房间。这里的 persistence 不是英雄式的，而是临床的：某物停在它本该停止的地方。

senses.title: A chemical that stays in the environment
senses.titleCN: 留在环境中的化学物质
senses.definition: the ability of a substance to remain in soil, water, or living tissue for a long time without breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 物质在土壤、水体或活体组织中长期存在而不分解的能力
senses.example: The persistence of the pesticide in river sediment alarmed regulators.
senses.exampleCN: 这种农药在河底沉积物中的持久残留让监管机构警觉。
senses.why: A lamp left on in an empty building: the chemical keeps standing after its usefulness is over. The word measures how long the light refuses to go out.
senses.whyCN: 像一盏留在空楼里的灯：化学物质在用处结束之后仍然站着。这个词衡量的是灯光多久不肯熄灭。

senses.title: The retina holding an image
senses.definition: the tendency of an image to remain briefly on the retina after the stimulus has moved or vanished
senses.definitionCN: 刺激移开或消失之后影像仍在视网膜上短暂停留的倾向
senses.example: Persistence of vision makes a rapid series of stills look like motion.
senses.exampleCN: 视觉暂留让一连串快速静止画面看起来像运动。
senses.why: Here the lamp is the eye itself, and the light outlives its cause by a fraction of a second. Persistence becomes the physical afterglow that cinema depends on.
senses.whyCN: 这里的灯是眼睛本身，光比它的成因多活了一瞬。persistence 成了电影所依赖的物理余辉。

senses.title: A memory that keeps returning
senses.definition: the quality of an impression or memory that stays available and keeps coming back to mind
senses.definitionCN: 印象或记忆保持可得、并不断回到心头的性质
senses.example: The persistence of that afternoon made the whole year feel unfinished.
senses.exampleCN: 那个下午挥之不去，让整年都像没有结束。
senses.why: The button is pressed by the past. Something in the mind keeps the light on long after the event, which is the emotional version of the same mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 按钮被过去按住了。心里的某样东西让灯在事件之后很久还亮着，这是同一机制的情感版本。

senses.title: A species or practice lasting
senses.titleCN: 物种或做法的长期存续
senses.definition: the continued existence of a species, language, or practice across long periods, often against pressure
senses.definitionCN: 物种、语言或做法在长时间内继续存在，常是在压力之下
senses.example: The persistence of the dialect owes much to a single village school.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方言得以存续，很大程度上归功于一所村庄学校。
senses.why: The largest lamp of all: a whole way of life stays lit. Persistence here is measured in generations, and the hand on the button is a community.
senses.whyCN: 这是最大的一盏灯：一整套生活方式持续亮着。这里的 persistence 以世代计量，按住按钮的手是一个共同体。

intro.en: Persistence comes from Latin persistentia, from persistere 'to continue steadfastly, to stand firm'. Persistere is per- 'thoroughly' plus sistere 'to stand, to take a stand'. English took the noun in the 15th century. The Latin verb sistere also gives assist, insist, resist, and consist, which is why the whole family feels like standing in different postures.
intro.cn: persistence 来自拉丁语 persistentia，出自 persistere“坚定持续、站稳”。persistere 是 per-“彻底”加 sistere“站立、站定”。英语在 15 世纪借入这个名词。拉丁动词 sistere 还产生 assist、insist、resist、consist，所以整个词族都像在不同姿势下站立。

items.en: Sistere means 'to cause to stand, to place, to stand firm'. It comes from the reconstructed PIE form *sta- 'to stand', the same root as English stand and statue.
items.cn: sistere 意为“使站立、放置、站稳”。它出自原始印欧语的重构形式 *sta-“站立”，与英语 stand（站立）、statue（雕像）同源。

items.en: Persistere adds per- 'thoroughly' to sistere: to stand through to the end, to keep one's position. Its participle persistens gives the adjective persistent.
items.cn: persistere 给 sistere 加上 per-“彻底”：站到最后、守住位置。其分词 persistens 产生形容词 persistent。

items.en: English persistence first means 'the act of persisting, constancy'. Persistency is an older doublet that survives mainly in technical usage.
items.cn: 英语 persistence 最早意为“坚持的行为、恒心”。persistency 是更早的异体，今主要存于技术用法。

items.en: The noun gains a negative shade: persistence in an opinion becomes stubbornness, the same posture seen from the other side.
items.cn: 17 世纪这个名词带上负面色彩：对某种意见的坚持变成固执，同一个姿势从另一面看。

items.en: Science adopts it: persistence of vision explains motion pictures, and the persistence of substances becomes a measure of how long they resist decay.
items.cn: 19 世纪科学采用它：视觉暂留解释电影，物质的持久性则成为衡量其抗降解能力的指标。

items.en: Computing adds data persistence, and medicine speaks of the persistence of symptoms or pathogens. The standing image now covers silicon, cells, and soil.
items.cn: 20 世纪计算机加入数据持久性，医学谈论症状或病原体的持续存在。这个“站立”的意象如今覆盖硅片、细胞与土壤。

note.en: The first group separates persistence from its verb, its adjective, and from perseverance, which looks like a twin but was formed differently. The second group compares tenacity, endurance, continuation, and obstinacy.
note.cn: 第一组把 persistence 与其动词、形容词分开，并区分看起来像双胞胎、其实构词不同的 perseverance。第二组比较坚韧、耐力、延续与固执。

entries.definition: to continue firmly or to keep existing. Persistence is the noun of that standing-still.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定继续或持续存在。persistence 是这种“站住不动”的名词形式。

entries.definition: continuing despite difficulty, or remaining for a long time. It describes the thing that stands; persistence names the standing.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管困难仍继续，或长时间保持。它描述站立的事物；persistence 命名站立本身。

entries.definition: steady persistence in a course despite difficulty. It comes from Latin perseverare, a different verb, though English uses the two almost interchangeably.
entries.definitionCN: 在道路上的稳定坚持。它出自另一个拉丁动词 perseverare，尽管英语几乎把两者当同义词使用。

entries.definition: to stand against something. It shares sistere 'stand' but reverses the direction with re- 'against'.
entries.definitionCN: 站在某物的对立面。它共享 sistere“站立”，但用 re-“对抗”把方向反过来。

entries.definition: the quality of holding firmly to a purpose or position. Its image is a hand gripping, while persistence is a body standing.
entries.definitionCN: 牢牢抓住目标或立场不放的品质。它的意象是手在紧握，而 persistence 是身体在站立。

entries.definition: the power to withstand hardship or to last. It stresses bearing pain over time rather than refusing to move.
entries.definitionCN: 承受艰难或持续长久的力量。它强调长时间忍受痛苦，而不是拒绝移动。

entries.definition: the act of carrying on after a pause or interruption. It is neutral and factual, with no praise or blame.
entries.definitionCN: 停顿或中断之后继续进行的行为。它是中性、事实性的，不含褒贬。

entries.definition: stubborn refusal to change course. It is the negative reading of persistence, with the virtue removed.
entries.definitionCN: 顽固拒绝改变方向。它是对 persistence 的负面读法，抽掉了美德成分。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: sistere 'stand', per- 'thoroughly', the sistere family (assist, insist, resist), the 15th-century noun, and the perseverance contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：sistere“站立”、per-“彻底”、sistere 词族（assist、insist、resist）、15 世纪的名词，以及与 perseverance 的对比。

normal.en: Sistere is 'to stand': persistence is standing thoroughly, per- 'through', until the difficulty passes or gives way.
normal.cn: sistere 是“站立”：persistence 就是“彻底站住”，站到困难过去或让路为止。

normal.en: Assist, insist, resist, and consist all contain sistere: each is a different way of standing — beside, upon, against, together.
normal.cn: assist、insist、resist、consist 都含 sistere：每一种都是一种站法——旁边、上面、对面、一起。

normal.en: The same posture can be praised as persistence or blamed as obstinacy; the word alone does not decide which.
normal.cn: 同一个姿势可以被赞为坚持，也可以被斥为固执；单凭这个词决定不了哪一种。

normal.en: Perseverance is the near twin from perseverare; the meaning overlaps, but the Latin verb behind it is different.
normal.cn: perseverance 是来自 perseverare 的近亲双胞胎；意义重叠，背后的拉丁动词却不同。

normal.en: Computing keeps the lamp lit across a restart; that is data persistence, the same button held by code.
normal.cn: 计算机让灯跨过重启继续亮着；这就是数据持久化，同一颗按钮由代码按住。

abstract.en: A hand on a button in a dark room is not hope; it is the refusal to let the dark have the last word.
abstract.cn: 黑暗中按着按钮的手不是希望；它只是拒绝让黑暗说了算。

abstract.en: A tradition survives because each generation stands in the same place for a moment before stepping aside.
abstract.cn: 传统得以存续，是因为每一代都在同一个地方站一会儿，然后才让开。

abstract.en: A chemical that will not decay is a guest who never learns to leave.
abstract.cn: 不会降解的化学物质，是一个永远学不会离开的客人。

examples.en: Her persistence finally convinced the publisher to read the manuscript.
examples.cn: 她的坚持最终说服出版方读了那份手稿。

examples.en: The persistence of the drought forced the town to ration water.
examples.cn: 干旱持续不退，迫使小镇实行配给供水。

examples.en: The database guarantees persistence even if the power fails.
examples.cn: 即使断电，这个数据库也能保证数据持久保存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破西斯特恩斯」——破开阻力，像“西”装骑士一样一站到底，手一直按着不松 → persistence 坚持不懈；持续存在（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 persistere「坚定持续、站稳」，由 per-「彻底」+ sistere「站立」构成（*sta-「站立」词根），名词为 persistentia；后缀 -ence（拉丁 -entia）表状态。核心是「一只手一直按在按钮上，灯始终没灭」。同族含 persist、persistent、persistently；perseverance 出自另一动词 perseverare，resist、insist、assist 则共享 sistere 但前缀不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of persistence all describe a hand that keeps the lamp lit. What changes is why it stays: difficulty, mere duration, stubbornness, a restart, a pathogen, soil, the retina, memory, or a whole community across generations.
sensesIntro.cn: persistence 的九个义项都描述一只让灯持续亮着的手。变化的是它为什么还按着：困难、单纯的延续、固执、一次重启、病原体、土壤、视网膜、记忆，还是一个跨越世代的共同体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand held on a button, so that the lamp never goes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手一直按在按钮上，那盏灯始终没有灭。

branches.en: THE HAND AND ITS SHADOW: the praised virtue of continuing against difficulty, and the same posture read as stubbornness.
branches.cn: 手与它的影子：面对困难继续前行的受赞美德，以及同一姿势被读成固执。

branches.en: MERE CONTINUANCE: things, traditions, and species that simply fail to stop.
branches.cn: 单纯的延续：只是没有停下来的事物、传统与物种。

branches.en: TECHNICAL REMAINDER: data that survives a restart, and chemicals that refuse to break down.
branches.cn: 技术性的留存：挺过重启的数据，以及拒绝分解的化学物质。

branches.en: THE BODY'S GUEST: a pathogen or symptom that stays after it should have left.
branches.cn: 身体里的客人：本该离开之后仍留下的病原体或症状。

branches.en: THE AFTERGLOW: an image left on the retina, and a memory that keeps returning to mind.
branches.cn: 余辉：留在视网膜上的影像，以及不断回到心头的记忆。

intro.en: Persistence is persist plus -ence, from Latin -entia, a state noun. Persist is Latin persistere, per- 'thoroughly' + sistere 'stand'. The same sistere carries assist, insist, resist, and consist, so the family reads like a set of standing postures.
intro.cn: persistence 是 persist 加 -ence（拉丁 -entia，状态名词）。persist 是拉丁 persistere，即 per-“彻底”+ sistere“站立”。同一个 sistere 还带着 assist、insist、resist、consist，所以这个词族读起来像一组站立的姿势。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is sistere 'to stand, place', persistere 'to stand firm', and persistentia 'constancy'. The root is PIE *sta- 'stand', which also gives English stand, stable, and statue.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 sistere“站立、放置”、persistere“站稳”、persistentia“恒心”。词根是原始印欧语 *sta-“站立”，它也产生英语 stand（站立）、stable（稳固）与 statue（雕像）。

items.meaning: the state of standing firm or continuing
items.meaningCN: 站稳或持续的状态（-ence 状态名词）
items.example: Persistence is often worth more than talent.
items.exampleCN: 坚持往往比天赋更值钱。

items.meaning: to stand firm, to continue
items.meaningCN: 站稳、持续（per- 彻底 + sistere 站立）
items.example: The problem persisted for a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题持续了十年。

items.meaning: standing firm; continuing
items.meaningCN: 站稳的；持续的（-ent 分词形容词词尾）
items.example: A persistent cough sent him to the clinic.
items.exampleCN: 持续的咳嗽让他去了诊所。

items.meaning: in a continuing manner
items.meaningCN: 以持续不断的方式
items.example: She persistently asked for the records.
items.exampleCN: 她一再要求查看记录。

items.meaning: the older doublet of persistence
items.meaningCN: persistence 的较早异体
items.example: The coating's persistency was tested in salt water.
items.exampleCN: 这种涂层的持久性在盐水中接受了测试。

items.meaning: to stand by someone, hence to help
items.meaningCN: 站在某人旁边，因而表示帮助（ad- 向 + sistere 站立）
items.example: A nurse assisted during the procedure.
items.exampleCN: 一名护士在手术过程中协助。

items.meaning: to stand upon something, hence to demand
items.meaningCN: 站在某物之上，因而表示坚持要求（in- 在上 + sistere 站立）
items.example: He insisted on paying for the meal.
items.exampleCN: 他坚持要付这顿饭钱。

items.meaning: to stand against
items.meaningCN: 站在对立面；抵抗（re- 对抗 + sistere 站立）
items.example: The material resists heat well.
items.exampleCN: 这种材料耐热性很好。

items.meaning: not remaining for long
items.meaningCN: 不长时间留存的（non- 否定）
items.example: Nonpersistent chemicals break down within weeks.
items.exampleCN: 非持久性化学物质在数周内分解。

latinEntries.meaning: to cause to stand, to place, to stand firm

definition_zh: 坚持不懈的；执着的；持续的；连绵不断的；反复出现的；顽固的；难以消除的；持久性的；长期存续的
definition_en: continuing firmly despite difficulty, or continuing to exist, appear, or remain far longer than expected, whether of a person, a symptom, a smell, a chemical, or stored data
core_image: 那颗按钮被一直按着，所以灯始终亮着，谁也没能把它关掉
scene: 楼道尽头那盏灯坏了三个月还没修，每次经过都还亮着。The lamp at the end of the hall has been a persistent fault for three months.
sceneCN: 这里 persistent 是「反复出现的、挥之不去的」（第 3 个义项：问题一再出现、始终没有消失）；句意：走廊尽头那盏灯是个持续了三个月的反复故障。

pos.zh: 坚持不懈的；持续的；反复出现的；顽固的；持久性的

derivatives.zh: 坚持不懈；持续存在；持久性

senses.title: Refusing to give up
senses.definition: of a person, continuing firmly with an aim despite obstacles, rejection, or repeated failure
senses.definitionCN: 指人面对障碍、拒绝或反复失败仍坚定继续追求目标
senses.example: A persistent student kept coming back until the proof worked.
senses.exampleCN: 一个不肯放弃的学生一次次回来，直到证明走通。
senses.why: Persistent is the present participle of persistere, 'standing thoroughly'. The adjective describes the hand that has not lifted from the button, not the difficulty it faces.
senses.whyCN: persistent 是 persistere“彻底站住”的现在分词。这个形容词描述的是那只还没有离开按钮的手，而不是它面对的困难。

senses.title: Continuing without a break
senses.definition: of a condition, sound, or process, continuing over a long period without stopping
senses.definitionCN: 指状况、声音或过程在长时间内不断持续
senses.example: A persistent hum came from the transformer all night.
senses.exampleCN: 变压器的持续嗡鸣响了一整夜。
senses.why: Here the light simply stays on. No struggle and no praise: the adjective measures duration, and persistent becomes close to continuous.
senses.whyCN: 这里的灯只是持续亮着。没有挣扎也没有赞许：形容词衡量的是时长，persistent 因此接近 continuous。

senses.title: Coming back again and again
senses.definition: of a problem, symptom, rumour, or error, appearing repeatedly and refusing to go away
senses.definitionCN: 指问题、症状、传闻或错误反复出现、不肯消失
senses.example: The persistent leak was traced to a hairline crack.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反复出现的渗漏最终被追查到一条细裂缝。
senses.why: The button is being pressed again each time the fault returns. The adjective marks the repetition, not the length, which is why a persistent cough can be short and a persistent rumour can be old.
senses.whyCN: 每次故障回来，按钮就被再按一次。这个形容词标记的是重复而非长度，所以 persistent 的咳嗽可以很短，persistent 的传闻可以很旧。

senses.title: Hard to remove
senses.definition: of a stain, smell, habit, or stain-like thing, remaining despite attempts to remove or change it
senses.definitionCN: 指污渍、气味或习惯在试图去除或改变之后仍然存在
senses.example: A persistent smell of smoke stayed in the curtains for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘上的烟味挥之不去，持续了好几周。
senses.why: Some lamps cannot be switched off by ordinary means. This sense stresses resistance to cleaning or correction, with the same image of a light that keeps burning.
senses.whyCN: 有些灯用普通办法关不掉。这个义项强调对清洁或纠正的抵抗，意象仍是那盏一直烧着的灯。

senses.title: Remaining in the environment
senses.definition: of a chemical or pollutant, remaining in soil, water, or organisms for a long time without breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 指化学品或污染物在土壤、水体或生物体内长期存在而不分解
senses.example: Persistent pesticides accumulate up the food chain.
senses.exampleCN: 持久性农药会沿食物链逐级累积。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the duration sense and made it a measurable property. The lamp refuses to go out, and the measure of that refusal becomes an environmental warning.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了持续义，并把它变成可测量的属性。灯拒绝熄灭，这种拒绝的程度就成了环境警告。

senses.title: Stored beyond the session
senses.definition: of data or an object in computing, remaining stored after a program, session, or device stops
senses.definitionCN: 指数据或对象在程序、会话或设备停止后仍被保存
senses.example: Persistent storage keeps the user's settings after a reboot.
senses.exampleCN: 持久化存储让用户的设置在重启后仍然保留。
senses.why: Memory loses its light when the power ends; persistent storage is built so the button is held by something slower and more permanent than electricity.
senses.whyCN: 内存断电就失去光；持久化存储的设计让按钮被某种比电更慢、更永久的东西按住。

senses.title: A symptom that will not settle
senses.definition: of a medical sign, infection, or pain, continuing longer than expected or returning after treatment
senses.definitionCN: 指医学体征、感染或疼痛持续超过预期，或治疗之后再次出现
senses.example: Persistent fever for more than a week needs investigation.
senses.exampleCN: 持续一周以上的发热需要进一步检查。
senses.why: The body's lamp stays lit after the illness should have ended. Medicine uses the adjective to separate a passing reaction from a state that has taken up residence.
senses.whyCN: 身体的灯在本该结束之后仍亮着。医学用这个形容词把一时的反应与已经“住下来”的状态分开。

senses.title: Refusing to be put off
senses.definition: of a person's manner, continuing to ask, demand, or appear despite hints that they should stop
senses.definitionCN: 指人的举止，在别人暗示应当停止时仍继续询问、要求或出现
senses.example: The persistent salesman called four times in one week.
senses.exampleCN: 那个纠缠不休的推销员一周打了四次电话。
senses.why: The same standing posture, now seen from the receiving side. Persistence is virtue when you want the goal; persistent is annoying when you are the obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 同一个站立的姿势，现在从被面对的一方来看。当目标是你要的，坚持是美德；当你就是障碍时，persistent 就很烦人。

senses.title: Lasting across generations
senses.definition: of a tradition, belief, species, or pattern, surviving over a very long period despite pressure to disappear
senses.definitionCN: 指传统、信念、物种或模式在消失的压力下仍长期存续
senses.example: The persistent custom survived two centuries of migration.
senses.exampleCN: 这个长存的习俗挺过了两个世纪的迁徙。
senses.why: The largest lamp again: a whole pattern stays lit. Persistent here is measured in generations, and the hand on the button is a community that keeps passing it on.
senses.whyCN: 又是最大的一盏灯：一整套模式持续亮着。这里的 persistent 以世代计量，按住按钮的是不断把它传下去的共同体。

intro.en: Persistent is the English adjective from Latin persistens, the present participle of persistere 'to stand firm, continue'. Persistere is per- 'thoroughly' plus sistere 'to stand'. The adjective entered English in the 16th century, first for persons and opinions, then spreading in the 19th and 20th centuries to symptoms, chemicals, and computer storage.
intro.cn: persistent 是来自拉丁语 persistens 的英语形容词，即 persistere“站稳、持续”的现在分词。persistere 是 per-“彻底”加 sistere“站立”。这个形容词在 16 世纪进入英语，最早用于人与意见，19 至 20 世纪扩展到症状、化学品与计算机存储。

items.en: Sistere 'to stand, to place' comes from the reconstructed PIE form *sta- 'to stand'. The prefix per- 'thoroughly' makes persistere 'to stand through to the end'.
items.cn: sistere“站立、放置”出自原始印欧语的重构形式 *sta-“站立”。前缀 per-“彻底”使 persistere 成为“站到最后”。

items.en: The present participle persistens, persistentem supplies English with both persistent and, through the noun persistentia, persistence. The two words entered English on parallel tracks rather than one from the other.
items.cn: 现在分词 persistens、persistentem 同时为英语提供 persistent 与（经名词 persistentia 的）persistence。这两个词是平行进入英语的，而不是一个由另一个派生。

items.en: English persistent first describes people and opinions that hold their ground. The tone can be admiring or critical depending on the sentence.
items.cn: 英语 persistent 最早描述守住立场的人与意见。语气可褒可贬，取决于句子。

items.en: Medicine and chemistry adopt it for symptoms and substances that stay: persistent fever, persistent odour, persistent dyes.
items.cn: 19 世纪医学与化学用它描述滞留的症状与物质：持续发热、挥之不去的气味、不易褪色的染料。

items.en: Computing adds persistent storage and persistent connections; environmental science fixes the phrase persistent organic pollutants.
items.cn: 20 世纪计算机加入持久化存储与持久连接；环境科学固定了“持久性有机污染物”这一说法。

items.en: Perseverant looks like a twin but comes from perseverare, a different Latin verb. Persistent is the participle of persistere; the two overlap in meaning without sharing a formation.
items.cn: perseverant 看起来像双胞胎，却来自另一个拉丁动词 perseverare。persistent 是 persistere 的分词；两者意义重叠，构词却不同。

note.en: The first group separates the adjective from its noun family and from two near neighbours built differently. The second group compares continual, continuous, stubborn, and lingering.
note.cn: 第一组把形容词与其名词词族分开，并区分两个构词不同的近邻。第二组比较 continual、continuous、stubborn、lingering。

entries.definition: the state of standing firm or continuing. It names the quality; persistent describes the thing that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 站稳或持续的状态。它命名品质，persistent 描述具有该品质的事物。

entries.definition: to continue firmly or keep existing. It is the verb behind the participle.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定继续或持续存在。它是分词背后的动词。

entries.definition: steadfast in a course of action, from Latin perseverare. It overlaps in meaning but is not the participle of persistere.
entries.definitionCN: 在行动道路上坚定不移的，出自拉丁 perseverare。意义重叠，却不是 persistere 的分词。

entries.definition: to stand against. It shares sistere 'stand' but points the posture in the opposite direction.
entries.definitionCN: 站在对立面；抵抗。它共享 sistere“站立”，却把姿势指向相反方向。

entries.definition: happening repeatedly over a period, often with interruptions. It fits a recurring cough or complaint better than an unbroken hum.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时间内反复发生，常有中断。它更适合反复的咳嗽或抱怨，而不是不间断的嗡鸣。

entries.definition: going on without any interruption. It covers the unbroken hum and the unbroken line, but not the stubborn person.
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何中断地持续。它适用于不间断的嗡鸣与不断的线，却不适用于固执的人。

entries.definition: unwilling to change one's attitude or course. It is the personal sense of persistent, usually with disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿改变态度或方向。它是 persistent 的个人义，通常带不赞成的语气。

entries.definition: remaining slowly after the cause has gone, as a smell or doubt. It stresses the slowness of departure rather than the strength of staying.
entries.definitionCN: 在成因消失后缓慢地残留，如气味或疑虑。它强调离开得慢，而不是留得有力。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: sistere 'stand', per- 'thoroughly', the participle persistens, the 16th-century entry, and the parallel noun persistence.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：sistere“站立”、per-“彻底”、分词 persistens、16 世纪的进入，以及平行的名词 persistence。

normal.en: Persistent is the standing participle: someone or something is standing thoroughly in place, and has not lifted the hand.
normal.cn: persistent 是“站立”的分词：某人或某物彻底站在原地，还没有把手拿开。

normal.en: It entered English in the 16th century for people, then moved to fevers, smells, and chemicals that also refuse to leave.
normal.cn: 它在 16 世纪先用于人，后来转到同样不肯离开的发热、气味与化学品。

normal.en: Persistent and persistence came into English on parallel tracks from the same Latin verb, not one from the other.
normal.cn: persistent 与 persistence 是从同一个拉丁动词平行进入英语的，并不是一个由另一个派生。

normal.en: Continual means repeated with gaps; continuous means without a break; persistent can mean either, depending on what it describes.
normal.cn: continual 指有间隔的重复；continuous 指没有中断；persistent 视所修饰的对象，两者都可以指。

normal.en: The same word praises a student and complains about a salesman; only the sentence decides which reading wins.
normal.cn: 同一个词既赞美学生，也抱怨推销员；只有句子能决定哪一种读法胜出。

abstract.en: A lamp that stays on after everyone has left is either a comfort or a waste, depending on who is paying.
abstract.cn: 所有人都离开后还亮着的灯，可能是安慰，也可能是浪费，取决于谁付电费。

abstract.en: A rumour is persistent because it asks nothing of the people who repeat it.
abstract.cn: 传闻之所以挥之不去，是因为它对传播它的人毫无要求。

abstract.en: A tradition survives by being boring enough to repeat and useful enough to keep.
abstract.cn: 传统之所以存续，是因为它无聊到可以重复，又有用到值得保留。

examples.en: The persistent noise from the fridge turned out to be a loose fan.
examples.cn: 冰箱那持续不断的噪音，最后查出来是风扇松了。

examples.en: Persistent organic pollutants travel thousands of kilometres.
examples.cn: 持久性有机污染物会迁移数千公里。

examples.en: She was persistent enough to get the archive opened after hours.
examples.cn: 她够执着，让档案馆在下班后重新开门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破西斯特恩特」——破了阻力还“死”站着不走，像钉子一样钉在原地 → persistent 坚持不懈的；持续不退的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 persistens，即 persistere「站稳、持续」的现在分词，由 per-「彻底」+ sistere「站立」构成（*sta-「站立」词根）；后缀 -ent 为拉丁分词词尾。核心是「按钮一直被按着，灯始终亮着」。同族含 persist、persistence、persistently；perseverant 出自另一动词 perseverare。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of persistent all describe a lamp that stays lit. What changes is what keeps it burning: a person's will, a condition's duration, a fault's return, a stain's resistance, a chemical's half-life, a disk, a symptom, a salesman, or a tradition.
sensesIntro.cn: persistent 的九个义项都描述一盏持续亮着的灯。变化的是谁让它烧着：人的意志、状况的时长、故障的回归、污渍的抵抗、化学品的半衰期、一块磁盘、一个症状、一个推销员，还是一项传统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a button held down so the lamp stays lit, and no ordinary attempt can switch it off.
core.cn: 核心意象：按钮被一直按着，灯始终亮着，普通的办法都关不掉。

branches.en: THE HOLDING PERSON: the admiring and the annoying readings of the same upright posture.
branches.cn: 按住的人：同一个挺立姿势的赞美读法与烦人读法。

branches.en: THE STUBBORN LIGHT: unbroken duration, repeated return, and resistance to removal.
branches.cn: 倔强的光：不间断的时长、反复的回归，以及对去除的抵抗。

branches.en: TECHNICAL STAYING: pollutants that will not break down, and data that survives a restart.
branches.cn: 技术性的停留：不分解的污染物，以及挺过重启的数据。

branches.en: THE BODY: a fever or infection that outlasts its expected course.
branches.cn: 身体：超过预期病程的发热或感染。

branches.en: THE LONGEST LIGHT: a custom or species carried across generations.
branches.cn: 最长的光：跨越世代被传下去的习惯或物种。

intro.en: Persistent is persist plus -ent, the Latin present-participle ending. Persist is persistere, per- 'thoroughly' + sistere 'stand'. The family includes the noun persistence, the adverb persistently, and the sistere clan: assist, insist, resist, consist.
intro.cn: persistent 是 persist 加 -ent，即拉丁现在分词词尾。persist 是 persistere，即 per-“彻底”+ sistere“站立”。词族包含名词 persistence、副词 persistently，以及 sistere 家族：assist、insist、resist、consist。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is sistere 'stand', persistere 'stand firm', and the participle persistens. The root *sta- 'stand' also gives English stand, stable, station, and statue.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 sistere“站立”、persistere“站稳”、分词 persistens。词根 *sta-“站立”还产生英语 stand（站立）、stable（稳固）、station（站点）与 statue（雕像）。

items.meaning: standing firm, continuing
items.meaningCN: 站稳的、持续的（-ent 分词词尾）
items.example: A persistent infection needs a longer course.
items.exampleCN: 持续不退的感染需要更长的疗程。

items.meaning: to keep standing, to continue
items.meaningCN: 继续站立、持续
items.example: The custom persisted into the next century.
items.exampleCN: 这个习俗延续到了下个世纪。

items.meaning: the state of continuing
items.meaningCN: 持续的状态；坚持不懈
items.example: Persistence carried the project to the end.
items.exampleCN: 坚持把项目带到了终点。

items.meaning: in a continuing manner
items.meaningCN: 以持续不断的方式
items.example: He persistently ignored the warnings.
items.exampleCN: 他一再无视警告。

items.meaning: the older doublet of persistence
items.meaningCN: persistence 的较早异体
items.example: The persistency of the dye was tested.
items.exampleCN: 这种染料的持久性接受了测试。

items.meaning: to stand by, to help
items.meaningCN: 站在旁边；帮助
items.example: Two volunteers assisted with the survey.
items.exampleCN: 两名志愿者协助了这项调查。

items.meaning: to stand upon, to demand
items.meaningCN: 站在上面；坚持要求
items.example: She insisted that the figures be checked.
items.exampleCN: 她坚持要核对数字。

items.meaning: to stand against
items.meaningCN: 站在对立面；抵抗
items.example: The coating resists salt water.
items.exampleCN: 这层涂层耐盐水。

items.meaning: not lasting long
items.meaningCN: 不长久留存的
items.example: Nonpersistent toxins clear within days.
items.exampleCN: 非持久性毒素在几天内就会清除。

definition_zh: 哲学的；哲学家的；达观的；冷静克制的；哲理性的；理论的；探究根本原理的；某一哲学流派的；关于人生根本问题的
definition_en: relating to philosophy or its methods, or describing a calm, accepting attitude toward difficulty, especially one reached by thinking about what matters most
core_image: 站在城邦广场上，不急着做事，先追问“这到底是什么、为什么”
scene: 项目失败后，别人都在追责，他只是把杯子放下，问大家到底想做成什么。He stayed calm and asked what they really wanted to build; his attitude was philosophical.
sceneCN: 这里 philosophical 是「达观的、看得开的」（第 3 个义项：面对失败仍能平静接受并退一步思考）；句意：他保持平静，转而追问大家真正想做成什么，这种态度很达观。

pos.zh: 哲学的；哲学家的；达观的；冷静的；哲理性的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 进行哲学思考；空谈哲理
语文学；文献学（philos 与 logos 的组合）

senses.title: Belonging to philosophy
senses.definition: relating to philosophy as a discipline, its questions, texts, and methods
senses.definitionCN: 与哲学作为一门学科、其问题、文本与方法有关的
senses.example: The book is a philosophical study of time, not a physics text.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是对时间的哲学研究，不是物理学教材。
senses.why: Greek philosophia is philos 'loving' plus sophia 'wisdom'. The adjective marks whatever belongs to that love of wisdom as a formal pursuit, with its own texts and arguments.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 philosophia 是 philos“爱”加 sophia“智慧”。这个形容词标记的是属于这种对智慧之爱的一切，作为一门有文本、有论证的正式学问。

senses.title: Of a philosopher or a philosopher's work
senses.titleCN: 哲学家的或哲学著作的
senses.definition: characteristic of a philosopher, or of the kind of writing and reasoning a philosopher produces
senses.definitionCN: 具有哲学家特征的，或具有哲学家所写、所论之作品特征的
senses.example: He answered in a philosophical tone, defining each word before using it.
senses.exampleCN: 他用哲学家的口吻回答，每用一个词之前先定义它。
senses.why: The adjective can move from the field to the person. A philosophical manner is one that treats the conversation as a place where terms must be fixed before anything can be claimed.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以从学科转到人身上。哲学家的作风，是把谈话当作必须先固定术语、然后才能下结论的场所。

senses.title: Accepting what cannot be changed
senses.titleCN: 接受无法改变之事的达观
senses.definition: calm and accepting about a loss or failure, especially after reflecting on what really matters
senses.definitionCN: 对损失或失败保持平静与接受，尤指在思考过真正重要的是什么之后
senses.example: She was philosophical about losing the race: the training mattered more.
senses.exampleCN: 她对输掉比赛很看得开：训练本身更重要。
senses.why: This is the philosopher's calm taken into daily life. The person steps back from the result, asks what it was for, and the loss becomes smaller than the question.
senses.whyCN: 这是把哲学家的平静带进日常生活。人从结果退后一步，追问它究竟为了什么，于是损失变得比那个问题更小。

senses.title: Calm under pressure
senses.definition: remaining composed and reasonable when others are agitated, especially in a crisis
senses.definitionCN: 在他人焦躁时仍保持沉着与讲理，尤指在危机中
senses.example: His philosophical response cooled the argument in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他冷静的回应让屋里的争论降温了。
senses.why: The same distance from results becomes a social skill. A philosophical face does not deny the problem; it refuses to let the problem set the tone.
senses.whyCN: 同一种与结果保持距离的能力变成一种社交本领。哲学式的面孔不否认问题存在，只是拒绝让问题决定语气。

senses.title: Carrying a deeper thought
senses.definition: of a remark, story, or work, containing a general reflection on life or human nature rather than only a fact
senses.definitionCN: 指言论、故事或作品含有对人生或人性的普遍思考，而不只是陈述事实
senses.example: The novel's ending is philosophical without being preachy.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的结尾有哲理性，却不显得说教。
senses.why: A sentence can carry a whole argument inside it. When an ordinary observation opens onto a general question, the adjective says that the smaller thing has become a window.
senses.whyCN: 一句话里可以装下一整套论证。当日常观察通向一个普遍问题时，这个形容词就表示那小事物变成了一扇窗。

senses.title: Theoretical rather than practical
senses.titleCN: 理论层面的而非实用的
senses.definition: concerned with abstract reasoning about a question rather than with its immediate practical solution
senses.definitionCN: 关注对问题的抽象推理，而不是它的直接实际解决
senses.example: Whether the machine can think is a philosophical question for now.
senses.exampleCN: 机器能否思考，目前还是一个理论层面的问题。
senses.why: The philosopher is not paid to fix the machine. This sense marks the distance from action, and it can be a compliment or a complaint depending on who needs the answer.
senses.whyCN: 哲学家并不负责修机器。这个义项标记的是与行动之间的距离，它可以是赞美，也可以是抱怨，取决于谁需要答案。

senses.title: Concerned with underlying principles
senses.definition: relating to the basic assumptions or principles beneath a practice, science, or institution
senses.definitionCN: 与实践、科学或制度底下的基本假设或原理有关的
senses.example: The reform raised philosophical questions about who owns the data.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革提出了关于数据归谁所有的根本原理问题。
senses.why: Every practice rests on assumptions it does not examine. The adjective points to that layer, the place where the ground of an argument is checked rather than used.
senses.whyCN: 每一种实践都建立在它自己不检查的假设上。这个形容词指向那一层，即论证的地基被核查而不是被使用的地方。

senses.title: Belonging to a particular school
senses.definition: relating to a specific tradition or school of philosophy, such as Stoic, Kantian, or Buddhist
senses.definitionCN: 与某一特定哲学传统或流派有关的，如斯多葛派、康德学派或佛教哲学
senses.example: The two authors come from very different philosophical backgrounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这两位作者来自非常不同的哲学背景。
senses.why: The love of wisdom has many households. Once a school forms, the adjective can name its address, and an argument becomes identifiable by the family it belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 对智慧的爱有许多户人家。一旦某个学派形成，这个形容词就能标明它的住址，一个论证也就可以凭所属家族被辨认出来。

senses.title: About the deepest human questions
senses.definition: relating to questions about existence, meaning, death, truth, or how one should live
senses.definitionCN: 与存在、意义、死亡、真理或人应当如何生活有关的问题
senses.example: Grief made the question of time feel philosophical rather than practical.
senses.exampleCN: 悲伤让时间的问题显得关乎人生根本，而不只是实用安排。
senses.why: Some questions cannot be settled by measurement. The adjective marks the point where a practical problem turns into a question about what a life is for.
senses.whyCN: 有些问题无法靠测量解决。这个形容词标记的是那个转折点：一个实际问题变成了关于人生为了什么的问题。

intro.en: Philosophical comes from Greek philosophikos, from philosophia 'love of wisdom', built on philos 'loving, dear' and sophia 'wisdom, skill'. English took the adjective through Latin philosophicus in the 16th century, alongside the noun philosophy. The older form philosophic still exists, and the -al form became the everyday adjective.
intro.cn: philosophical 来自希腊语 philosophikos，出自 philosophia“对智慧的爱”，由 philos“爱、亲爱的”与 sophia“智慧、技艺”构成。英语在 16 世纪经拉丁 philosophicus 借入这个形容词，同时借入名词 philosophy。更早的形式 philosophic 仍然存在，而 -al 形式成为日常形容词。

items.en: Philos means 'loving, dear, friendly', the same word used for a friend. Sophia means 'wisdom, cleverness, skill'. Philosophia is literally 'the love of wisdom', not 'the possession of it'.
items.cn: philos 意为“爱的、亲爱的、友好的”，也用来指朋友。sophia 意为“智慧、聪明、技艺”。philosophia 字面是“对智慧的爱”，而不是“拥有智慧”。

items.en: Philosophos, 'a lover of wisdom', is said to have been used by Pythagoras, and the noun philosophia appears in Greek prose by the 5th century BC.
items.cn: philosophos“爱智慧的人”据说由毕达哥拉斯使用，名词 philosophia 在公元前 5 世纪的希腊散文中已经出现。

items.en: English borrows philosophical through Latin philosophicus. Early uses cover natural philosophy, which we would now call science, because both were reasoned inquiry into nature.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪经拉丁 philosophicus 借入 philosophical。早期用法涵盖“自然哲学”，也就是今天的科学，因为两者都是对自然的推理探究。

items.en: The word narrows to the discipline of philosophy as the sciences separate from it, and the figurative sense 'calm about outcomes' develops in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 随着科学从哲学中分离，这个词缩小到哲学学科；比喻义“对结果平静接受”则在日常语言中发展出来。

items.en: The ending -ical is Greek -ikos through Latin -icus, with -al added in English. Philosophic and philosophical mean the same; the longer form simply won the everyday slot.
items.cn: 词尾 -ical 是希腊 -ikos 经拉丁 -icus，再在英语中加 -al。philosophic 与 philosophical 意思相同，只是较长形式占了日常用法。

items.en: Philology also begins with philos, but its second element is logos 'word, reason', so it means 'love of words'. Philanthropy is philos plus anthropos 'humanity'. Only philosophy has sophia inside.
items.cn: philology 也以 philos 开头，但第二部分是 logos“言词、理性”，所以意为“爱言辞”。philanthropy 是 philos 加 anthropos“人类”。只有 philosophy 内部是 sophia。

note.en: The first group separates the philosophy family from two words that share only the philos half. The second group compares thoughtful, stoical, academic, and abstract, the four adjectives most often used in philosophical's place.
note.cn: 第一组把哲学词族与两个只共享 philos 一半的词分开。第二组比较 thoughtful、stoical、academic、abstract，这四个形容词最常被用来替代 philosophical。

entries.definition: the love and study of wisdom, or a person's set of beliefs about life. Philosophical is its adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 对智慧的热爱与研究，或一个人对人生的整套信条。philosophical 是它的形容词。

entries.definition: a lover of wisdom, or a person who studies philosophy. The -er marks the person; -ical marks the belonging.
entries.definitionCN: 爱智慧的人，或研究哲学的人。-er 标记人，-ical 标记归属。

entries.definition: the study of language and texts. It shares philos 'loving' but replaces sophia with logos 'word', so it is love of words, not of wisdom.
entries.definitionCN: 对语言与文本的研究。它共享 philos“爱”，却把 sophia 换成 logos“言词”，所以爱的是言辞而非智慧。

entries.definition: the giving of money or help to good causes. It shares philos but its second element is anthropos 'human being', so it means love of humanity.
entries.definitionCN: 向公益事业捐钱或提供帮助。它共享 philos，但第二部分是 anthropos“人”，所以意为对人类的爱。

entries.definition: showing care for others, or given to careful thinking. It is warmer and more social than philosophical, which stresses reasoning about principles.
entries.definitionCN: 体贴他人的，或善于深思的。它比 philosophical 更温暖、更社会性，后者强调对原理的推理。

entries.definition: enduring pain or loss without complaint, after the Stoic school. It is the emotional sense of philosophical, but narrower and more severe.
entries.definitionCN: 不抱怨地忍受痛苦或损失，源自斯多葛学派。它是 philosophical 的情感义，但更窄、更严厉。

entries.definition: relating to schools, universities, or scholarly research. It covers the setting, while philosophical covers the kind of question asked.
entries.definitionCN: 与学校、大学或学术研究有关的。它覆盖场景，而 philosophical 覆盖提问的种类。

entries.definition: concerned with general ideas rather than concrete cases. It is the theoretical side of philosophical, but without the love-of-wisdom image.
entries.definitionCN: 关注一般观念而非具体事例。它是 philosophical 的理论一面，却没有“爱智慧”的意象。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: philos 'loving', sophia 'wisdom', the 16th-century Latin route, the philosophic variant, and the logos/anthropos traps.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：philos“爱”、sophia“智慧”、16 世纪的拉丁路径、philosophic 异体，以及 logos 与 anthropos 陷阱。

normal.en: Philosophia is the love of wisdom, not wisdom itself: the adjective describes anything that belongs to that pursuit.
normal.cn: philosophia 是对智慧的爱，而不是智慧本身：这个形容词描述属于这种追求的一切。

normal.en: Philos also gives philanthropy 'love of humanity' and philology 'love of words'; only philosophy has sophia in the middle.
normal.cn: philos 还产生 philanthropy“爱人类”与 philology“爱言辞”；只有 philosophy 中间是 sophia。

normal.en: In the 16th century natural philosophy still included what we now call physics, which is why old texts use philosophical for scientific inquiry.
normal.cn: 16 世纪的自然哲学仍包含今天的物理学，所以旧文本用 philosophical 指科学探究。

normal.en: Philosophic and philosophical are the same adjective; the longer one simply became the everyday choice.
normal.cn: philosophic 与 philosophical 是同一个形容词；较长的那个成了日常选择。

normal.en: Being philosophical about a loss means stepping back far enough to ask what the loss was for.
normal.cn: 对损失看得开，意思是退得足够远，好追问这场损失究竟为了什么。

abstract.en: The philosopher stands in the market and asks what money is, while the merchants keep trading.
abstract.cn: 哲学家站在集市上追问钱是什么，商人们则继续交易。

abstract.en: A calm face in a burning room is not indifference; it is a decision about which fire to fight first.
abstract.cn: 燃烧的房间里面孔平静不是冷漠；那是关于先扑哪一处火的决定。

abstract.en: A child asking why the sky is blue is doing philosophy with better questions than most adults.
abstract.cn: 一个追问天空为什么是蓝的孩子，提的问题比多数成年人更像哲学。

examples.en: They stayed up arguing a philosophical point about free will.
examples.cn: 他们熬夜争论一个关于自由意志的哲学问题。

examples.en: He was philosophical about the delay: the trains were beyond anyone's control.
examples.cn: 他对延误很看得开：火车的事谁也控制不了。

examples.en: The design rests on a philosophical belief about how people learn.
examples.cn: 这个设计建立在一种关于人如何学习的哲学信念之上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「菲洛索菲扣」——菲洛捧着书追着“索”要一个“菲”常根本的答案，先问为什么再动手 → philosophical 哲学的；达观的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 希腊 philosophia「对智慧的爱」，由 philos「爱、亲爱的」+ sophia「智慧」构成，形容词 philosophikos 经拉丁 philosophicus 进入英语；后缀 -ical（希腊 -ikos + 拉丁 -icus + 英语 -al）。核心是「不急着做事，先追问这到底是什么、为什么」。philology（philos + logos）与 philanthropy（philos + anthropos）只共享 philos，后半不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of philosophical all begin with a step back from action to ask what something really is. What changes is the distance: the discipline, the person, a loss accepted, a crisis calmed, a remark deepened, a theory defended, a foundation examined, a school joined, or a life questioned.
sensesIntro.cn: philosophical 的九个义项都从“退后一步、先追问这到底是什么”开始。变化的是距离：学科、人、被接受的损失、被平息的危机、被深化的言论、被辩护的理论、被核查的地基、所加入的学派，还是被追问的人生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing in the city square, not rushing to act, first asking what a thing is and why it is so.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在城邦广场上，不急着行动，先追问事物是什么、为何如此。

chain: AN ACTION IS ABOUT TO HAPPEN

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND ITS PEOPLE: the formal study of wisdom, and the manner of those who practise it.
branches.cn: 学科与从业者：对智慧的正式研究，以及实践这种研究者的作风。

branches.en: THE CALM DISTANCE: accepting a loss after reflection, and staying composed while others panic.
branches.cn: 平静的距离：在反思后接受损失，以及在他人慌乱时保持沉着。

branches.en: THE DEEPER WINDOW: a remark that opens onto life, and questions about existence, death, and meaning.
branches.cn: 更深的窗口：通向人生的言论，以及关于存在、死亡与意义的问题。

branches.en: THE THEORETICAL LAYER: questions removed from practice, and the basic assumptions beneath a practice.
branches.cn: 理论层：脱离实践的问题，以及实践底下的基本假设。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: an identifiable tradition with its own texts, terms, and arguments.
branches.cn: 学派：一个有自身文本、术语与论证的可辨识传统。

intro.en: Philosophical is Greek philosophikos plus English -al, or philosophy plus -ical. The compound is philos 'loving' + sophia 'wisdom'. English also keeps the shorter philosophic. The family extends through philosopher, philosophize, and the shared-philos words philology and philanthropy.
intro.cn: philosophical 是希腊 philosophikos 加英语 -al，或 philosophy 加 -ical。复合词是 philos“爱”+ sophia“智慧”。英语还保留较短的 philosophic。词族经 philosopher、philosophize 延伸，并有共享 philos 的 philology 与 philanthropy。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is philosophicus and philosophia, both borrowed from Greek. Latin added no new root: it only carried the Greek compound into European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 philosophicus 与 philosophia，两者都借自希腊语。拉丁语没有增加新词根，只是把这个希腊复合词运进欧洲各语言。

items.meaning: belonging to the love of wisdom
items.meaningCN: 属于对智慧之爱的（-ical 形容词词尾）
items.example: The debate raised a philosophical difficulty.
items.exampleCN: 这场辩论提出了一个哲学上的难题。

items.meaning: the love and study of wisdom
items.meaningCN: 对智慧的热爱与研究（philos 爱 + sophia 智慧）
items.example: Her philosophy of teaching is to ask before telling.
items.exampleCN: 她的教学信条是先问再讲。

items.meaning: a lover of wisdom
items.meaningCN: 爱智慧的人；哲学家
items.example: The philosopher wrote on friendship and time.
items.exampleCN: 这位哲学家写了关于友谊与时间的著作。

items.meaning: the shorter variant of philosophical
items.meaningCN: philosophical 的较短异体
items.example: The essay takes a philosophic view of failure.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章以哲学视角看待失败。

items.meaning: in philosophical terms, or calmly
items.meaningCN: 从哲学上，或达观地（-ly 副词）
items.example: She was philosophically prepared for bad news.
items.exampleCN: 她对坏消息在心理上做好了准备。

items.meaning: to reason or talk in a philosophical way
items.meaningCN: 以哲学方式思考或谈论（-ize 动词）
items.example: They philosophized until the café closed.
items.exampleCN: 他们一直谈哲理到咖啡馆关门。

items.meaning: the love and study of words and texts
items.meaningCN: 对语言与文本的热爱和研究；语文学（philos + logos）
items.example: Philology traces how a word changed across centuries.
items.exampleCN: 语文学追溯一个词在数百年间的变化。

items.meaning: love of humanity, shown by giving
items.meaningCN: 对人类的爱，以捐赠等方式体现；慈善（philos + anthropos）
items.example: The hospital was built by private philanthropy.
items.exampleCN: 这家医院由私人慈善捐助建成。

items.meaning: wisdom, cleverness, skill
items.meaningCN: 智慧、聪明、技艺
items.example: Philosophy joins philo- 'loving' with sophia 'wisdom'.
items.exampleCN: “哲学”一词把表示“爱”的 philo- 与表示“智慧”的 sophia 连在一起。

definition_zh: 身体上；体力上；体格上；物质上；按物理规律地；实际地；亲自地；在物理空间中地；有形地
definition_en: in a way that concerns the body, the material world, or the laws of physics, or in person rather than in thought or at a distance
core_image: 身体撞到墙时的那一声闷响，和随之而来的一阵疼
scene: 医生说这项检查要看他的体力，而不只是看化验单。The test asks whether he is physically able to lift those boxes.
sceneCN: 这里 physically 是「体力上」（第 2 个义项：就身体的力量与能力而言）；句意：这项检查要确认他在体力上能不能搬动那些箱子。

pos.zh: 身体上；体力上；物质上；按物理规律地；亲自地

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 身体的；物质的；物理的；体检

senses.title: In the body
senses.definition: in a way that involves or affects the body, as opposed to the mind or the emotions
senses.definitionCN: 以涉及或影响身体的方式，相对于心智或情感
senses.example: After the crash he was shaken but not physically hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 撞车之后他受了惊，但身体没有受伤。
senses.why: Greek physis is 'nature', the growing body. Physical first meant 'natural' and then 'bodily'; physically marks the place where the wall is met by flesh rather than by thought.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 physis 是“自然”，即生长着的身体。physical 先表示“自然的”，再表示“身体的”；physically 标记的是墙被肉而不是被思想撞到的那个地方。

senses.title: In terms of bodily strength
senses.definition: with regard to a person's strength, stamina, or ability to do bodily work
senses.definitionCN: 就一个人的力量、耐力或从事体力工作的能力而言
senses.example: The job is physically demanding but not technically hard.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作对体力要求高，技术上却不难。
senses.why: The body is also a tool with a capacity. This sense measures that capacity, which is why a task can be physically hard while being mentally easy.
senses.whyCN: 身体也是一件有容量的工具。这个义项测量这种容量，所以一项任务可以体力上很难、脑力上却很简单。

senses.title: In build or appearance
senses.definition: with regard to the shape, size, or visible condition of a person's body
senses.definitionCN: 就一个人身体的形状、大小或可见状态而言
senses.example: He looked physically stronger than he had in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他看起来比春天时体格更强壮。
senses.why: The wall's sound tells you something about the body that hit it. Here physically describes the body as an object others can see and measure.
senses.whyCN: 撞墙的声音能说明撞上去的身体是什么样。这里的 physically 把身体描述成他人能看见、能测量的对象。

senses.title: In the material world
senses.definition: in a material or tangible way, as opposed to symbolically, legally, or in thought
senses.definitionCN: 以物质的、可触摸的方式，相对于象征、法律或思想层面
senses.example: The two offices are physically separate but share one budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个办公室在物理空间上是分开的，却共用一份预算。
senses.why: From the body the word widens to matter in general. Anything that occupies space and can be bumped into counts as physically real, even if it is not alive.
senses.whyCN: 从身体开始，这个词扩展到一般物质。任何占据空间、能被撞到的东西都算物理上真实，即使它不是活的。

senses.title: According to the laws of physics
senses.definition: in a way that obeys, or is explained by, physical laws such as conservation of energy or causality
senses.definitionCN: 以遵守或被物理规律（如能量守恒或因果性）解释的方式
senses.example: A perpetual motion machine is physically impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 永动机在物理上是不可能的。
senses.why: Here the word invokes the discipline, not the body. Physically impossible means the wall cannot be walked through, no matter how strong the will.
senses.whyCN: 这里调用的是学科，而不是身体。physically impossible 意味着无论意志多强，墙都穿不过去。

senses.title: Actually, not merely on paper
senses.titleCN: 实际存在而非纸面上的
senses.definition: in actual fact, so that something exists or happens rather than being only planned or claimed
senses.definitionCN: 在事实上，使某物真实存在或发生，而不只是被计划或被声称
senses.example: The backup site exists physically, not only in the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 备份站点是实际存在的，不只存在于计划里。
senses.why: A plan is weightless. Physically real means the thing can be visited, weighed, or unplugged, which is the test the word applies to claims.
senses.whyCN: 计划没有重量。physically real 意味着这东西可以被走访、称重或拔掉电源，这就是这个词对声明所用的检验。

senses.title: In person, not remotely
senses.definition: by being present in the same place, rather than by phone, letter, or network
senses.definitionCN: 通过身处同一地点，而不是通过电话、信件或网络
senses.example: The witness must appear physically before the court.
senses.exampleCN: 证人必须亲自出庭。
senses.why: A voice on a wire has no body. Physically present restores the wall and the room: the person can be seen, touched, and held to account in one place.
senses.whyCN: 电线里的声音没有身体。physically present 把墙和房间还回来：人能被看见、被触到，并在同一个地方被追究。

senses.title: At a point in space
senses.definition: in a particular location in space, as opposed to being distributed, virtual, or undefined
senses.definitionCN: 位于空间中的某个特定位置，相对于分散、虚拟或位置不明
senses.example: The servers are physically in Frankfurt but logically in the cloud.
senses.exampleCN: 这些服务器物理上位于法兰克福，逻辑上却在“云”里。
senses.why: The word insists on coordinates. A cloud has no address until someone points to a building, and physically is the adverb that points.
senses.whyCN: 这个词坚持要坐标。云没有地址，直到有人指向一栋楼，而 physically 就是那只指过去的手。

senses.title: In a tangible form
senses.definition: in a form that can be touched or handled, such as a printed copy or a physical object
senses.definitionCN: 以能够触摸或拿取的形式，如印刷副本或实物
senses.example: The archive keeps the files physically as well as digitally.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆既保存数字文件，也保存实体文件。
senses.why: A file can be a ghost in a machine. Physically kept means there is paper you can drop, which is the oldest test of whether something is really there.
senses.whyCN: 文件可以是机器里的幽灵。以物理形态保存下来，意味着有可以掉在地上的纸，这是检验某物是否真的存在的最古老办法。

intro.en: Physically is physical plus -ly. Physical comes from Latin physicus 'natural, of nature', from Greek physikos, from physis 'nature'. Physis derives from phyein 'to bring forth, grow', so the oldest sense is not 'body' but 'what grows by itself'. English first used physical for medicine and natural things, then for the body, and only later for the science of physics.
intro.cn: physically 是 physical 加 -ly。physical 来自拉丁 physicus“自然的、属于自然的”，出自希腊 physikos，再上溯 physis“自然”。physis 又出自 phyein“产生、生长”，所以最古老的意义不是“身体”，而是“自己长出来的东西”。英语最早用 physical 指医药与自然事物，之后指身体，再往后才指物理学。

items.en: Physis means 'nature, natural form, growth'. The verb phyein means 'to bring forth, grow'. The physical is therefore first of all the growing world, not the body as opposed to the mind.
items.cn: physis 意为“自然、自然形态、生长”。动词 phyein 意为“产生、生长”。所以 physical 首先是生长着的世界，而不是与心智相对的身体。

items.en: Physicus in Latin means 'natural, of nature', and also 'a natural philosopher'. English physical enters in the 14th century with the sense 'medicinal, healing', since medicine studied natural bodies.
items.cn: 拉丁 physicus 意为“自然的、属于自然的”，也指“自然哲学家”。英语 physical 在 14 世纪进入，义为“医药的、治疗性的”，因为医学研究的是自然身体。

items.en: The sense 'bodily, of the body' becomes common, and the noun physics settles as the name of the science of matter and motion.
items.cn: “身体的、肉体的”这一义项在 16 世纪变得常见，名词 physics 则固定为研究物质与运动的科学名称。

items.en: Physically extends from the body to matter in general and to the laws of nature: physically impossible, physically separate.
items.cn: physically 从身体扩展到一般物质与自然规律：物理上不可能、物理上分开。

items.en: The adverb is the plain -ly form of physical. No new meaning is added: it turns 'of the body or of matter' into 'in the body or in matter'.
items.cn: 副词是 physical 的规则 -ly 形式。没有增加新意义：它把“身体或物质的”变成“在身体上或在物质中”。

items.en: Fiscal looks close but comes from Latin fiscus 'basket, treasury', so it means 'of public money'. Physique shares the physis root but names the shape of the body. Physician also shares physis, since medicine was the study of nature.
items.cn: fiscal 看起来相近，却来自拉丁 fiscus“篮子、国库”，所以意为“财政的”。physique 共享 physis 词根，却指身体的形状。physician 也共享 physis，因为医学本是对自然的研究。

note.en: The first group separates the physis family from the fiscal trap. The second group compares bodily, materially, tangibly, and actually, the four adverbs closest to physically.
note.cn: 第一组把 physis 词族与 fiscal 陷阱分开。第二组比较 bodily、materially、tangibly、actually，这四个副词最接近 physically。

entries.definition: relating to the body, to matter, or to physics. The adverb only turns this into a manner.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体、物质或物理学有关的。副词只是把它变成一种方式。

entries.definition: the shape and build of a person's body. It is a noun, so it names the body's form rather than a way of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人身体的形状与体格。它是名词，命名身体形态而非行为方式。

entries.definition: a doctor of medicine. It shares physis because medicine was once the study of natural bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 医生。它共享 physis，因为医学曾是对自然身体的研究。

entries.definition: relating to public money, taxes, and budgets. Its root is fiscus 'basket, treasury', so it has no bodily or physical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 与公共资金、税收和预算有关的。它的词根是 fiscus“篮子、国库”，所以没有身体或物理含义。

entries.definition: relating to the body, especially as opposed to the mind. It is narrower than physically, which also covers matter and physics.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体有关的，尤指相对于心智。它比 physically 窄，后者也覆盖物质与物理学。

entries.definition: in a way that concerns matter or material wealth. Its 'physical' sense is about stuff; its other sense is about money.
entries.definitionCN: 在涉及物质或物质财富的方式上。它的“物理”义关乎东西，另一义则关乎金钱。

entries.definition: in a way that can be touched or clearly perceived. It is the touchable side of physically, not the legal or logical one.
entries.definitionCN: 以可触摸或清楚感知的方式。它是 physically 可触摸的一面，而不是法律或逻辑的一面。

entries.definition: in fact, really. It contrasts with what is said or expected, while physically contrasts with what is mental or virtual.
entries.definitionCN: 事实上、真的。它与所言或所期待相对，而 physically 与心智或虚拟相对。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: physis 'nature', phyein 'grow', Latin physicus, the 14th-century medicinal sense, and the fiscus trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：physis“自然”、phyein“生长”、拉丁 physicus、14 世纪的医药义，以及 fiscus 陷阱。

normal.en: Physis is 'nature, growth': physical first meant 'natural', and only later 'bodily'.
normal.cn: physis 是“自然、生长”：physical 先表示“自然的”，后来才表示“身体的”。

normal.en: The adverb is just -ly: physically means 'in the body or in matter', the same relation with a different position.
normal.cn: 副词只是 -ly：physically 意为“在身体上或在物质中”，关系相同，位置不同。

normal.en: Medicine gave the word its early home, which is why physician and physical share a root.
normal.cn: 医学给了这个词早期归宿，所以 physician 与 physical 共享词根。

normal.en: A plan has no weight; physically real means you can go there and put your hand on it.
normal.cn: 计划没有重量；physically real 意味着你能走过去把手放上去。

normal.en: Fiscal looks like a cousin but comes from fiscus 'treasury'; money is not matter.
normal.cn: fiscal 看起来像表亲，却出自 fiscus“国库”；钱不是物质。

abstract.en: The sound of a body hitting a wall is the oldest proof that there is a wall.
abstract.cn: 身体撞上墙的声音，是“墙确实存在”最古老的证据。

abstract.en: A voice on a wire can lie about where it is; a body in a chair cannot.
abstract.cn: 电线里的声音可以谎报自己在哪；椅子上的身体不行。

abstract.en: A cloud is a place until someone asks where its buildings are.
abstract.cn: 云是一个地方，直到有人问它的楼在哪里。

examples.en: The tablet is physically identical to the one sold last year.
examples.cn: 这台平板与去年出售的那台在物理上完全相同。

examples.en: She was physically exhausted after the climb.
examples.cn: 爬完之后她身体极度疲惫。

examples.en: The director was physically present at the signing.
examples.cn: 签署时董事亲自到场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「菲兹克利」——身体“菲”常实在地撞到墙上，发出一声“兹”，疼是真的 → physically 身体上；物质上；物理上（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 physicus「自然的」，出自希腊 physikos 与 physis「自然」，再上溯 phyein「产生、生长」；后缀 -ly 构成副词。核心是「身体撞到墙时那声闷响，以及随之而来的疼」。同族含 physical、physics、physique、physician；fiscal（fiscus「国库」）只是形近，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of physically all begin with a body meeting the world. What changes is the aspect in view: the flesh, the strength, the build, matter in general, the laws of nature, actual existence, presence in person, location in space, or a tangible copy.
sensesIntro.cn: physically 的九个义项都从“身体与世界相遇”开始。变化的是所看的侧面：肉、力量、体格、一般物质、自然规律、实际存在、亲自到场、空间位置，还是一份有形的副本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the dull sound of a body hitting a wall, and the pain that proves the wall is there.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体撞到墙时的那声闷响，以及证明墙确实存在的那阵疼。

branches.en: THE BODY: flesh that can be hurt, strength that can be spent, and a build that can be seen.
branches.cn: 身体：会被伤到的肉、会被消耗的力量，以及看得见的体格。

branches.en: MATTER AND FORM: the material world at large, and objects that can be touched or printed.
branches.cn: 物质与形式：广义的物质世界，以及可触摸或可印刷的实物。

branches.en: THE LAWS: what physics permits or forbids, regardless of desire.
branches.cn: 规律：物理学允许或禁止什么，与愿望无关。

branches.en: REAL AND LOCATED: actual existence rather than plans, and a point with real coordinates.
branches.cn: 真实且有位置：实际存在而非计划，以及有真实坐标的地点。

branches.en: PRESENT IN PERSON: a body in the room rather than a voice on a wire.
branches.cn: 亲自到场：房间里的身体，而不是电线里的声音。

intro.en: Physically is physical + -ly. Physical is Latin physicus, from Greek physikos and physis 'nature'. The family is unusual because it produced three separate English words from one root: physical, physics, and physician.
intro.cn: physically 是 physical 加 -ly。physical 是拉丁 physicus，出自希腊 physikos 与 physis“自然”。这个词族不寻常之处在于，同一个词根产生了三个各自独立的英语词：physical、physics、physician。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is physicus 'natural, of nature', also used as a noun for a natural philosopher, and physica 'natural things, natural science'. Greek supplied physis and physikos.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 physicus“自然的、属于自然的”，也作名词指自然哲学家，以及 physica“自然事物、自然科学”。希腊语提供了 physis 与 physikos。

items.meaning: in the body, in matter, or according to physics
items.meaningCN: 在身体上、在物质中，或按物理规律（-ly 副词）
items.example: The two buildings are physically joined.
items.exampleCN: 这两栋楼在物理上是相连的。

items.meaning: of the body, of matter, or of physics
items.meaningCN: 身体的、物质的或物理学的
items.example: Physical evidence was collected at the site.
items.exampleCN: 现场收集到了实物证据。

items.structure: Greek ta physika 'natural things', via Latin physica
items.meaning: the science of matter, energy, and motion
items.meaningCN: 研究物质、能量与运动的科学；物理学
items.example: Physics explains why the bridge holds.
items.exampleCN: 物理学解释了这座桥为什么撑得住。

items.meaning: the build and shape of a body
items.meaningCN: 身体的体格与形状
items.example: Rowing changed his physique.
items.exampleCN: 划船改变了他的体格。

items.structure: Old French fisicien, from Latin physicus
items.meaning: a doctor of medicine
items.meaningCN: 医生；内科医生
items.example: The physician ordered a chest X-ray.
items.exampleCN: 医生要求做胸部 X 光检查。

items.meaning: the quality of being bodily or tangible
items.meaningCN: 身体性或实体感
items.example: The dance stresses weight and physicality.
items.exampleCN: 这段舞蹈强调重量与身体感。

items.meaning: treatment by movement and physical means
items.meaningCN: 用运动与物理手段进行的治疗；物理疗法
items.example: Physiotherapy restored his shoulder.
items.exampleCN: 物理治疗让他的肩膀恢复了。

items.meaning: relating to public money
items.meaningCN: 与公共资金有关的；财政的（fiscus 国库）
items.example: The fiscal year ends in March.
items.exampleCN: 财政年度在三月结束。

items.structure: Old French fisique < Latin physica < Greek physike 'natural science, medicine'
items.meaning: medicine or the art of healing (archaic); to treat with medicine
items.meaningCN: 药；医术（古旧用法）；用药物治疗
items.example: The old herbals list a physic for fever.
items.exampleCN: 古旧的草药书里列有一种退烧的药。

latinEntries.structure: Latin adjective and noun, from Greek physikos
latinEntries.meaning: natural, of nature; a natural philosopher
latinEntries.meaningCN: 自然的、属于自然的；自然哲学家
篮子、国库（与 physis 无关）

definition_zh: 两极分化；偏振；电极极化；材料的极化；群体极化；无线电波的极化；膜电位极化；政治极化；自旋极化
definition_en: the state of being divided into two opposed groups or directions, or the physical alignment of light waves, electric charges, magnetic moments, or particle spins along one axis
core_image: 一根磁针被两股力拉向两端，中间空出一段谁都不肯待的地方
scene: 同一场选举之后，社交平台上两拨人的发言越来越像两堵墙。After the election, the two camps on social media drifted into polarization.
sceneCN: 这里 polarization 是「政治极化」（第 8 个义项：党派与阵营之间的对立不断加深）；句意：选举之后，社交平台上的两个阵营逐渐陷入政治极化。

pos.zh: 两极分化；偏振；极化；对立加剧

derivatives.zh: 使极化；使两极分化；使偏振
极化的；两极分化的；偏振的

senses.title: A society split into rich and poor
senses.definition: the widening of the gap between groups at opposite ends of a society, especially in income, opportunity, or living standards
senses.definitionCN: 社会两端群体之间在收入、机会或生活水平上的差距不断扩大
senses.example: Wage polarization left the middle of the job market thin.
senses.exampleCN: 工资两极分化让就业市场的中段变得稀薄。
senses.why: Greek polos is the pivot of a sphere, the axis with two ends. Polarization is the pulling of a whole population toward those two ends, leaving the middle empty.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 polos 是球体的轴心，有两端。polarization 就是把整个群体拉向这两端，让中间空出来。

senses.title: Light waves aligned one way
senses.definition: in optics, the condition in which the vibrations of a light wave are restricted to one plane or one direction
senses.definitionCN: 光学中光波的振动被限制在一个平面或一个方向上的状态
senses.example: The sunglasses cut glare by blocking one polarization of light.
senses.exampleCN: 这副太阳镜通过挡住一种偏振方向来削减眩光。
senses.why: A wave that shakes in every direction is pulled into one line. The physical image is the same: what was spread around the axis is forced to one side of it.
senses.whyCN: 向各个方向抖动的波被拉成一条线。物理意象相同：原本围绕轴散开的东西被逼到轴的一侧。

senses.title: Electrodes pushed off balance
senses.definition: in electrochemistry, the change in an electrode's potential from its equilibrium value when current flows
senses.definitionCN: 电化学中通电时电极电位偏离其平衡值的现象
senses.example: High current caused strong polarization at the anode.
senses.exampleCN: 大电流在阳极造成了强烈的极化。
senses.why: Current pushes charges to one side of the boundary and leaves the other side short. The axis is the electrode surface, and the two ends are the two sides of it.
senses.whyCN: 电流把电荷推到界面的某一侧，让另一侧短缺。轴就是电极表面，两端则是它的两侧。

senses.title: Charges shifted inside a material
senses.definition: in a material, the separation of positive and negative charge, or the alignment of magnetic moments, under an applied field
senses.definitionCN: 材料在外加场下正负电荷分离，或磁矩沿同一方向排列
senses.example: The dielectric shows strong polarization between its plates.
senses.exampleCN: 这种介质在两端板之间表现出强烈的极化。
senses.why: Tiny dipoles are turned to face the same way, like compass needles in a field. The material as a whole gains two ends, one positive and one negative.
senses.whyCN: 微小的偶极子被转向同一方向，像磁场里的罗盘针。整块材料于是有了两端，一端正、一端负。

senses.title: A group pushed to extremes
senses.definition: in social psychology, the tendency of a discussion among like-minded people to move the group toward a more extreme position
senses.definitionCN: 社会心理学中，志同道合者讨论之后整个群体向更极端立场移动的倾向
senses.example: Group polarization explains why the jury became harsher after debate.
senses.exampleCN: 群体极化解释了陪审团为何在讨论后变得更严厉。
senses.why: The group's opinions were already leaning one way; talk pushes them further out along that axis. The middle is not argued away, it is simply left behind.
senses.whyCN: 群体的意见本来就偏向一边；讨论把它们沿这条轴推得更远。中间不是被论证掉的，而是被落在了后面。

senses.title: The plane in which a radio wave vibrates
senses.definition: in radio engineering, the orientation of a wave's electric field, which must match between transmitting and receiving antennas
senses.definitionCN: 无线电工程中波的电场所取的取向，发射与接收天线必须一致
senses.example: Misaligned polarization cost the link half its signal.
senses.exampleCN: 极化方向没对上，使这条链路损失了一半信号。
senses.why: An antenna is a rod with one direction. If the incoming wave shakes along a different line, the rod cannot catch it well: two axes must be lined up.
senses.whyCN: 天线是一根有方向的杆。如果来波沿另一条线抖动，杆就抓不住它：两根轴必须对齐。

senses.title: A membrane held at a voltage
senses.definition: in cell biology, the state of a cell membrane having a voltage across it, or the shift away from its resting voltage
senses.definitionCN: 细胞生物学中细胞膜两侧存在电位差的状态，或偏离静息电位的改变
senses.example: Depolarization of the membrane opens the sodium channels.
senses.exampleCN: 膜的去极化打开了钠通道。
senses.why: The membrane is a wall with charge on both sides, a small battery. Polarization is that charge being held apart; losing it is what lets a signal travel.
senses.whyCN: 细胞膜是一堵两侧带电荷的墙，一节小电池。极化就是让电荷分开待着；失去这种分离，信号才能传导。

senses.title: Politics split into camps
senses.definition: the growing distance between political parties or camps, so that agreement across the divide becomes rare
senses.definitionCN: 政党或阵营之间的距离不断加大，使跨阵营的共识变得罕见
senses.example: The study links polarization to the decline of local newspapers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把政治极化与地方报纸的衰落联系起来。
senses.why: Politics is the most visible version: two poles, each with its own facts. The word describes not disagreement but the disappearance of the middle ground where disagreement could be discussed.
senses.whyCN: 政治是最显眼的版本：两个极，各有一套事实。这个词描述的不是分歧本身，而是可以让分歧被讨论的中间地带消失了。

senses.title: Particle spins lined up
senses.definition: in physics, the condition in which the spins of particles in a material or beam point predominantly in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中材料或束流里粒子自旋主要指向同一方向的状态
senses.example: Spin polarization above eighty percent was measured in the beam.
senses.exampleCN: 束流中测得了超过八成的自旋极化。
senses.why: The smallest compass needles of all are the spins. Polarization here is the alignment of those arrows along one axis, the same gesture repeated at the quantum scale.
senses.whyCN: 最小的罗盘针是自旋。这里的极化就是这些箭头沿一条轴排列，是同一个手势在量子尺度上的重复。

intro.en: Polarization is polarize plus -ation, from Latin -ationem. Polarize is polar + -ize; polar comes from Latin polaris 'of the pole', from polus 'axis, pole', borrowed from Greek polos 'axis, pivot, the sky'. The optical sense was established in the early 19th century; the social and political senses are late 19th and 20th century extensions of the same two-ends image.
intro.cn: polarization 是 polarize 加 -ation（拉丁 -ationem）。polarize 是 polar 加 -ize；polar 来自拉丁 polaris“极的”，出自 polus“轴、极”，借自希腊 polos“轴心、枢轴、天空”。光学义在 19 世纪初确立；社会与政治义则是 19 世纪末至 20 世纪对同一个“两端”意象的延伸。

items.en: Polos means 'axis, pivot, the pole of a sphere', and also 'the vault of the sky', because the sky was imagined turning on a pivot. The two ends of the axis are the poles.
items.cn: polos 意为“轴、枢轴、球体的极”，也指“天穹”，因为天空被想象成绕一个枢轴旋转。轴的两端就是两极。

items.en: Polus and polaris give English polar. The earth's poles, the poles of a magnet, and the poles of a cell all inherit the idea of two ends of one axis.
items.cn: polus 与 polaris 产生英语 polar。地球的极、磁体的极、电池的极，都继承“一条轴的两端”这一观念。

items.en: The optical sense is established in the early 19th century, after experiments showed that light passing through certain crystals takes on a fixed direction of vibration.
items.cn: 光学义在 19 世纪初确立，此前实验显示通过某些晶体的光会取得固定的振动方向。

items.en: Electrochemistry and material science extend the word to electrodes and dielectrics: charges held at two sides of a boundary.
items.cn: 19 世纪电化学与材料科学把这个词扩展到电极与电介质：电荷被分持在界面的两侧。

items.en: Social psychology names group polarization, political science speaks of a polarized electorate, and physics adds spin polarization. The image survives the change of scale.
items.cn: 20 世纪社会心理学提出群体极化，政治学谈论极化的选民，物理学加入自旋极化。意象在不同尺度上都沿用。

items.en: The English noun pole meaning a long stick or post comes from Latin palus 'stake', not from polus 'axis'. So telegraph poles and the North Pole are not related, even though both are spelled pole.
items.cn: 英语中表示长杆或柱子的 pole 来自拉丁 palus“木桩”，不是 polus“轴”。所以电线杆与北极在词源上无关，尽管拼写都是 pole。

note.en: The first group follows the polus family and marks the pole/palus trap. The second group compares division, split, divergence, and dichotomy, the four nouns closest to polarization in social writing.
note.cn: 第一组沿着 polus 词族，并标出 pole/palus 陷阱。第二组比较 division、split、divergence、dichotomy，这四个名词在社会议题写作中最近似 polarization。

entries.definition: relating to the poles of the earth or of a magnet. Polarization is the process of producing two such poles.
entries.definitionCN: 与地球两极或磁极有关的。polarization 是产生这样两个极的过程。

entries.definition: to divide into two opposed groups, or to align waves or charges. The noun names the resulting state.
entries.definitionCN: 使分成两个对立群体，或使波与电荷取向一致。名词命名由此形成的状态。

entries.definition: the condition of having two opposite poles or tendencies. It names the two-endedness itself, while polarization names the process that creates it.
entries.definitionCN: 具有两个相反极或相反倾向的状态。它命名“两端性”本身，而 polarization 命名造成它的过程。

entries.definition: Either an end of an axis (from polus) or a long post (from palus 'stake'). The two meanings share spelling but not origin.
entries.definitionCN: 既可以指轴的一端（出自 polus），也可以指长杆（出自 palus“木桩”）。两个意义拼写相同，来源不同。

entries.definition: the act or state of being separated into parts. It is neutral and can describe any split, not only a split into two camps.
entries.definitionCN: 被分成部分的行为或状态。它是中性的，可以描述任何分裂，而不只是分成两个阵营。

entries.definition: a separation or disagreement within a group. It often implies a single event, while polarization implies a gradual widening.
entries.definitionCN: 群体内部的分裂或分歧。它常暗示一次事件，而 polarization 暗示逐渐拉大。

entries.definition: the process of becoming different or moving apart. It stresses paths separating, not a population forming two ends.
entries.definitionCN: 变得不同或分开的过程。它强调路径分离，而不是人群形成两端。

entries.definition: a division into two sharply contrasted categories. It is a way of describing or organizing, while polarization is a social condition that people suffer.
entries.definitionCN: 分成两个鲜明对照类别的划分。它是一种描述或组织方式，而 polarization 是人们承受的社会状况。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: polos 'axis', Latin polaris, the 1810s optical sense, the 20th-century social senses, and the palus trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：polos“轴”、拉丁 polaris、19 世纪初的光学义、20 世纪的社会义，以及 palus 陷阱。

normal.en: Polos is the pivot of a sphere: polarization is everything being pulled toward the two ends of one axis.
normal.cn: polos 是球体的枢轴：polarization 就是一切都被拉向同一条轴的两端。

normal.en: Light was the first thing to be polarized: waves that shook in all directions were made to shake in one plane.
normal.cn: 光是最先被“极化”的东西：向各方向抖动的波被迫只在一个平面内抖动。

normal.en: The social senses reuse the same shape: a middle that empties as both sides grow.
normal.cn: 社会义复用同一个形状：两边变大，中间被腾空。

normal.en: A magnet has two poles, a battery has two poles, and a debate can end up with two poles; the word is the same gesture.
normal.cn: 磁体有两个极，电池有两个极，一场辩论也能只剩两个极；这个词是同一个手势。

normal.en: Pole the stick is from palus, pole the axis is from polus: same letters, different roots.
normal.cn: 木杆的 pole 出自 palus，轴端的 pole 出自 polus：字母相同，词根不同。

abstract.en: Two magnets pulled apart still feel each other; the gap is the relationship.
abstract.cn: 两块磁体被拉开后仍然感到彼此；那段空隙就是它们的关系。

abstract.en: A room where everyone agrees gets louder, not wiser; that is group polarization.
abstract.cn: 一个所有人都同意的房间会变得更响，而不是更明智；这就是群体极化。

abstract.en: A country with two news feeds does not argue about facts; it argues about which feed is the country.
abstract.cn: 拥有两套新闻流的国家并不争论事实；它争论的是哪一套流才算国家。

examples.en: Income polarization has outpaced the growth of the middle class.
examples.cn: 收入两极分化的速度超过了中产阶层的增长。

examples.en: A polarizing filter removes one polarization of the light.
examples.cn: 偏振滤镜会滤掉光的一种偏振成分。

examples.en: The survey measured political polarization across ten years.
examples.cn: 这项调查测量了十年间的政治极化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼了赖什恩」——两边的人把水全“泼”向自己的那一端，中间被“赖”着不站人 → polarization 两极分化；偏振（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 polaris「极的」，出自 polus「轴、极」，再上溯希腊 polos「轴心、枢轴」；构词为 polar + -ize + -ation（拉丁 -ationem）。核心是「一根轴的两端被拉开，中间空出来」。同族含 polar、polarize、polarity；表示长杆的 pole 出自拉丁 palus「木桩」，与 polus 不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of polarization all describe one axis with two ends and a middle that empties. What changes is what is being pulled: a society, light, an electrode, a material, a discussion group, a radio wave, a cell membrane, a parliament, or a beam of particles.
sensesIntro.cn: polarization 的九个义项都描述一条有两端、中间被腾空的轴。变化的是被拉开的东西：社会、光、电极、材料、讨论小组、无线电波、细胞膜、议会，还是一束粒子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one needle pulled toward both ends at once, with a stretch of empty space left in the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根针同时被拉向两端，中间空出一段谁都不肯待的地方。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL AXIS: income and opportunity splitting into rich and poor, and politics splitting into camps.
branches.cn: 社会之轴：收入与机会分成贫富两端，政治分成阵营。

branches.en: THE WAVE'S AXIS: light restricted to one plane, and radio waves whose orientation must match the antenna.
branches.cn: 波之轴：光被限制在一个平面，无线电波的取向必须与天线匹配。

branches.en: THE CHARGE'S AXIS: electrode potentials off balance, dipoles turned in a material, and the voltage held across a membrane.
branches.cn: 电荷之轴：偏离平衡的电极电位、材料中被转向的偶极子，以及跨膜保持的电压。

branches.en: THE GROUP'S AXIS: like-minded talk pushing a discussion further toward one end.
branches.cn: 群体之轴：同质化的讨论把话题进一步推向某一端。

branches.en: THE SPIN'S AXIS: particle spins lined up along one direction at the quantum scale.
branches.cn: 自旋之轴：量子尺度上粒子自旋沿同一方向排列。

intro.en: Polarization is polar + -ize + -ation. Polar is Latin polaris, from polus 'axis, pole', borrowed from Greek polos. The ending -ation is Latin -ationem, an action noun. English built polarize, polarized, and polarization on a root that originally named the pivot of the sky.
intro.cn: polarization 是 polar + -ize + -ation。polar 是拉丁 polaris，出自 polus“轴、极”，借自希腊 polos。词尾 -ation 是拉丁 -ationem，动作名词。英语在一个原本指“天穹枢轴”的词根上造出了 polarize、polarized 与 polarization。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is polus 'axis, pole', polaris 'of the pole', and the verb form polarizare used by later science. Greek supplied polos 'pivot, sky'. Latin palus 'stake', source of the other pole, is unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 polus“轴、极”、polaris“极的”，以及后世科学使用的动词形式 polarizare。希腊语提供了 polos“枢轴、天空”。另一个 pole 的来源 palus“木桩”与它无关。

items.meaning: the state or process of forming two poles
items.meaningCN: 形成两极的状态或过程（-ation 动作名词）
items.example: Polarization of the electorate increased after the reform.
items.exampleCN: 改革之后选民的两极分化加剧了。

items.meaning: to divide into two ends, or align along an axis
items.meaningCN: 分成两端，或沿一条轴排列（-ize 动词）
items.example: The issue polarized the committee.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题让委员会分成两派。

items.meaning: of a pole or the polar regions
items.meaningCN: 极的；极地的
items.example: Polar ice reflects sunlight.
items.exampleCN: 极地冰盖反射阳光。

items.meaning: divided into two camps, or filtered to one vibration plane
items.meaningCN: 分成两派的，或滤成单一振动平面的
items.example: The room was polarized before the vote.
items.exampleCN: 投票之前房间里已经分成两派。

items.meaning: the state of having two opposite poles
items.meaningCN: 具有两个相反极的状态；极性
items.example: Check the polarity before connecting the battery.
items.exampleCN: 接电池之前先检查极性。

items.meaning: a device that filters light to one plane
items.meaningCN: 把光滤成单一平面的器件；偏振片
items.example: Two crossed polarizers block almost all light.
items.exampleCN: 两片正交的偏振片几乎挡住全部光线。

items.meaning: the loss of a membrane's resting voltage
items.meaningCN: 膜静息电位的丧失；去极化
items.example: Depolarization precedes the nerve impulse.
items.exampleCN: 去极化发生在神经冲动之前。

items.meaning: division into exactly two blocs
items.meaningCN: 分成恰好两个集团；两极化
items.example: Bipolarization marked the early Cold War.
items.exampleCN: 两极化是冷战早期的特征。

items.structure: Latin polus for an axis end; Latin palus for a stake
items.meaning: an end of an axis, or a long post (two different roots)
items.meaningCN: 轴的一端，或长杆（两个不同词根）
items.example: The North Pole is not the same word as a telegraph pole.
items.exampleCN: 北极与电线杆并不是同一个词源。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 木桩、柱子（与 polus 无关）

latinEntries.meaning: axis, pivot, the vault of the sky
